You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
You will be part of the Policy and Plans Division in the Crisis Strategy and Operations Group, working with MOH divisions and relevant stakeholders to strengthen Singapore’s health-sector readiness for nuclear and radiological emergencies.

This is a planning role that involves upstream policy and strategic planning, as well as support for downstream response planning where required. You will be supporting the development of health-sector emergency preparedness and response plans for nuclear and radiological emergencies, as well as contributing to other strategic planning work as required.

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.
jobResponsibilities:
What will you be working on?

(1) Health-sector planning for nuclear and radiological emergencies

•	Support the development of MOH’s health-sector emergency preparedness and response plans, including planning inputs across key response areas such as medical triage, pre-hospital response, in-hospital management, contamination control, medical counter-measures, psychosocial support and longer-term health monitoring.
•	Translate Whole-of-Government planning parameters and technical risk assessments into health-sector planning assumptions, response requirements and operational considerations.
•	Identify capability gaps and support efforts to strengthen health-sector readiness over time.

(2) Other strategic planning work

•	Support other strategic planning workstreams as required, including reviewing existing plans, developing planning approaches and plans, and providing inputs to related workstreams across disease outbreaks, civil emergencies and national emergencies.

(3) Coordination with Whole-of-Government, healthcare and operational stakeholders

•	Work with Whole-of-Government partners to understand national planning parameters, response assumptions and inter-agency dependencies.
•	Work with relevant MOH divisions, healthcare clusters, hospitals and other relevant partners on downstream response planning, where alignment is required. 
•	Coordinate inputs across policy, clinical, operational, logistics and inter-agency stakeholders to support integrated health-sector planning.
•	Support exercises, tabletop discussions and reviews to test and refine response plans.

(4) Secretariat and coordination support

•	Prepare meeting materials, briefs, updates and records of discussion for relevant platforms.
•	Track key inter-ministerial workstreams, milestones, action items and follow-ups across stakeholders.
•	Support coordination of MOH’s health-sector inputs into relevant Whole-of-Government workgroups and planning platforms.
•	Synthesise complex technical and operational information into clear planning notes and updates.
jobRequirements:
The applicant should be comfortable working in a technical domain and translating concepts such as radiation exposure, contamination, dose, health impact, protective actions and medical countermeasures into clear planning and operational considerations.

Applicant should meet the following requirements:
•	Tertiary qualifications, preferably in nuclear science, physics, applied sciences, public health policy, public policy, or a related field.
•	At least 2 years of relevant experience in emergency preparedness, policy/strategic planning, operational implementation or related areas.
•	Background or interest in technical domains related to nuclear and radiological emergency preparedness would be an advantage.
•	Able to translate technical information into clear planning assumptions, operational requirements and recommendations.
•	Able to work across Whole-of-Government, policy and operational stakeholders.
•	Strong analytical, writing, communication and presentation skills.
•	Organised, adaptable and comfortable working in an evolving technical domain.

Other Key Competencies Required:

•	Thinking Clearly & Making Sound Judgements – Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities to support the crafting of sound policy recommendations; ability to grasp timelines, operating context and ground realities.
 
•	Learning & Putting Skills into Action - Possesses the drive and curiosity to learn and apply new skills, knowledge and new ways of working. 

•	Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the risks involved. 

•	Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective purpose.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment

jobDescription: PRINCIPAL / SENIOR / EXECUTIVE SOFTWARE ENGINEER, SYSTEMS
jobResponsibilities:
At Centre for Autonomous Mobility (CAM), You will build the digital products that make safe autonomous vehicle deployments possible in Singapore, at scale. We lead Singapore’s national effort to deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale safely. The Systems team builds the digital tools behind that mission — for instance, developing a monitoring system for AVs to collect and analyse AV operational data to support LTA’s regulatory and safety assurance work. But the role is broader than any single product: wherever software can move AV deployment forward, that is where we will build.

As a Software Engineer, you will

● Design and build production-quality digital products end to end: You will understand and take ownership of problem statements, before designing and architecting systems on cloud infrastructure from conception through deployment and ongoing maintenance.

● Build the suite of safety-assurance products LTA needs to regulate AVs reliably: analytics, dashboards and visualisations; implement enforcement and performance tracking, event management and data-anomaly alerts.

● Identify and address pain points bottlenecking deployment velocity: Work in a tight-knit and cross-functional CAM team, with a clear north-star of driving safe AV deployments at scale — which includes non-passenger vehicles and AVs on public paths (Autonomous Mobile Robots). Talk to users and industry, identify gaps and propose products that move AV deployments forward.

● Evolve our products to the next bound: Our product portfolio spans several digital products, including the AV Monitoring System that monitors every AV on Singapore’s public roads. We are building for scale so that systems can handle a growing number of AVs and developers amidst evolving needs, strengthening data pipelines and system observability for high-volume telemetry, and potentially integrating with other LTA enterprise platforms for operations and incident management.

● Monitor and support production systems that AV operations and regulation including helping respond to incidents when they arise.

● Apply AI, ML and Data Analytics where it adds value as well as identify gaps and proose products that strengthen AV safety and drive AU deployments.
jobRequirements:
● Knowledge preferably in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.

● Can build software end to end, and is strong across the stack — demonstrated through prior work, shipped products or personal projects; what you’ve built matters more than specific degrees. You should be comfortable designing and implementing digital products with maintainable data models.

● Thinks clearly about systems — data pipelines, APIs, data integrity and authentication, and designing for scale and reliability — making technical decisions that balance performance, maintainability and real-world needs.

● Able to listen and distil issues faced by stakeholders into key problem and/or opportunity statements to devise effective solutions, while being able to clearly explain and obtain buy-in from other engineers and key stakeholders.

●Takes initiative, has pride in their craft, and cares about the public good — writes tests, cares about code quality, maintainability and correctness. Self-directed and curious in picking up new knowledge, and invested in team success beyond individual contributions. Motivated by the mission of driving safe AV deployments at scale.

● Experience with data-intensive systems, dashboards and data visualisation, or cloud infrastructure.

● UI/UX sensibility — experience designing usable interfaces, or working closely with designers to craft intuitive user experiences.

● Familiarity with JavaScript/TypeScript with some Python, React, cloud services and open-source tooling, on relational databases (SQLite and Postgres).

● Familiarity in working with geospatial data and relevant libraries will be advantageous

● Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform), CI/CD pipelines, and Agile delivery.

● Interest in autonomous vehicles, transport planning, generative AI, or safety-critical systems.

jobResponsibilities:
As Manager (Strategy & Policy), you will spearhead critical initiatives that position Singapore as a responsible and innovative space nation. You will develop the National Space Strategy 1.0, establishing Singapore's comprehensive roadmap for space development across government, industry, and research sectors. This foundational strategy will guide Singapore's space ambitions and coordinate efforts across multiple agencies and stakeholders.

You will lead the development of national space legislation, crafting the legal framework that will govern Singapore's space activities whilst ensuring compliance with international obligations and supporting commercial space development. This includes analysing existing regulatory gaps, consulting with industry stakeholders, and designing legislation that balances innovation with responsible space governance.

Your role extends to developing Singapore's international policy positions on space matters, requiring deep analysis of emerging space technologies, geopolitical considerations, and economic opportunities. You will formulate policy recommendations that advance Singapore's national interests whilst contributing to global space governance.

On the international stage, you will represent Singapore in multilateral forums, particularly within the United Nations system, advocating for Singapore's positions whilst helping to shape international space law and norms. This includes participating in negotiations, building coalitions with like-minded nations, and contributing to the development of guidelines for responsible space activities.

•	The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in policy development, international relations, or space governance. jobDescription: The Industry & CUGE Division (Centre for Urban Greenery and Ecology) of the National Parks Board oversees the industry development and skills training for sectors and industries under the purview of NParks such as landscaping, orchids, ornamental fish and aquatic plants, etc. Our goal is to uplift companies and people in these sectors by enhancing operational productivity, improvement in business operations, raising the level of professionalism of the sectors, and enabling digitalisation and innovation for the industry.
jobResponsibilities:
[What the role is]

One key area of work to achieve our goals is to plan, develop, and manage land and space for businesses in these sectors. Through these functions, we support business continuity, optimise Singapore’s land and space use, and contribute to supply chain resilience.

[What you will be working on]

The candidate will take on a dual focus: managing NParks' leasehold and tenancy tenders and contracts in the landscape, orchid, ornamental fish and aquatic plant sectors, as well as contributing to policy and planning work to safeguard the long-term land needs of these sectors.

Tender and Contract Management

• Manage the full pipeline of agri-land tenders, from preparation, launch, evaluation and award through to client management.
• Review plans submitted by lessees and tenants to ensure alignment with land tender conditions, broad regulatory requirements and policy parameters.
• Track lessees' and tenants' ability to fulfil contractual obligations and meet renewal criteria.
• Manage client relationships for daily operational matters, including carrying out regular engagements with nurseries and farms, conducting site visits to obtain first-hand observations, and supporting clients in meeting their contractual obligations.

Policy and Planning

• Contribute to policy and planning matters for the long-term land use needs of the landscape, orchid, ornamental fish and aquatic plant sectors.
• Work with internal teams and external agencies — including land planning and development agencies — to plan and develop a steady supply of land, indoor space, buildings and infrastructure for these sectors.
• Engage with relevant agencies to safeguard the land needs of these sectors within Singapore's broader land use planning framework.
• Review land-related policies for the stated sectors, i.e. allowable use of land, tenure, tender requirements etc

Additional Responsibilities

• Maintain a database of all NParks' lessees and tenants in the relevant farm plots, tracking current lease terms, upcoming renewal cycles, progress in meeting construction and regulatory milestones, and productivity targets.
• Explore, evaluate and test GovTech's suite of productivity tools to determine their suitability and effectiveness in managing lessees' and tenants' administrative matters, including tracking of contract renewal requirements and TOP/CSC progress, as well as supporting basic data analysis of trends of interest.
jobRequirements:
• Education: Area of studies in real estate, estate management, urban planning, business administration, building or construction management, or a related field

• Experience: At least 2 years of relevant working experience in revenue contracting, contract and tenant management, or policy and planning. Experience working with government agencies, land planning, land contracts or tenancy management, or in the landscape, horticulture, aquaculture or agri-food sectors would be an advantage.

• Skills and Competencies: An analytical mindset with an interest in policy and planning work. Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple contracts and deadlines concurrently. Good written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to engage effectively with both internal teams and external stakeholders.

As many of the stakeholders in the landscape, orchid, ornamental fish and aquatic plant sectors commonly communicate in Mandarin, proficiency in Mandarin would be a distinct advantage. Familiarity with database or IT systems management is advantageous.

agencyDescription:
The National Security Coordination Secretariat’s mission is to build a shared picture of cross-cutting national security risks, and mobilise the multi-agency effort needed to mitigate risks. 

We work to secure Singapore against risks in any domain that could compromise Singapore’s survival and success. This includes vulnerabilities to disruptions to day-to-day life, social divisions, and coercion to act against our national interest. Such risks impact multiple sectors and require multi-sector responses to effectively mitigate risks to Singapore.
jobDescription:
The National Security Coordination Secretariat (NSCS) is a unit under the Prime Minister's Office responsible for national security planning and coordination. NSCS works with agencies and stakeholders to develop and co-ordinate strategies to address national security concerns. NSCS also works with agencies to anticipate and identify emergent security risks, and to build up capabilities and resources to deal with these.

The role will give you the opportunity to strengthen:

o	Critical Thinking: You will need to keep abreast of national security developments and synthesise information across domains (geopolitical, economic, social, environment, information, etc.) to identify and analyse cross-cutting national security risks. These include economic security risks, digital security risks, concentration risks, and inter-dependency risks.

o	Systems Thinking: You will need to integrate analysis of external developments with assessments of Singapore’s vulnerabilities and how the latter will change over time. You will recommend the best way to structure the Whole-of-Government response to the risk. This will require you to suggest constructive solutions which balance multiple policy considerations across domains. For specific risks, you could contribute to the full policy value-chain from strategic planning, policy formulation, policy-operations, to comms and implementation (e.g., legislation).

o	Influence: You will need to mobilise colleagues from a wide range of agencies, with different mandates and policy considerations, to work with you on the overall risk assessment. You will need to build consensus on the risk level Singapore can live with and the Whole-of-Government action needed to mitigate the risks. This would require you to build extensive and deep networks across domains and seniority levels, and develop a deep understanding of their considerations and constraints.

o	Depending on your performance and experience, you could be given the opportunity to lead a team (of 2-3 officers) or project, and individually handle complex and sensitive policy pieces that cut across NSCS’s work.
jobResponsibilities:
You will work in a team / lead a team:

o	To hunt out Singapore’s cross-cutting vulnerabilities (e.g., in critical infrastructure, social resilience) that could be exploited/ disrupted and build shared risk pictures (through policy analysis and/ or data analysis) to inform decision-making by public sector leaders.

o	To mobilise collective Whole-of-Government efforts to tackle complex, collective-action problems. This could involve putting forth recommendations to achieve better national outcomes through balancing differing policy objectives.

jobDescription:
This role is part of MHA’s Civilian Generalist career track. Learn more: https://go.gov.sg/civiliangeneralist 

The Singapore Police Force (SPF) keeps Singapore safe and secure by preventing, deterring and detecting crime.
Operationalised on 1 February 2024, the Online Criminal Harms Act (OCHA) 2023 enables the OCHA Office to work with government agencies and industry partners to counter online criminal activity. This includes issuing directions to restrict Singapore users’ access to specified criminal content and requiring designated online services to implement upstream measures against scams and cyber-enabled crimes.

As Staff Officer (Outreach & Engagement) in the OCHA Office, you will engage online platforms to understand their systems, policies and safeguards, and work with them to disrupt online criminal activity affecting Singapore users. You should have a strong grasp of OCHA 2023, its Code of Practice and related Government Directions, platform operating models, and policy considerations shaping SPF’s engagement strategies. Through strategic partnerships, risk-based engagement and evidence-based guidance, you will help develop practical upstream measures to reduce online harms, including scams, radicalisation and emerging threats.

You will be placed under the Management Executive Scheme.
jobResponsibilities:

•	Platform partnerships and OCHA administration 
•	Identify new online platforms with a Singapore presence, and proactively establish partnership with them.
•	Educate online platforms on OCHA 2023 and their obligations, and work with them to establish workflows for administration of the Act as well as to align their internal policies and processes with the Act, where required. 
•	Engagement strategy 
•	Keep abreast on emerging online crime trends and develop tailored engagement roadmaps.
•	Online platforms’ safeguards and threat response
•	Research and engage online platforms on their safeguards, limitations, and future plans to detect, counter and prevent online criminal activities. 
•	Engage stakeholders to strengthen platform safeguards, incorporate industry good practices in the Codes of Practice to combat criminal activities effectively. 
•	Monitor global and local online criminal threat developments and work with online platforms to strengthen their safeguards to counter critical online threats.
•	Performance monitoring
•	Track key performance indicators on platform safeguard effectiveness and reduction in online crime.
jobRequirements:

•	Strong stakeholder management, negotiation and interpersonal skills.
•	Strategic & analytical skills and ability to translate insights into actionable engagement plans.
•	Ability to plan, execute and monitor multi-stakeholder initiatives under tight timelines

jobDescription:
The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) is at the heart of our nation. We aim to build a caring and cohesive community that we can all be proud of, and to create opportunities for Singaporeans to come together as one people.

Youths are critical to make this happen. In Singapore, youths are defined as age 15–35 years old, and they play a pivotal role in contributing to the success and strengthening the social fabric of our nation. Youths are increasingly civically engaged and have a desire to make a difference. It is important that the views of youths are heard and valued, and that they have sufficient opportunities to partner the Government to make a difference, and to achieve their diverse aspirations in life.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of a dynamic team to develop and implement policies and initiatives to support youth development, engagement, and ground-up action. This will include understanding youth-related issues and the current landscape, identifying gaps through research, data analysis, and engagements, and proposing sound recommendations to address these gaps. As part of the work, you will need to independently drive action and collaborate with both internal and external stakeholders, to conceptualise, implement, and enhance programmes that support and engage our youths.

A key focus of this role is the Somerset Belt and *SCAPE portfolio, where you will work to place-make the Somerset Belt into a vibrant youth precinct connected to the wider Orchard Road rejuvenation plans. jobDescription:
The officer will support the Principal Economist in establishing a new team dedicated to aviation economic analysis in support of Singapore's air hub strategy. As the middle-level manager of the team, the officer will have supervisory responsibilities for a junior-level economist and will be integral in formulating the team’s analytical direction, ensuring the quality and rigour of work, and translating economic insights into actionable recommendations for senior leadership and policy stakeholders.

The officer will play a crucial role in shaping evidence-based aviation policy and hub development strategy, drawing on deep expertise in econometric analysis, quantitative modelling, and transport economics. Working together with the Principal Economist, the officer will have opportunities to lead research projects across government agencies and the OneAviation community that meaningfully inform national aviation policy and Singapore's long-term hub competitiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
The officer will have responsibilities in the following areas:

a. Day-to-day direction and oversight of the unit’s demand modelling, including projections, policy counterfactuals and other quantitative research programme to inform national aviation policy.

b. Analysis on global aviation trends, market dynamics, and competitive positioning, with a focus on translating findings into strategic insights for decision-makers.

c. Middle-level engagement with government agencies, industry stakeholders, and inter-agency partners to ensure the unit's analytical work is well-integrated into air hub strategy and policy.

d. Presentation and communication of economic analysis and forecasting results to senior management and MOT to support policy, programme, and investment decisions.

e. Stewardship of the unit's work on economic assessments and data-driven insights for industry consultations and public-facing engagements.

Beyond the unit’s core analytical mandate, the officer will be responsible for building and sustaining organisational capabilities in economic analysis and transport economics across CAAS. This includes mentoring junior staff, establishing best practices, and contributing to the development of a strong analytical culture.
jobRequirements:
• Strong training in Economics, Econometrics, or a quantitative discipline with substantial economics content. Advanced studies in Economics would be an advantage

  • Strong background in theoretical and empirical economics

  • Minimum of 8 years work experience, with at least 5 years professional experience in quantitative economic analysis

  • Proven record of conducting independent research

  • Advanced programming skills (for eg Python, R, Stata)

  • Excellent written and oral communication

  • Passion in contributing to Singapore’s aviation sector and public policy in general

Note: Your appointment designation will commensurate with your relevant work experience. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance, and may be considered for placement on a permanent tenure or subsequent contract renewal.

jobDescription: PRINCIPAL / SENIOR / EXECUTIVE CYBERSECURITY ENGINEER, AV CYBERSECURITY
jobResponsibilities:
Centre for Autonomous Mobility (CAM) leads Singapore’s national effort to deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale. As AVs move onto public roads, their cybersecurity becomes a matter of public safety: a compromised vehicle is not just a data breach but a physical risk. You will be part of the cybersecurity team responsible for developing the cybersecurity assurance regime for AVs, to ensure autonomous vehicles are deployed safely and securely in Singapore. You will drive to grow into AV cybersecurity. You will help build the function from the ground up assuring the cybersecurity of AVs themselves, and securing the systems CAM builds to oversee them.

Your responsibilities:

● Drive the development of the regulatory framework for AVs, such as establishing requirements for a Cyber Security Management System (CSMS) that covers the vehicle’s lifecycle — development, production and deployment.

● Assess AV developers’ cybersecurity submissions against our assurance criteria, applying Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA) and the R155 Annex 5 threats and controls, as well as standards such as ISO/SAE 21434.

● Define expectations for secure over-the-air software updates in line with the intent of UN R156 (a Software Update Management System), and for managing cyber risk across the AV supply chain.

● Establish monitoring, detection and incident response requirements for AVs, including analysing threats, vulnerabilities and mitigations to contribute to collective knowledge for the AV ecosystem.

● Maintain the policies, standards and playbooks for AV cybersecurity, and support engagement with local partners and international fora (e.g. UNECE WP.29 / GRVA).

Help secure CAM’s digital products / DevSecOps (secondary)

The other part of the team’s remit is making sure the systems CAM builds to regulate and monitor AVs — such as the Autonomous Vehicle Monitoring System — are themselves secure by design.

● Work with the Systems team to build security into the software development lifecycle, from design through CI/CD to production.

● Conduct security architecture and design reviews and risk assessments of CAM’s systems, and provide and implement remediation recommendations.

● Support security reviews of application code and architecture, and help design secure-by-default components.

● Set up automated security testing — SAST/DAST, dependency and secrets scanning, and infrastructure-as-code checks — in the delivery pipeline.

● Assist with breach detection and incident response for these products.

Help build the function

● As you grow into the role, you will naturally spot gaps and suggest tools, processes and improvements as the team and its remit grow.

● Evaluate emerging security technologies and recommend tools and approaches for the team to adopt.

● Provide security advice to CAM project teams on design and architecture decisions, and help build a security-minded culture across CAM, working alongside engineers, AV developers and agency partners.

For more senior hire, you will:

● Own and drive the AV cybersecurity assurance framework end to end, and set the assurance criteria AV developers must meet.

● Lead assessments of AV developers’ cybersecurity management systems and act as a technical authority in deployment-approval decisions on cybersecurity assurance adequacy.

● Help establish security architecture governance and compliance with relevant frameworks.

● Lead cybersecurity incident response for the AV fleet and our products, and define the team’s tooling, standards and processes.

● Mentor junior engineers and help grow the team.
jobRequirements:
● Knowledge preferably in Computer Science, Cybersecurity or a related field

● Thinks analytically about risk — can reason about threats, weigh trade-offs, and understand the limits of a cybersecurity control on safety outcomes.

● Eager to learn vehicle regulations — genuinely interested in standards and frameworks like R155, and able to pick them up quickly.

● Communicates clearly — can explain security issues to both technical and non-technical people.

● Takes initiative and cares about the public good — this is new ground, so you will help shape the standards rather than inherit them.

● Familiarity with automotive / vehicle cybersecurity standards and regulation — UN R155 and R156, ISO/SAE 21434, CSMS and TARA — or a track record of picking up new regulatory frameworks quickly.

● Exposure to automotive, operational-technology (OT) or embedded / safety-critical systems security, including security architecture of cloud-native applications and/or OT systems.

● Hands-on DevSecOps experience: secure SDLC, CI/CD pipeline security, cloud security (e.g. AWS), and SAST/DAST tooling.

● Hands-on experience with security tools such as SIEM, WAF, IPS, privileged access management (PAM), or data loss prevention (DLP).

● Professional accreditations such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, GICSP, GCIH or OSCP.

● A strong interest in autonomous vehicles, emerging mobility technology and overall vehicular safety.

jobDescription:

At NLB, you can look forward to a flexible, hybrid work environment with rewarding, impactful deliverables that improve the lives of the community. With caring colleagues, you will be in an ideal environment for professional development, innovation and impact.

We can offer you:
• A chance to Impact the Community, bridge gaps and empower everyone with the opportunity for learning and discovery.
• An opportunity to Innovate and Push Boundaries. We value ideas, curiosity and a passion for innovation to transform our libraries and archives.
• An organisation that Cares for your Growth and Wellbeing through investment in staff development and wellbeing in a supportive and collaborative environment.

We are seeking a Assistant Manager/Manager to support the development and implementation of MOLLY, NLB's mobile library service that promotes the love of reading among families, persons with disabilities, and underserved communities. This role focuses on leading the strategic development and management of MOLLY's services, as well as building community partnerships and collaborations to expand programme reach.
jobResponsibilities:
• Ability to develop and implement strategic plans to grow and sustain MOLLY's services and outreach.
• Experience in designing and evaluating community programmes, with the ability to use data and insights to inform improvements.
• Ability to identify gaps in service delivery and propose innovative solutions to better serve target communities.
• Promote MOLLY’s library collection and services during outreaches, including providing book recommendations and setting up book displays.
• Engage library patrons by conducting programmes, such as storytelling sessions and roadshows.
• Provide quality customer service and maintain excellent service standards, including handling email queries, membership registrations, and customer service follow-ups.
• Manage temporary staff and volunteers in engaging library patrons and stakeholders. This includes training and guiding them on patron enquiries, customer service, collection maintenance and user education on MOLLY’s facilities and services.
• Ensure MOLLY’s facilities are well maintained to meet both operational and customers’ needs.
• Support MOLLY operations including preparing staff roster, conducting site recces, supervising drivers, compiling reports and statistics, crisis and incident management, financial matters, and systems and administrative support etc.
• Engage partners and stakeholders and build network to promote MOLLY’s library collection and services.
jobRequirements:
• Minimum of 1-2 years of experience in programme management, community outreach, engagement, partnership development, or similar role.
• Passion for promoting reading and serving families, persons with disabilities and underserved communities is an advantage.
• Good analytical, written and verbal communications skills.
• Good customer service and engagement skills with the ability to build and maintain relationships with diverse stakeholders.
• Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work collaboratively across teams.
• Ability to supervise staff and maintain quality standards.
• Ability to adapt quickly to change in a fast-paced environment.
• Ability to provide logistics support, including carrying boxes of books.
• Willingness to perform shift work, including on weekends.

Please highlight any other skills that you might have for example, data analytics, design, etc.

You will be based at Jurong Library and be required to go on islandwide outreaches on the MOLLY bus.

Successful applicants will be appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance.

jobTitle: Senior Engineer (Nuclear Safety, Security and Safeguards CapDev Department)
agencyDescription:
The National Environment Agency (NEA) is the leading public organisation responsible for ensuring a clean and sustainable environment for Singapore. Its key roles are to improve and sustain a clean environment, promote sustainability and resource efficiency, maintain high public health standards, provide timely and reliable meteorological information, and encourage a vibrant hawker culture. NEA works closely with its partners and the community to develop and spearhead environmental and public health initiatives and programmes. It is committed to motivating every individual to care for the environment as a way of life, in order to build a liveable and sustainable Singapore for present and future generations.

For more information, visit www.nea.gov.sg
jobDescription:
The Radiation Protection and Nuclear Science Group in the National Environment Agency (NEA) is the national authority for radiation protection in Singapore and serves to protect the public, radiation workers and the environment from the harmful effects of radiation. Its Nuclear Safety Division is responsible for developing capabilities, plans and ecosystems to support national nuclear safety & security assessment, radiological emergency response, and nuclear regulatory development efforts. The division is also responsible for ensuring that Singapore fulfils its obligations to international conventions and agreements with respect to the safe and peaceful use of nuclear material and technology.

Singapore is studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy as part of its long-term energy strategy. Singapore will also need to prepare for the possibility of nuclear power deployment by other countries in the region. These endeavours involve conducting comprehensive studies and developing technical capabilities with respect to nuclear safety, security and safeguards (3S).

You will be a key member of the team that will play a pivotal role in developing core capabilities necessary to assess the safety of advanced nuclear energy technologies and develop drawer plans for safety requirements, standards and acceptance criteria for a potential nuclear power programme.

This is a rare opportunity to be at the forefront of Singapore’s nuclear energy journey.
jobResponsibilities:
Nuclear is a complex and emotive topic, and requires a diverse range of expertise to fully assess its implications for Singapore.

By joining this team, you will have the opportunity to shape Singapore’s nuclear regulatory landscape, collaborate with international experts, and contribute to nuclear safety, security, safeguards and radiation protection capability building efforts domestically and regionally.

You will be part of the nuclear safety capability development team. This will involve:

  • Building understanding and technical competency in nuclear licensing requirements and enforcement functions across the lifecycle of a nuclear power plant to enable development of comprehensive safety requirements, standards and criteria to regulate the siting, construction, commissioning, operation and decommissioning of nuclear power plants

  • Building capabilities essential for evaluating licensee/vendors’ safety case submission

  • Understanding the approaches taken by overseas regulators to verify that operators/vendors are compliant with safety standards and criteria

  • Collaboration with overseas regulators and international organisations such as IAEA and OECD-NEA to gain insights and recommendations on safety assessment and contribute to regional efforts to build capability in safety assessment

  • Keeping up to date with current international good practices, experiences, and new developments around nuclear safety, safety assessments and regulatory review of safety analysis

  • Institutionalising knowledge and developing draft regulatory procedures and protocols

  • Representing Singapore at international forums discussing nuclear safety and safety standards

  • Participating in the projects to build up capability in nuclear safety regulation, including studies on nuclear energy issues to provide a regulator’s perspective
jobRequirements:
• Experience and/or qualification in nuclear, mechanical, chemical, aerospace, electrical or systems engineering or related fields

  • Applicants should have at least 5 years of relevant working experience

  • Excellent analytical, coordination and communication (written and verbal) skills

  • Able to translate technical expertise into clear, structured documentation

  • Able to communicate with internal and external stakeholders in a clear and concise manner, and to build and maintain relationships with them

  • Able to work in a team and independently with minimal supervision

  • Able to adapt to changes and a positive work attitude

  • Able to travel overseas for official trips and training attachments

  • We are looking for a committed team player, with a strong interest to shape Singapore’s nuclear regulatory landscape

jobDescription:

HPRG contributes to the development of biomedical sciences in Singapore by administering a robust, scientific and responsive regulatory framework.

The Innovation Office and Clinical Trials Branch (IOCTB) of HPRG is responsible for the regulation of clinical trials in Singapore. In addition to the evaluation of clinical trial applications, the Innovation Office provides early regulatory consultations to companies and researchers to facilitate
efficient innovative therapeutic product development.

We are looking for an experienced and qualified medical doctor to join the Innovation Office and Clinical Trials Branch. Working as a core member of a cross-functional team, the Senior / Regulatory Specialist / Consultant provides/leads the provision of regulatory and scientific advice to stakeholders, and conducts/leads the medical and scientific review of clinical trial applications to support the safe use of investigational products in clinical trials, facilitate innovative product development and enable timely product approval in Singapore.

As the regulatory landscape modernises, an interest and competency in digital health, artificial intelligence (AI), and tech-driven solutions will be a significant advantage, enabling the branch to evaluate advanced trial methodologies and drive innovation to increase the efficiency of internal operations.

Beyond application reviews, the individual is expected to contribute to regulatory policy and guidance review and development, day-to-day operational excellence, and the execution of key branch projects. The individual is also expected to keep abreast of rapid scientific and clinical advances, and contribute to professional networking, regulatory collaborations, and partnerships at national, regional, and international levels.
jobResponsibilities:
• Provide/lead regulatory, medical and scientific advice to stakeholders as part of the Innovation Office to facilitate efficient development of innovative therapeutic products.
  • Conduct/lead medical and scientific review of clinical trial applications, including the evaluation of safety data and adverse events; provide cross-branch support for therapeutic product evaluations when required.
  • Contribute to stakeholder training, communication and engagement
  • Lead/contribute to regulatory policy and guidance review and development, efficient and effective operations, and implementation of branch projects, including the adoption of digital tools and automation to drive operational efficiency.
  • Keep abreast of emerging scientific and medical advances relating to novel technologies, digital health and product types with a view to provide relevant strategic and scientific inputs to ensure the regulatory framework is responsive to emerging developments.
  • Represent Singapore’s interest and contribute to networking, development of harmonised technical guidance, regulatory collaborations and partnerships at national, regional and international levels.
jobRequirements:
• Relevant medical background
  • 2–10 years’ clinical practice experience in a hospital or clinic setting, and/or regulatory or scientific experience in the non-clinical, quality, or clinical development of therapeutic products in the pharmaceutical industry or academia.
  • Knowledge of the drug development process, regulatory requirements, GCP (Good Clinical Practice) guidelines and other relevant drug development scientific guidelines
  • Experience and expertise in scientific disciplines relevant to drug development, such as medical review, clinical pharmacology, toxicology, immunology, molecular biology, precision medicine, regulatory science, model‐informed drug development, adaptive / innovative trial design and statistics would be an advantage.

  • A strong interest, competency, or track record in utilising digital tools, data analytics, or automation to optimise workflows, with prior experience in developing or implementing such systems considered a significant advantage.

agencyDescription:
Yellow Ribbon Singapore
Formerly known as Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises (SCORE), Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) is a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Our purpose is to help inmates and ex-offenders rebuild their lives and lower the recidivism rate through skills and long term career development, with an effective Aftercare support network. As the lead agency championing Hope, Forgiveness, Acceptance and Second Chances for ex-offenders, we strive towards building a safer and more inclusive Singapore.

Beyond Second Chances
Without second chances, a released offender will leave the first physical prison and find himself entering into a second social prison. Therefore, it is not enough to give an offender a skill, we need to offer him a job that can lead to a long-term career. It is not enough to ask an offender to renounce his gang and past, his family needs to accept him back, and the community must be ready to reintegrate him. However, ex-offenders are not mere recipients of second chances. When successfully reintegrated, they can pay it forward and actively give back to the community too. As individuals, or collectively as a community. Individuals, organisations and employers do not just offer second chances when they can accept an ex-offender. In fact, their actions inspire others as well. Together, our collective effort can build a safer and more inclusive society. 

At Yellow Ribbon Singapore, we aim to build a community where ex-offenders are empowered to look beyond their past and towards the future. The journey is for them to make but we ensure that it would not be a lonely one. Join us, as we embark on this exciting journey of Beyond Second Chances. Be part of the YRSG family, together we can support the Yellow Ribbon cause and inspire collective action for a more inclusive and safer Singapore.

agencyDescription:
About the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore 
Established in 2015, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) seeks to keep Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure to underpin our Nation Security, power a Digital Economy and protect our Digital Way of Life. It maintains an oversight of national cybersecurity functions and works with sector leads to protect Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure. CSA also engages with various stakeholders to heighten cyber security awareness, build a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem supported by a robust workforce, pursue international partnerships and drive regional cybersecurity capacity building programmes. CSA is part of the Prime Minister’s Office and is managed by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information. For more news and information, please visit www.csa.gov.sg
jobDescription:
You will be part of the Attack Simulation Group (ASG) within the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), a specialist team responsible for delivering advanced security testing and adversary-led assessments to strengthen the resilience of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). This is a senior, hands-on role for experienced offensive security practitioners who want to apply real-world attack techniques to complex, high-impact systems in support of Singapore’s national cyber security mission.

ASG is a technically driven team within CSA focused on realistic attack simulation, penetration testing, red teaming, and purple-teaming outcomes. Our work goes beyond compliance-driven assurance, emphasising hands-on testing, attacker tradecraft, and practical security improvements.

Operating within the realities of government, we value curiosity, adaptability, and out-of-the-box thinking. Specialised training and development opportunities are provided to continuously deepen and expand our technical capabilities, and team members are expected to continuously learn, apply skills across domains, and contribute to the evolution of attack simulation practices across Singapore’s CII.

We also believe in sharing and growing our craft where appropriate. Some of our public work and tooling can be found at:
👉 https://github.com/hack-techv2/
jobResponsibilities:
- Lead and conduct penetration testing, red teaming, and adversary simulation activities across web, mobile, infrastructure, cloud, OT, and telecommunications environments.
- Execute realistic attack scenarios to assess the resilience of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII), including systems supporting essential services.
- Support purple-teaming activities by translating offensive techniques into actionable detection and response improvements.
- Lead engagements end-to-end, including planning, execution, reporting, and technical debriefs with stakeholders.
- Mentor junior consultants and contribute to raising the team’s overall technical standard.
- Drive continuous improvement of ASG’s testing methodologies, tooling, and research, including taking on problem spaces outside your primary domain when required.
- And because this is government, be prepared to occasionally switch gears by contributing to strategic initiatives, supporting and executing procurement activities, participating in industry outreach, or undertaking coordination work, all of which ultimately help us strengthen security outcomes and make Singapore a safer place to live and work.

Why Join ASG at CSA
- Work on nationally significant systems, including CII, OT, and telecommunications environments rarely accessible outside government.
- Engage in deep, technically challenging work that prioritises realism, learning, and security outcomes over high-volume testing.
- Apply your offensive security expertise to a public mission that directly contributes to Singapore’s cyber resilience.
- Be part of a specialist team that is deliberately building towards strong technical depth, continuous learning, and moving beyond compliance-driven assurance, and help shape what “good” looks like along the way.
jobRequirements:
- An attacker’s mindset with strong technical understanding of operating systems, networks, and modern enterprise environments.
- Proven ability to identify and execute real-world attack scenarios, beyond automated or checklist-based testing.
- Experience in penetration testing and/or red team operations, with exposure to adversary tradecraft and attack chaining.
- Demonstrated adaptability to transfer skills across technical domains (e.g. web to mobile, IT to OT, on-prem to cloud).
- Strong technical writing skills and the ability to clearly articulate security risks and impact.
- Typically 5–8 years of relevant experience in penetration testing, red team operations, or related offensive security roles, with demonstrated depth in hands-on technical work.
- Relevant industry certifications such as OSCP, CREST (e.g. CRT, CCT), CRTO, or equivalent are desirable.
- That said, we recognise that certifications alone do not define capability. Hands-on experience, problem-solving ability, and technical depth matter more to us than badges.

jobDescription:
Want to use behavioural science to solve real-world public service challenges?

We are looking for a curious, analytical and purpose-driven Behavioural Insights Intern to join the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS).

In this role, you will apply behavioural science to tax administration — uncovering why people behave the way they do through research, and testing what works through randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and A/B testing.
jobResponsibilities:
You will contribute to 1 to 2 behavioural science and/or design projects that aim to make tax compliance intuitive and taxpayer-centric.

•	Design and run trials: Support A/B tests and randomised controlled trials (RCTs) to find out what truly works.
•	Conduct user research: Support surveys, interviews and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) to understand taxpayers’ needs, behaviours and pain points.
•	 Analyse evidence: Clean datasets, run statistical analyses and evaluate trial results to measure the impact of behavioural interventions.
•	Turn insights into action: Combine qualitative stories with quantitative data to develop practical recommendations for better service delivery.

You will be mentored by a supervisor, work closely with project leads, and receive real-time feedback as you build hands-on experience in applying behavioural insights within a public service context.
jobRequirements:
•	Students in Psychology, Economics, Statistics or related fields
•	Strong foundation in experimental design and results analysis, including randomised controlled trials and/or A/B testing
•	Experience or interest in quantitative and/or qualitative research
•	Strong presentation, writing and verbal communication skills
•	Good self-management skills, with the ability to work independently and meet project deadlines

Internship Duration: 6 to 12 months, with intake from August 2026 onwards.

jobResponsibilities:
Keeping Singapore Competitive: Corporate Tax Incentives in the BEPS 2.0 Era

You will study how other jurisdictions use production-based tax incentives, with a focus on designs that qualify as Qualified Tax Incentives under the Substance-Based Tax Incentive Safe Harbour. You will identify common design features, assess how such incentives are distinguished from income- or sales-based incentives, and consider whether any models may be relevant for Singapore’s future corporate tax incentive framework. The final deliverable will be a jurisdiction scan, a typology of incentive designs, and a policy note setting out possible implications for Singapore.

jobTitle: Lead Consultant / Senior Consultant, Technical Architecture Office
agencyDescription:
About the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore 
Established in 2015, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) seeks to keep Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure to underpin our Nation Security, power a Digital Economy and protect our Digital Way of Life. It maintains an oversight of national cybersecurity functions and works with sector leads to protect Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure. CSA also engages with various stakeholders to heighten cyber security awareness, build a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem supported by a robust workforce, pursue international partnerships and drive regional cybersecurity capacity building programmes. CSA is part of the Prime Minister’s Office and is managed by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information. For more news and information, please visit www.csa.gov.sg
jobDescription: The Technical Architecture Office (TAO) is CSA's central authority for technical and architecture governance, driving the technology decisions that underpin Singapore's national cybersecurity posture. As the organisation's subject matter expert on all things technical, TAO plays a pivotal role in ensuring that CSA's architecture and technology investments are strategically aligned, efficiently resourced, and built to last.
jobResponsibilities:
If you are a technical governance or solution architect professional who thrives at the intersection of strategy and engineering, designing end-to-end solutions, translating complex requirements into robust architectures, and ensuring technology decisions are governed with rigour, then TAO offers you the opportunity to:

•	Partner with and act as a trusted advisor to stakeholders within CSA and beyond, co-creating system designs and solution architectures for cybersecurity systems that deliver real operational impact.
•	Provide thought leadership on integrated solution design and high-effectiveness architecture, defining how cybersecurity capabilities are structured, interconnected, and sustained at a national level.
•	Analyse national cybersecurity operational requirements, assess current-state architectures, and co-create next-generation solution designs that deliver integrated operational effects.
•	Establish and manage a repository of architecture principles, standards, and artefacts that form the backbone of CSA's technical governance framework.
•	Manage the Architecture Review Board, evaluating solution proposals, managing ongoing architecture change requests, and ensuring clear ownership of architectural decisions across the organisation.
jobRequirements:
•	Strong written and verbal communication, interpersonal, presentation and consulting skills, coupled with strong interest in emerging technology, network security and cybersecurity threat capabilities
•	10 to 15 years of relevant experience in Enterprise Architect, Network Security, Management Consulting, Threat Risk Assessment and Security Governance 
•	Proven experience translating complex business and operational requirements into scalable, end-to-end solution architectures, with a strong grasp of integration patterns, middleware, and API-driven design.
•	Demonstrated ability to architect solutions across hybrid and multi-cloud environments, with an understanding of how infrastructure, application, and security layers interact at an enterprise scale.
•	Experience working across cross-functional teams and managing architecture governance processes, such as architecture review boards, design authorities, or technical steering committees.
•	Familiarity with architecture frameworks and methodologies such as TOGAF, Zachman, or SABSA, and the ability to apply them pragmatically in a complex operational environment.
•	Professional certifications in TOGAF, Cloud Architecture (AWS/Azure/GCP), Integration platforms, or Agile Development are preferred.

agencyDescription: MAS is the central bank of Singapore. Our mission is to promote sustained non-inflationary economic growth, and a sound and progressive financial centre.
jobDescription: The Prudential Policy Department (PPD) fosters a sound and dynamic financial sector through prudential policy formulation.
jobResponsibilities:
Within PPD, the Prudential Advisory Division (PAD) formulates deposit insurance policies that support the orderly resolution of failing banks, with the aim of maintaining financial stability and protecting small depositors. You will help ensure that the deposit insurance framework strikes the right balance across competing policy considerations, and that its implementation processes run smoothly.

We also work with colleagues across PPD to design and implement the capital framework for banks, focusing on the eligibility of capital instruments (such as Additional Tier 1 instruments) and disclosure requirements. This work is grounded in the international Basel III regulatory framework and spans research and analysis, drafting legislative amendments, and engaging with banks on regulatory queries.

Beyond domestic policy work, we support senior management's participation in international fora — principally the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the Financial Stability Board. In this capacity, you will contribute to international policymaking on banking prudential issues and broader financial stability risks, while advocating for Singapore's interests. Work at these fora may touch on emerging or cross-cutting issues that do not fall neatly within any single department's remit. As the home of banking prudential policy in MAS, PAD takes the lead in coordinating and advancing Singapore's positions on such issues. Through this work, you will deepen your understanding of international dynamics and emerging risks, and how regulation is used to address them, while building close working relationships with colleagues across MAS. The role will also sharpen your writing, analytical, and interpersonal skills.

Successful candidates will be assigned a portfolio covering a subset of these responsibilities.

agencyDescription: MHA - Singapore Police Force (SPF)
jobDescription:
Are you a meticulous and organised individual who takes pride in maintaining order and integrity in everything you do? Join the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) at the Singapore Police Force (SPF) and play a critical behind-the-scenes role in supporting one of Singapore's most important law enforcement agencies.

As a Store Officer (Case Exhibits) in CID, you will be responsible for the end-to-end management of the case exhibit store, ensuring that all exhibits are properly registered, stored, and disposed of in accordance with established procedures. You will report to the Head of Corporate Services and play a key role in preserving the chain of evidence that underpins CID's investigative work.

You will be placed under the Management Executive Scheme.
jobResponsibilities:
You will oversee the daily operations of the case exhibit store, including the deposit, withdrawal, and disposal of exhibits. This involves checking, packing, and sealing exhibits to the required standards, as well as organising storage space to ensure efficient use of the facility. On a monthly basis, you will coordinate the transportation and disposal of exhibits at incinerators, and on a quarterly basis, you will initiate reviews of existing case exhibits with the various branches and track the outcomes of these reviews.

You will also be responsible for tracking vehicle case exhibits, ensuring their integrity and timely movement to the vehicle pound. This includes managing the exchange of valuable exhibits with outsourced vendors and CID officers and conducting regular audits of outsourced storage facilities to ensure compliance with all relevant procedures.

Beyond store management, you will work closely with investigation officers to ensure they comply with the relevant SOPs when depositing, withdrawing, or moving exhibits. You will also provide logistical support during major CID operations and may be called upon to develop internal standing orders to improve case exhibit processes.
jobRequirements:
REQUIREMENTS

•	Articulate and proficient in the English language, with good written and verbal communication skills.
•	Proficient in MS Office and comfortable using computer-based inventory management systems.
•	Meticulous and detail-oriented, with strong organisational skills and a commitment to accuracy and compliance.
•	Able to work independently and manage a broad range of responsibilities with minimal supervision.
•	Prior experience in the logistics industry is an advantage.
•	Possession of a valid driving license is an advantage.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.

jobDescription:
The Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) team oversees PUB's enterprise risk management framework to strengthen organisational resilience and support the delivery of PUB's mission. Working closely with both operational and corporate departments, the team facilitates the identification, assessment and management of enterprise risks across the organisation.

Beyond maintaining the enterprise risk management framework, the team conducts regular reviews of key enterprise risks, emerging issues and mitigating measures to ensure that PUB's Enterprise Risk Register remains relevant and responsive to changes in the operating environment.
jobResponsibilities:
We are looking for someone who has a strong appreciation of how engineering and operational risks can affect organisational resilience and mission success. The ideal candidate enjoys understanding complex operational issues, engaging technical specialists across different engineering disciplines, and translating these into strategic insights that support informed decision-making.

Candidates should preferably possess an engineering qualification with relevant operational experience in one or more of the following disciplines:

  • Civil Engineering
  • Mechanical Engineering
  • Electrical Engineering
  • Instrumentation Engineering
  • or other related engineering disciplines

What You Will Bring

Besides relevant technical experience, the successful candidate should possess strong analytical, systems and strategic thinking skills, and be able to examine issues from both technical and enterprise perspectives.

The candidate should also be able to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, to translate complex engineering and operational issues into clear, relevant and actionable insights for audiences with varying levels of technical knowledge, including Senior Management.

As enterprise risk management often involves working across multiple functional domains, we are looking for someone who is intellectually curious, enjoys learning about unfamiliar technical areas, and is comfortable dealing with ambiguity while exercising sound judgement.

Working with Stakeholders

As part of a small and dynamic ERM team, you will work closely with officers across PUB's operational and corporate departments to oversee enterprise operational risks and strengthen organisational resilience.

The role requires building strong working relationships with engineering and operational teams to understand their technical concerns, challenge assumptions where appropriate, and facilitate balanced discussions on risk management approaches.

You will also have opportunities to broaden your exposure by supporting the management of corporate enterprise risks and engaging Senior Management through regular enterprise risk management discussions and governance forums.
jobRequirements:
• Has at least five years of relevant engineering or operational experience in infrastructure, utilities or related sectors;
  • Preferably possesses a recognised Engineering degree;
  • Demonstrates intellectual curiosity and enjoys learning across diverse engineering and operational domains;
  • Is self-motivated, resourceful and has good communication skills
  • Is interested in of emerging technologies and global developments, and is able to assess their implications for PUB's enterprise risks;
  • Experience in Enterprise Risk Management, governance, business continuity or strategic planning would be advantageous, but is not essential.

jobTitle: Snr/Asst Director, Cyber Crisis Preparedness, Technology & Logistics Policy Div
agency: Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX)
agencyDescription: HTX is the world’s first Science and Technology agency that integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally-ready solutions for homeland security. As a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs and integral to the Home Team, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower Singapore’s frontline of security. Our shared mission is to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team’s advantage and secure Singapore as the safest place on planet earth.
jobDescription:
We are seeking a motivated Senior Assistant Director, Cyber Crisis Preparedness to play a critical role in enhancing MHA's resilience against evolving cyber threats. In an increasingly dynamic cyber landscape, this role is critical to ensuring our ability to effectively respond to and recover from cyber crises. Reporting to the Deputy Director (Cyber Readiness & Crisis Preparedness), you will be tasked to evolve our crisis preparedness and enhance MHA’s ability to respond effectively and recover quickly from any form of cyber crisis.

- Emerging Threat Trend Analysis: Work with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) within government agencies (e.g. HTX, GovTech and CSA) and/or with external parties (e.g. third-party vendors) to determine the threat landscape.
 - Strategize the Cyber Crisis Preparedness: Determine current cyber preparedness posture, identify mismatch between threats and preparedness, clarify assumptions and aspects of preparedness and formulate the strategy to enhance the MHA’s cyber preparedness.
- Strategize the Response & Recovery Plan: Design and maintain adaptive response playbooks and recovery procedures. E.g. develop strategies for various cyber scenarios (e.g. ransomware), supply chain attacks and advanced persistent threats (APTs). Establish robust backup verification and restoration protocols.
- Coordination during Cyber Crisis: Step up to coordinate with respective key appointment holders during severe or prolonged and/or sustained cyber crisis. Expected to work with other counterparts to provide updates to the MHA’s senior management in times of cyber crisis.
- Post-Crisis Review & Remediation: Work with incident response team to provide comprehensive post-incident reviews for all significant cyber security incidents, specifically focusing on the efficacy of crisis management, communication, and recovery efforts. Drive the implementation of critical lessons learned and remediation plans to prevent recurrence and enhance future response.
jobResponsibilities:
The principal accountabilities of the jobholder include (but not limited to):

- Coordinate with HTDs and HTX to ensure timely reporting of all governance matters (e.g. CCoP, IM8 & MHA policies, NIDAS findings, Cyber Exercise findings) including periodic updates as well as ad hoc requests from various authorities.
- Coordinate with HTDs and HTX on the conduct of annual cybersecurity risk assessment mandated by Cybersecurity Act.
- Perform risk assessment on issues, especially in cases of non-compliance or deviations.
- Coordinate with HTDs and HTX to provide proactive updates on compliance and health status to MHA senior management.
- Coordinate all matters in the Security & Emergency (S&E) Sector helmed by MHA under the Cybersecurity Act e.g. designation of CIIs, determination of CII boundary exercise, notification of material change, collate, update and submit CII information records to CSA, reclassification of CIIs from ICT to OT or vice versa.
- Participate in deliberations on cybersecurity matters with HTDs and CSA e.g. SingHealth COI Recommendations, ICS guideline consultations. This is to influence the requirements arising from such deliberations so that the requirements are not too onerous for HTDs to fulfil.
- Participate and coordinates in CSA’s initiatives e.g. CSA organised national and sector level Cyber Exercises, CII Preparedness Committee meetings, OTCEP forum, workshops, Minister’s sector visit.
- Maintain S&E Sector’s Cyber Defence Plan and Sectoral Threat Profile that provides a holistic picture of S&E Sector in terms of the core mission, cyber ecosystem, risks and challenges faced, development plans to boost cybersecurity capabilities, capabilities & processes that S&E Sector has in place.
jobRequirements:
•	Tertiary qualification in computer science, computer engineering or equivalent, preferably with a major in cybersecurity.
•	Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM would be advantageous.
•	Preferably at least 8 years of working experience, with at least 3 years in a cybersecurity or policy governance role.
•	Familiarity and experience with the Cybersecurity Act, Cybersecurity Code of Practice (CCoP) and public sector policies would be a bonus
•	Able to work independently as well as a good team player
•	Good interpersonal skills and negotiation skills
•	Able to work within tight deadlines
•	Good writing and communication skills
•	Good analytical and critical thinking skills

All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

All shortlisted applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement.

agencyDescription: Singapore Customs is a government agency under the Ministry of Finance. It is also responsible for the implementation of customs and trade enforcement measures including those related to Free Trade Agreements and strategic goods.
jobDescription:
[A Trade Facilitator, A Trade Regulator and A Law Enforcer]
 
Singapore Customs advances Singapore’s economic development by protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy. We protect revenue – that is invested in the progress and well-being of our Singapore community, making Singapore a better place today and for tomorrow. We make trade easy, fair and secure by maintaining Singapore’s status as a global trading hub while ensuring the integrity of the trading system. As part of the OneCustoms team, you will have the opportunity to take on different roles during your career with us – a Trade Facilitator, a Trade Regulator, and a Law Enforcer. You can look forward to seamless advancement opportunities with our integrated grade structure under the Customs Unified Scheme of Service (CUS).
jobResponsibilities:
In Singapore Customs, we work, play, learn and grow together as OneCustoms team. With regular job rotations under our Open Posting System that offer many opportunities for competency and skills development, you will get to experience our Customs core functions in trade facilitation, regulation and compliance as well as enforcement during the foundational phase. 
 
You lead and guide a team of officers who share a common objective of protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy. 
· Trade Facilitator: You facilitate customs connectivity across borders for a seamless and resilient end-to-end international supply chain, and work closely with local and international partners to advance Singapore’s economy. 
· Trade Regulator: You safeguard Singapore’s reputation as a global trade hub by upholding the rules of trade and tariffs, and keeping a close watch on strategic goods and technologies to maintain an effective and robust regulatory regime. 
· Law Enforcer: You protect Singapore’s revenue by adopting a whole-of-government approach, and working closely with other enforcement agencies to enforce against revenue-related and trade offences. 
 
No matter what your role is or how you spend your time, the impact of your contributions count. 
 
[Sign-on Bonus] Eligible officers who are newly appointed to the Public Service and Singapore Customs will receive a sign-on bonus of $8,000 paid in two tranches. 
 
[Retention Bonus] You will receive attractive retention pay-outs in your 4th, 7th, and 10th in Customs scheme of service. 

[Starting Salary] · $4,398-$5,196*
 
*Starting monthly salary may vary based on a holistic assessment of academic qualifications, relevant work experience and completion of full-time National Service.
jobRequirements:
You can be a part of the OneCustoms team to protect the revenue to be invested in the progress and well-being of our Singapore community and to contribute to maintaining Singapore’s status as a global trading hub! The role is open to applicants from all disciplines who are keen on the opportunity to take on different roles in Customs through the regular job rotations under our Open Posting System – a Trade Facilitator, a Trade Regulator, and a Law Enforcer. We have a structured career development roadmap to nurture you as a professional Customs officer. We put our traders, travellers and our people at the heart of everything we do. We serve with commitment and purpose yet being able to deliver decisively at the same time.

jobTitle: [LTA-TRO] SENIOR/ EXECUTIVE/ DATA ENGINEER - TRANSPORT AI PROGRAMME
agencyDescription:
