•	Analyse and document user needs and work with the Product Manager to translate them into user stories and acceptance criteria.
•	Engage with stakeholders to understand their needs, gather feedback, and support the Product Manager in ensuring alignment between organisational strategy, user needs, and engineering effort.
•	Analyse existing business processes, identify pain points and areas for improvement, and communicate solutions to stakeholders.
•	Coordinate Scrum ceremonies, working with stakeholders to ensure that the delivered product meets business requirements and expectations.

•	Support the Product Manager in analysing data to support decision-making, identifying trends, and providing insights for product growth or enhancements.
•	Support the Product Manager in preparing and maintaining product documentation, which includes Product Requirements Documentation and User Manuals.
•	Foster collaboration within the product team to ensure a shared understanding of project goals and priorities.
•	Track development progress, measure product team performance, and provide regular reports on development status, velocity, and other relevant metrics.
•	Drive continuous improvement initiatives within products team and the organisation, identifying opportunities to enhance processes and deliver greater value.
•	Support the implementation of changes, ensuring that stakeholders are informed, engaged, and prepared for the impact of new features or enhancements.
•	Work with the Product Manager to ensure that deliverables meet quality standards, conducting reviews and inspections when required.

agencyDescription: The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) is Singapore's national land use planning authority. URA prepares long term strategic plans, as well as detailed local area plans, for physical development, and then co-ordinates and guides efforts to bring these plans to reality. Prudent land use planning has enabled Singapore to enjoy strong economic growth and social cohesion, and ensures that sufficient land is safeguarded to support continued economic progress and future development.
jobDescription:
The Infrastructure Planning Authority Group (IPAG) drives a coordinated approach through partnerships, best practices and innovative solutions to optimise the use of infrastructure space and reap synergies for infrastructure planning in Singapore. IPAG coordinates the master planning process for major network infrastructure across the Infrastructure & Environment sector, and appoints Lead Implementing Agencies to coordinate the planning and implementation of multi-agency infrastructure projects.

We are looking for a systems-minded officer to support Singapore's upstream infrastructure planning and coordination work under the National Infrastructure Plan (NIP). The NIP brings together land development agencies, infrastructure agencies and utility licensees to align major infrastructure and development plans over a 15-year horizon. Through this process, potential issues, competing needs and trade-offs are surfaced early so that agencies can resolve them upfront, plan infrastructure provision more effectively, and identify opportunities to co-locate or integrate infrastructure for better land use and delivery outcomes.

You will work on issues that sit at the intersection of land development, infrastructure capacity, policy priorities, technology shifts and project implementation. The role requires the ability to see interdependencies across systems, connect upstream planning choices with downstream delivery risks, and work with agencies to develop practical whole-of-government solutions.
jobResponsibilities:
You will support infrastructure planning and coordination work across the planning-to-implementation lifecycle. This includes:
•	Supporting the annual NIP review, including the review and alignment of land development, infrastructure and utility plans across agencies.
•	Analysing infrastructure requirements arising from housing, commercial, industrial, transport, utilities, environmental and digital infrastructure needs.
•	Identifying infrastructure gaps, conflicts, interdependencies and implementation risks early, and working with agencies to develop mitigation measures.
•	Supporting the coordination of major infrastructure corridors and utility networks, including opportunities for co-location, integration, space optimisation and coordinated implementation.
•	Reviewing infrastructure proposals and helping agencies balance development needs, infrastructure capacity, land constraints, cost, implementation feasibility and long-term resilience.
•	Working with agencies and utility licensees to align project timelines, resolve planning and implementation issues, and reduce abortive works, repeated excavations and downstream delivery risks.
•	Supporting the appointment and coordination of Lead Implementing Agencies for multi-agency infrastructure projects, where applicable.
•	Applying geospatial, digital and data-driven tools to support infrastructure analysis, coordination, decision-making and tracking of implementation dependencies.
•	Preparing clear papers, presentations, submissions and management updates to explain complex infrastructure issues, trade-offs and recommended courses of action.
•	Contributing to policy, workflow and process improvements to strengthen whole-of-government infrastructure planning and delivery.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for candidates who can think across systems, work through ambiguity and engage multiple stakeholders to solve infrastructure planning problems. Fresh graduates are welcome to apply, and candidates with relevant experience in infrastructure planning, engineering, utilities coordination, implementation or policy work — particularly from infrastructure-related statutory boards, public agencies or utility licensees — will have an advantage.

Knowledge
•	Understanding of interdependencies between development plans, infrastructure capacity, policy shifts, technology trends and project implementation constraints.
•	Familiarity with major infrastructure planning, underground utilities, road reserve planning, utility diversion, corridor safeguarding, site investigation, GIS or geospatial analysis is advantageous.
•	Experience in or with infrastructure-related statutory boards, public agencies or utility licensees — including agencies involved in transport, water, drainage, sewerage, power, gas, telecommunications, waste, environmental management or land development — is advantageous.

Skills
•	Strong analytical ability, with the capacity to structure complex problems and identify practical planning or coordination interventions.
•	Excellent written, presentation and stakeholder communication skills, with the ability to prepare high-quality papers and present technical recommendations clearly to senior management, inter-agency stakeholders and non-technical audiences.
•	Ability to explain technical infrastructure issues clearly to both engineering and non-engineering audiences.
•	Proficiency in applying geospatial, digital and data-driven tools to support infrastructure analysis and decision-making.
•	Experience reviewing infrastructure plans, feasibility studies, implementation schedules, cost-benefit considerations or inter-agency submissions is advantageous.

Attitude
•	Strong interest in infrastructure planning, utilities coordination, urban systems, land use planning and public-sector problem solving.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-disciplinary team.
•	Confidence in engaging internal and external stakeholders across agencies, and a collaborative approach to resolving complex, multi-party issues.
•	Comfortable working through ambiguity and navigating competing priorities to develop practical, whole-of-government solutions.

jobDescription: The key scope of work for the position is to provide operational support of Energy Management Systems which involves round the clock monitoring and control of electricity generators as well as the electricity and natural gas transmission networks. jobResponsibilities:
Energy Management System (EMS) Operations & Supporting Infrastructure

  • Provide operational and first-level technical support for the Energy Management System (EMS) to ensure high availability and reliability of power system operations. This includes supporting 24/7 monitoring and control of electricity generation, electricity transmission networks, and natural gas transmission system.

  • Perform operations and maintenance of EMS platforms, supporting operational technology (OT) systems, and associated OT/IT network and security infrastructure. Investigate and resolve technical issues reported by Power System Operators to ensure continuous and reliable system performance.

  • Support the enhancement and development of mission-critical EMS capabilities, including the integration of renewable energy resources such as solar power, energy storage systems, and electricity imports.

  • Assist in maintaining and optimizing power system applications used for real-time operations, such as contingency analysis, transmission network analysis, short circuit analysis, automatic generation control, load forecasting, solar PV forecasting, telemetry systems, state estimation, and dispatcher training simulators.

  • Coordinate with licensees and stakeholders to facilitate the connection of new generation facilities and transmission equipment. This includes updating and validating EMS databases to ensure alignment between system models, field equipment, and operational requirements.

  • Support the maintenance and operation of critical infrastructure that enables reliable control centre operations, including uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, fire protection systems, and physical security access control systems.

Cybersecurity Monitoring and Incident Management

  • Provide operational support for the Cybersecurity Operations Centre (CSOC) to monitor and manage cybersecurity threats affecting power system operations and the Power Sector's Critical Information Infrastructure (CII).

  • Responsibilities include analysing security alerts, identifying anomalies, performing incident triage, and coordinating with relevant stakeholders and CII operators to investigate and resolve cybersecurity incidents.

Cybersecurity Risk Management

  • Support the implementation of cybersecurity controls and mitigation measures to strengthen the security posture of EMS and related systems in compliance with regulatory requirements, including the Cybersecurity Act and relevant Codes of Practice.

  • Assist in conducting security reviews, risk assessments, and audits to identify vulnerabilities and security gaps. Support remediation activities such as implementing audit recommendations, performing system patching, and maintaining security documentation.
jobRequirements:
Requirements:

  • Keen interest in the field of OT cybersecurity, power system engineering and serving in public service.

  • Competency in computer programming, technical hardware architecture, Linux/Unix/Windows Operating System.

  • Familiar with networking commands and understanding of basic networking protocol and security concepts.

  • Good understanding of information security practices related to ISO 27001, Risk Assessment, Application and Network Security.

  • Good understanding of Power System Engineering, Control Centers Operations, electricity substation/gas facility environments and devices would be added advantage.

jobDescription:
The operating environment of the Public Service is undergoing fundamental and rapid change. The issues we face are complex and multi-faceted, which impact the way the Public Service operates and organises itself. To prepare the Public Service for these changes, we have begun the journey towards Public Sector Transformation (PST).  
 
As part of the current phase of PST, ServiceSG aims to be on par with globally leading companies in our delivery of public services. A key transformation in the delivery of citizen services is to take a citizen-centric service journey approach to organising services in an integrated manner via a a) digital concierge via the LifeSG app, b) a physical concierge via an expanded network of Service Centres; and c) a national contact centre. Our aim is to transform the current citizen experience of having to navigate across different public agencies to an experience of the Public Service “knowing, understanding and interacting with me as One”. 
 
There are currently hundreds of hotlines across the Whole of Government (WOG). The Contact Centre team in ServiceSG aims to work with agencies who own these hotlines to streamline and integrate these contact centres, especially those that provide related services. The goal is to establish a central ServiceSG contact centre that can address the queries of citizens across related citizen services, serving as a “outsourced shared service” for selected agencies. The team will also support surges in contact centre call loads for key agencies during peak periods, and act as the central call centre in a national pandemic or crisis. 
 
Responsibilities 
Reporting to the Senior Assistant Director, you will be responsible for supervising a team to oversee the operations of ServiceSG Contact Centre, developing systems and processes to support operations. You will build strong partnerships with agency stakeholders, understand their business and requirements, anticipate and manage call surges, and ensure that the outsourced partner delivers the required KPIs. In addition, you will also design processes to ensure that the contact centre works seamlessly with other service channels to provide omnichannel service to the public.

  • Seek approvals from relevant authorities for procurement, system design, and technical specifications, as required.

MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. jobTitle: Senior/ Investigation Officer, Investigation Department, FMMD
agencyDescription:
Championing Human Potential for a Thriving Singapore
Singaporeans are at the heart of what we do. The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) empowers our people and fosters a thriving, inclusive workforce that drives Singapore's growth and prosperity. By working closely with our tripartite partners, industry and community stakeholders, we strive to create workforce and workplace policies that foster resilience, adaptability, and a bright future for a thriving Singapore. 

As an MOM officer, you will be part of this meaningful mission, contributing across diverse and impactful areas - from shaping forward-looking and effective manpower policies and strengthening industrial relations, to enhancing workplace safety standards and ensuring balanced local and foreign workforce regulations. Here at MOM, we are committed to creating an inclusive experience not just for our national workforce, but also for our officers who work tirelessly to champion human potential for a thriving Singapore.
jobDescription:
Foreign Manpower Management Division (FMMD)’s work is to maintain high compliance of the work pass framework and to protect migrant workers (MWs) and migrant domestic workers (MDWs)’ basic rights. This helps businesses get the foreign manpower they need to grow, and thereby provides employment opportunities for locals.

The Investigation Department supports the division’s missions, through ensuring compliance through investigation of breaches, as well as taking enforcement actions against offenders.  Enforcement actions against offenders can include prosecution in Court.
jobResponsibilities:
As an Investigation Officer (IO) in the Investigation Department (FMMD), you conduct investigation into offences under the following legislations:

1)	Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA);
2)	Employment Agencies Act (EAA);
3)	Foreign Employees Dormitories Act (FEDA); and
4)	Prevention of Human Trafficking Act (PHTA).

Through investigations, you play a key role in upholding in maintaining a high level of compliance to MOM’s work pass framework and protecting the basic interests of the migrant workers.  When assigned with a case, you shall identify the potential offences, plan and manage resources required to ensure investigations can be completed on time with the appropriate outcomes.  You are required to conduct interviews and take statements and steer the collection of evidence.  Thereafter, you shall make an assessment based on the evidence gathered, on an appropriate course of action to be taken against the parties investigated. You may have to plan and conduct operations.
You will also be given opportunities to build expertise through cross divisional postings within MOM to grow yourself professionally in the enforcement job function.
jobRequirements:
You should have the following qualities:
• Mission-focused; driven; able to perform under stressful situations; 
• Good time management; able to multi-task effectively
• Meticulous; strives for excellence and quality
• Good writing skills; able to put information together in a cogent manner;
• Analytical and has a curious mind
• Apply good judgement 
• Strong written and communication skills 

Note: Officers may be activated for ad-hoc night/weekend duties due to the nature of the work

It will be good if you have:
• Experience in enforcement and investigation
• A valid Class 3/3A driving license

jobTitle: Manager / Senior Manager (Operations and Service Excellence)
agencyDescription: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore's raison d'etre is to develop the air hub and aviation industry in Singapore, expanding Singapore's links to the rest of the world. We enable opportunities through aviation, making connections, opening doors and enabling choices in people's lives.
jobDescription:
The Singapore Aviation Academy (SAA) is the training arm of Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS). SAA trains aviation professionals in support of capability development and capacity building for the Singapore air hub and the international aviation community.

To ensure its continued relevance and to further establish itself as a centre of excellence for aviation knowledge, SAA is undergoing transformation of andragogy, learning spaces and service experience.

The transformation will enable SAA to provide an enhanced learning experience for aviation professionals at the junior, middle and top management levels. The new SAA building will also be a vibrant hub providing new community and event spaces for the public to enjoy.

The SAA is looking to recruit Manager / Senior Manager (Operations and Service Excellence) who would play a critical role in driving operational efficiency and exceptional service delivery at SAA. This position offers two areas of specialisation – Operations Excellence and Service Excellence. Candidates may apply with a preference for either specialisation based on expertise and career interests.
jobResponsibilities:
Operations Excellence

  • Co-create thoughtful customer journeys from pre-course, course registration to post-course completion.
  • Develop and implement operational systems, policies and procedures to streamline SAA’s operations to achieve high levels of operational efficiency and service delivery.
  • Manage and oversee the daily operations of SAA to ensure smooth day-to-day operations.
  • Identify operational gaps, conduct root cause analysis and address process-related issues promptly.
  • Spearhead process improvement initiatives and conduct process reviews to eliminate operational inefficiencies.
  • Manage operational KPIs such as SLAs and performance metrics.
  • Drive a culture of continuous improvement through agile workstreams.

Service Excellence

  • Design thoughtful customer journeys from pre-course, course registration to post-course completion.
  • Establish service standards for consistent service delivery to SAA’s trainees, high level visitors and guests.
  • Manage and monitor customer feedback across omnichannel touchpoints, analyse trends and drive actionable service improvements.
  • Manage customer satisfaction KPIs such as SLAs and service performance metrics.
  • Create feedback loops between instructors, course managers and schools.
  • Address service-related issues promptly to achieve high levels of operational efficiency and service delivery.
  • Lead initiatives to improve service quality and customer satisfaction including benchmarking against industry best practices.
  • Promote a culture of customer-centricity and service excellence through internal communications and service training.
  • Develop standardised customer communication materials to ensure consistency in vocabulary, writing style and tone of voice.
  • Work with internal and external stakeholders to deliver excellent customer service to SAA’s course participants, guests and visitors.
jobRequirements:
Operations Excellence

  • At least 5 years of relevant operations and service experience.
  • Results-oriented with strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Proven track record in implementing successful process improvement projects.
  • Experience in facilitating workshops and leading change initiatives.
  • Strong organisational skills, action-oriented, attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

Service Excellence

  • At least 5 years of relevant service management, hospitality or customer experience.
  • Adept in service design, journey mapping and process improvement.
  • Strong organisational skills, action-oriented, attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment
  • Possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and the ability to exceed expectations of customers at all levels and engage internal and external stakeholders.

Note: Your appointment designation will commensurate with your relevant work experience. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance, and may be considered for placement on a permanent tenure during the contract period.

jobResponsibilities:
The MOE Digital Excellence and Products Division’s Teacher Productivity team is hiring a top-tier product designer to actively develop and execute discovery to drive scale, tap new opportunities as we design, develop and mature tools that help teachers interact effectively and efficiently with their students and colleagues. Partnering with Product, Design, and Engineering, you will tackle our highest impact problems, influencing the overall area’s strategy for both the short and long term.

We're a tight-knit team that moves quickly and values quality, collaboration, and a clear sense of purpose in the work we do. Here you’ll join a team that values craft, speed, trust, and purpose, and you’ll have a real impact on shaping digital experiences that matter.

Your core responsibilities will be to:

  • Independently drive and deliver strategic research and recommendations and materially influencing the vision and strategy

  • Break down complex business challenges into clear research plans; lead the end to end research process and demonstrate strong storytelling skills to deliver significant impact on each product within the vertical

  • Design and lead workshops that inspire collaboration, align stakeholders, and generate actionable insights

  • Harness your product mindset and storytelling chops to influence product roadmap, by framing and telling the story of design solutions, communicating research findings, conceptual ideas, and design rationale both verbally and visually

  • Advocate for the role of Research as a strategic partner in the business process

  • Create service design deliverables including experience maps, user journeys, service blueprints, interaction models, flows, and wireframes

  • Translate concepts into wireframes and low-fi prototypes, iterating quickly based on feedback from users, team, and internal stakeholders
jobRequirements:
• 5+ years in experience, product, or service design, with a strong portfolio demonstrating both strategic and hands-on work that have led to shipped products

  • Expertise in applying a variety of research methodologies, including both qualitative and quantitative techniques, to address product challenges spanning from opportunity identification, concept testing, to feature iterations

  • The ability to guide decision-making with structured and sharp product thinking, being excellent at laddering key user needs to critical product decisions and broader business impact

  • Takes on a deeply collaborative approach with cross-functional partners and stakeholders, seeing discovery and delivery as a process to build consensus and momentum, instead of simply passively making recommendations

  • A visual and verbal storyteller who can deliver insights about people and behavior, and design decisions in ways that generate empathy and engagement from teams and stakeholders

  • Extensive knowledge of rapid prototyping methods, ranging from paper sketching to digital prototypes across different media

  • Strong sense of ownership over your work, ability to run independently while believing deeply in collaboration, a strong sense of initiative, and a comfort with navigating ambiguity, and comfort in challenging the status quo when it benefits our users to do so

While not required, it’s a bonus if:

  • 2+ years in product design and delivery, with demonstrable experience designing and shipping products

  • A deep interest or prior experience working in education, and a love for learning

  • Experience with design systems and agile processes

GovTech is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diverse voices and perspectives, as we believe it is key to innovation.

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks.

    • Operational Policy Development: Formulate and review operational policies to support programme implementation and grants management, translating policy directives into operational guides

    • Continuous Improvement Management: Implement systematic refinements to enhance operational effectiveness while maintaining compliance and quality standards.

• Strong problem-solving skills with an eagerness to design, build, and improve systems.
• Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical teams.

jobTitle: Assistant Manager/Manager/Senior Manager (ECRS - Disability Policy), FCD/EN
agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription:
The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)’s Enabling Division (EN) is the national focal point for policy issues concerning persons with disabilities (PwDs) and their caregivers and coordinates these issues across the whole of Government. Our work is guided by the Enabling Masterplan 2030 (EMP2030) and MSF’s commitment to build a more caring, inclusive, and fair society in Singapore. We partner SG Enable to develop and review relevant policies and programmes, and collaborate with stakeholders across the public, people and private sectors to better support PwDs and their caregivers.

EN’s Employment and Community-based Services Branch oversees the following policy issues:
i) Employment and supported employment for persons with disabilities.
ii) Community-based care for persons with disabilities, including centre-based and home-based options; and
iii) Support for caregiver of persons with disabilities.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be a member of the team developing, reviewing and coordinating policies to enable PwDs to live well in the community, and manage MSF-funded community-based care programmes such as our Day Activity Centres and the Home-based Behavioural Intervention Service. You will also play a key role in the caregiver support landscape and oversee initiatives such as the Assisted Deputyship Application Programme and the Special Needs Savings Scheme to help caregivers look after and make long-term care plans for their PwD loved ones.

Responsibilities:
• You will work with the team to:
o Review the needs, challenges and aspirations of PwDs who require care, and ensure our community-based care programmes provide them with the necessary support within the overall landscape of post-18 services.
o Evaluate our programme funding models to ensure they remain affordable for families of PwDs and financially sustainable for service providers.
o Plan and secure resources to ensure our community-based care programmes are accessible and have sufficient capacity to meet future demand.
o Assess the adequacy and effectiveness of existing policies and initiatives to address the needs, challenges, and aspirations of caregivers of PwDs.
o Coordinate and strengthen efforts across the whole of Government to provide integrated, family-centric support to meet the evolving needs of caregivers and their care recipients across different life stages.

• You may also support the Branch in other projects and tasks that are important to EN, such as engaging key stakeholders in the disability sector and communicating to them key policy shifts that promote the stability, self-reliance and social inclusion of PwDs and their families.
jobRequirements:
• Experience in public policy and/or project management would be an advantage.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Strong interpersonal skills and ability to network with internal and external stakeholders.
• Good written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to manage tight timelines, exercise initiative and deliver outcomes in a fast-paced working environment.


Only shortlisted candidates will be notified within 4 weeks from the closing date of this position.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.
jobDescription: Municipal Services Office (MSO) was set up in October 2014 to support MND’s vision of “An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City” by improving the Government’s overall coordination and delivery of municipal services. These services include the upkeep and improvement of our common living environment, so that future generations can continue to enjoy a high standard of living as well as a strong social cohesion in Singapore. We have made large strides in improving the quality of municipal services, by pushing for systemic solutions and championing service excellence among our partner agencies in the municipal sector. Now we are embarking on the next exciting chapter of our journey – to review more fundamentally how we can better manage complex municipal issues which could lead to protracted neighbour disputes.
jobResponsibilities:

You will help to assess the  feedback and assign them to the correct agency in a timely manner, so that the agency can follow up on  the cases promptly.

You may also be assigned to liaise with other public agencies as well as external organisations to enhance the coordination of service delivery.
jobRequirements:

Experience in feedback management/case triaging is advantageous. 

This is an entry-level position open to degree/diploma holders.

jobDescription:
The Economist Service is the premier service for economists in the Singapore public sector. By developing a core group of professional economists, the objective of the Economist Service is to sharpen economic analysis in the public sector in order to improve public policies.

Economists in the Economist Service undertake economic research and analysis in many Ministries and agencies across the public sector. These include the Ministry of Trade and Industry, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Manpower, Ministry of Social and Family Development, Ministry of Health, and Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment. Through postings to diverse Ministries and agencies, the economists contribute their expertise to inform a wide range of public policies, from economic policies to fiscal, socio-economic, health, security and infrastructural policies.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of a team of economists whose primary focus is to develop a comprehensive evidence base to support policy formulation in Singapore. Together with your team, you will strive to keep abreast of the latest economic/socio-economic issues in our public discourse, be at the forefront of the latest economic ideas and thinking, and be thought leaders on economic issues within the Singapore public sector. This will be achieved through:

(i) Identifying pertinent “hot-button”, emerging and/or longer-term economic/socio-economic issues in Singapore by conducting pre-emptive sensemaking;

(ii) Synthesising what is currently known about these issues by drawing on existing research studies and the experience of other economies to form an evidence base; and

(iii) Leading research and policy projects to provide insights on these issues within the Singapore context if there are gaps in the existing literature.
jobRequirements:
* Degree / Master’s / PhD in Economics. While a postgraduate degree will be advantageous, strong candidates with an undergraduate degree will also be considered.

* Strong quantitative skills (e.g., econometrics) for policy modelling and simulations, as well as impact evaluation studies.

* Strong passion for empirical research and extensive experience in solving complex problems using quantitative approaches.

* Proficiency with statistical/programming software (e.g., STATA, R, Python).

* Ability to distil, synthesise and explain the key insights from existing research studies and economic theory.

* Strong interest and a willingness to develop expertise in a diverse range of issues, including economic structure and growth, sustainability and resilience, labour market, internationalisation and investments, as well as productivity and innovation.

* Excellent communication skills, including an ability to express complex ideas simply and clearly.

Interested candidates should submit a copy of the latest educational certificate and transcripts from 'A' Levels or Diploma onwards, including unofficial transcripts (if any), to facilitate the processing of your application. If there are any coursework projects or thesis in Economics, please submit a copy for reference too.

Sector Strategy and Development (SSD) is a central policy directorate within the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) that oversees sector-wide policies and programmes to ensure (a) sustainable and well-planned services; (b) a competent and future-ready workforce; (c) future-ready social service agencies that deliver quality services, and (d) a well-resourced sector with active contributions from the community.

Under SSD, the Manpower Policy and Planning (MPP) division identifies sector-wide manpower challenges using analysis of manpower trends. This allows for informed policies and schemes designed to ensure sufficient and capable manpower, by building sustainable pipelines, improving attraction and retention, and strengthening capabilities of the social service workforce.
jobResponsibilities:
You will drive sector manpower demand and supply planning under the Manpower Planning team, which includes formulating strategies to ensure sustainable pipelines for key social service professionals and optimisation of the sector workforce structure. 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

•	Oversee the manpower demand-supply projections model for key professions, including review of the parameters and assumptions used in manpower demand-supply projections to evaluate relevancy and robustness of the methodology
•	Process and transform datasets through cleaning, fusion and structuring, to refresh projections or into user-friendly data visualisations for presentation to senior management.
•	Conceptualise and develop strategies to meet sector manpower needs and optimize sector manpower through alternative manpower models and job redesign.
•	Collaborate with Institutes of Higher Learning, social service agencies and other public sector organisations to ensure sufficiency of pre-employment (PET) and continuing education and training (CET) pipelines for key professions. 
•	Assess manpower implications of new or updated services, including staffing ratios and competency requirements.
jobRequirements:
•	Background in a related discipline, with interest in the social sector. 
•	Good understanding of Singapore’s social service sector/ landscape would be an advantage.  
•	Creative, analytical, resourceful and highly motivated.
•	Strong data analysis, systems-thinking, and policy development skills. Experience in managing projections methodology, handling datasets and building dashboards would be preferred.
•	Strong written and verbal communication skills.
•	Strong interpersonal skills; comfortable working with people of all levels and able to build good collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
•	Effective team player with good team and project management skills

Your work will directly contribute to the advancement of autonomous systems for multi-robot reconnaissance in complex terrain – pushing the boundaries of applied R&D in autonomy.

•	Continuous Innovation: Drive the continuous improvement of AI & robotics development tools and methodologies to stay at the cutting edge of technology.
•	Edge Robotics Applications: Contribute to software and AI Engineering for edge robotics, focusing on real-time decision-making and system efficiency.
•	Research and Development: Stay abreast of advancements in areas such robotics, networking, computer vision, cybersecurity, human-robot interaction, assured autonomy, robotics systems integration, swarm intelligence, and much more.
jobRequirements:
•	Robotics-grounded tinkerers hailing from, but not limited to, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, EE/EEE, Mechatronics.
•	Resourceful and unyielding self-starters who thrive in an ambiguous environment, with passion for taking ideas from concept to fruition.
•	Hands-on experience in robotics development, including both software and hardware integration.
•	A team player who values clean code, robust documentation, and effective communication.
•	An eager learner who is committed to upskilling and sharing knowledge to elevate the team’s performance.
•	Ability to influence and lead technical discussions, driving programme success through effective communication and technical expertise.

agencyDescription:
Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.

Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Research, Evaluation and Monitoring (REM) division, which drives the development of data-driven insights and analytics to inform health promotion strategies across HPB. The division focuses on translating cutting-edge research and emerging technologies into HPB programmes. By distilling learnings from diverse datasets, applied research, and innovative pilots, REM supports the translation of evidence into practice for delivery in national-scale platforms. The division also plays a key role in strengthening programme design, evaluation, and continuous improvement, ensuring that interventions are evidence-based, outcomes-driven, and relevant for real-world implementation.
jobResponsibilities:
As a member of the Analytics and Translation team in the Research, Evaluation and Monitoring division, you will work in a cross-functional, matrix team to contribute to high-impact projects in priority growth areas.

You will generate actionable insights through advanced analytics on diverse datasets (e.g. large longitudinal cohorts, sensors, and combined datasets), applying appropriate statistical and machine learning approaches to support risk prediction, population segmentation, and identification of behavioural patterns.

You will support the development and application of predictive models and segmentation approaches (e.g. clustering) to inform programme targeting, intervention design, and risk stratification, ensuring outputs are robust, interpretable, and relevant for real-world decision-making.

You will set up and support behavioural experiments and programme evaluations, including contributing to study design, data preparation, and analysis to distil research insights and evaluate suitability for translation into programme delivery.

You will develop compelling data-driven narratives for impactful storytelling to both internal and external stakeholders, translating technical findings into clear, concise, and actionable insights that inform programme and policy decisions.

You will work with cross-functional teams and external partners to support collaborations and analytics projects, contributing to delivery of strategic outcomes and facilitating knowledge sharing and learning across teams.

You will support the development of data pipelines, feature engineering, and preparation of datasets to enable efficient and scalable analytics, including working with relevant data platforms where required.
jobRequirements:
The ideal candidate will be a dynamic and self-motivated individual with a strong interest in advancing health promotion through data, research, and analytics. The candidate should be comfortable working at the intersection of data science and real-world application, and is motivated by translating insights into impact at scale.

The candidate should also possess:

  • Degree in statistics, data analytics, social sciences, life sciences, public health, or any related quantitative discipline

  • At least 2–6 years of practical experience working with data as an analyst or in a related role

  • Experience in applying statistical techniques and/or machine learning methods (e.g. regression, clustering, predictive modelling) to real-world datasets

  • Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g. R, Python). Familiarity with Databricks, SparkR, PySpark or working with large datasets will be advantageous

  • Additional familiarity with statistical software (e.g. SPSS, STATA) will be a bonus

  • Familiarity with programme evaluation methods or quasi-experimental study designs will be advantageous

  • Strong communication skills, especially in communicating technical findings to a non-technical audience

  • Strong project management skills and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

  • Comfortable working independently and as part of a team

  • Strong sense of intellectual curiosity and willingness to learn and seek continuous improvement

  • Adaptable, flexible, and able to take initiative and prioritise among competing demands

Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract in the first instance.

jobResponsibilities:
Digital transformation within the public sector is at the heart of what GovTech (Government Technology Agency of Singapore) does. We harness the best info-communications technologies to make a difference to the everyday lives of people in Singapore (about GovTech)

GovTech is seeking an engineering manager to work on technically challenging problems in an environment running like a modern product company, solving important underserved problems in the public sector. Some of the problems are related to different programs including healthcare, manpower transformation, trade facilitation, national development, HR and Finance products.

As an Engineering Manager / Lead Software Engineer, you will be responsible for technical direction and processes in one (or more) teams. Additionally, you will drive the design, implementation & delivery of one or more products owned by your team.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Defining your team’s engineering vision, strategy, and directions that align with the organization’s overall vision and goals.

  • Partnering with stakeholders and agencies to prioritize and manage roadmaps for delivering towards product vision incrementally and efficiently.

  • Creating a long-term technical plan and roadmap for the assigned team, and for other teams as needed. Update the roadmap regularly to meet future product/business needs and infrastructure requirements.

  • Work regularly with engineers to engage in conversations regarding their performance, professional growth, offering constructive feedback, mentoring, and guidance as needed.

  • Working with cross-functional partners to develop quality, reliability, and security strategies within your team.

  • Proactively identifying and initiating worthwhile engineering initiatives to maximize our impact on the public good.

  • Establishing practices and tools to encourage a strong engineering culture and maximize engineering effectiveness and impact.

  • Helping with recruitment, particularly for more senior hires.
jobRequirements:
• Experience working on reasonably large, high-availability software systems that have operated at scale.

  • Experience in modern full-stack web application technologies; experience in modern front-end engineering like Next.Js/React.js and Java/TypeScript on the backend is preferred.

  • Have a strong sense of what it means to be a technical leader, particularly as it relates to the suite of soft skills beyond just your technical chops.

  • Passion towards engineering excellence; you deeply understand that software engineering is a team sport, and you take pride in the craftsmanship aspect of software engineering.

  • Passion towards working for public good with interest.

  • The ability to guide a team to achieve important goals together.

  • 2+ years of experience coaching developers; helping them enhance their performance and grow their careers.

What we offer you:

GovTech is an equal-opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diverse voices and perspectives, as we believe that diversity is the foundation to innovation.   

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. These include leave benefits to meet your work-life needs and employee wellness programs.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.
jobDescription: You will assist with 1. Exploring feasibility and expirement with latest AI tools to enable a bot to allow users to 'chat with their municipal data'.

jobDescription: You will assist in managing and optimising the data architecture and analytical environment that the Data Analytics team uses on a day to say basis. jobDescription:
SSG is a dynamic and forward-thinking organization dedicated to empowering individuals and shaping the future of Singapore's workforce. As the National Skills Authority, SSG leads the charge in driving the SkillsFuture movement, a national initiative that promotes lifelong learning and skills development. With a strong focus on innovation and collaboration, SSG works closely with employers, training providers, and individuals to create a vibrant ecosystem of learning and growth. By offering a wide range of initiatives, programs, and funding schemes, SSG enables individuals to unlock their full potential, acquire new competencies, and stay ahead in a rapidly changing job market.

Join the Skills Intelligence and Planning Division in SSG to shape the future of SSG’s skills policies, undertake strategic skills planning, and develop cutting-edge jobs-skills analytics. You will have the opportunity to contribute to the National Jobs-Skills Intelligence (NJSI) engine, advancing surveillance on jobs-skills trends and generating critical insights that drive the SkillsFuture agenda forward. By driving jobs-skills intelligence to support strategic partnerships with frontier firms, best-in-class institutions, and international organisations, you'll enhance our capabilities and position us as a leading authority in the skills landscape, influencing national policies and operational strategies.
jobResponsibilities:
The Manager, Skills Strategy & Planning plays a pivotal role in advancing SkillsFuture Singapore's mission to enable individuals to learn for life, pursue skills mastery, and develop fulfilling careers for a future-ready Singapore.

As an individual contributor, this position supports the end-to-end development of jobs-skills policies, plans, and strategies, drawing on labour market intelligence and industry insights to ensure their continued relevance and effectiveness. The role requires strong analytical capabilities, sound policy judgement, and the ability to collaborate across diverse stakeholders to embed intelligence-driven planning into programme development.

Policy Development and Strategic Planning

Support the end-to-end development of policies and planning for jobs and skills initiatives, encompassing planning, execution, communications, and policy paper preparation. You will contribute to policies that underpin the national Skills Framework, as well as performing meeting secretariat duties.

Data Analysis and Ecosystem Development

Analyse labour market data and industry feedback to derive insights on jobs-skills trends, informing policy reviews and programme development. You will synthesise and draw connections between industry needs, labour market trends and jobs-skills initiatives to ensure their relevance and effectiveness. You will also review methodologies, data, processes and jobs-skills related digital products with a systems perspective, identifying opportunities to support the needs of the national jobs and skill ecosystem.

Stakeholder Engagement and Collaboration

Collaborate with internal stakeholders to embed intel-driven planning into programme development. You will navigate and manage diverse stakeholder needs and interests, and drive engagement that achieves policy goals.
jobRequirements:
We'd love to hear from you if you have the required competencies to execute the job duties proficiently:

  • Comfortable working with data and identifying key issues that affect policy outcomes.
  • Able to turn complex analysis into clear, actionable recommendations to guide decision-making.
  • Effective written and verbal communication abilities to synthesize and present ideas coherently, ensuring effective stakeholder engagement across all levels
  • Self-starter with strong learning agility to independently drive initiatives and deliver outcomes
  • Iterative mindset and comfortable with fast-evolving environment
  • Familiarity with large language models (LLMs) and the ability to use them to support data analysis, policy research and stakeholder insights would be an added advantage.
  • Up to 6 years of relevant work experience in policy development and implementation, planning roles, or operational policy planning and review. However, those with no relevant experience but can show the demonstration of required skills through relevant projects or short stints in relevant areas / functions are also encouraged to apply

Successful candidates will be offered a contract in the first instance and may be considered for an extension or be placed on a permanent tenure.

Candidates are encouraged to sign up for a Careers & Skills Passport (CSP) account and include your CSP public profile in your resume. Please check out www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg for details on the CSP.

Your skills and experience counts! Come talk to us!

We are seeking an experienced Engineer/Architect to support our dynamic team delivering the CORENET X project. As an Engineer/Architect playing the role as a business owner, you will play a crucial role in supporting the organization for changes brought about by policy and process transformations and new IT system. You will be working with multiple parties, including the IT vendor, the BCA internal IT Team, line departments, representatives from the business units of different government agencies, and the end users.

Key Responsibilities:

Digital technologies for construction design:

Conduct market research on state-of-the-art technologies related to construction design. Understand the capabilities and limitations of the relevant technologies, assess the technology readiness level, and propose the way forward. This entails working with other teams in BCA.

Setting the success metrics and gathering user requirements:

Collate business requirements to be developed in the IT systems, which may include process re-engineering. Work with project teams to map out end-to-end workflows, pain points and the AS-IS process, thereafter to re-design efficient TO-BE processes. Quantify the savings and efficiencies gained from the changes. Test the system, and coordinate with users to do testing.

Change Management activities:

Assess the impact of the changes and the parties affected. Work with the change management team to implement the change management plan including the communications and change management activities.

Training:

Coordinate training by the vendor to the end users for major releases. Be the in-house “expert” for the product. Handle queries from Helpdesk, change agents and change champions or end users on usage of the system, gather feedback, and advise on future enhancements.

Ops support:

Support the IT department for operations and maintenance issues, e.g. clarifying the intended behaviour of the system, or assessing bugs and defects and mitigation measures for defects.

The following skills and experiences that align with the specified responsibilities:

  • Technology management: Knowledge of BIM and construction design technologies, and be able to formulate assessment and plans to incorporate relevant technologies into processes.

  • Have past experience with managing organizational changes especially due to process changes and IT system changes.

  • Good communication and interpersonal skills.

Strategic planning and implementation of MOH’s innovations strategy, particularly in key areas of interest, for example – robotics and automation, artificial intelligence, clinical 3D printing, and other potentially high-impact process and product innovations. jobDescription:
Description of Group: 
Looking for a workplace with passion and commitment to empower and restore lives of the vulnerable population in Singapore? Join the Rehabilitation and Protection Group (RPG)! RPG undertakes the statutory functions in the rehabilitation of adult and youth offenders, and the protection of children and families. Our mission is to empower individuals and families to break cycles of abuse, neglect and offending. You influence and shape lives, and in the process, the future of the rehabilitation and protection landscape in Singapore. To support your professional development, you will receive comprehensive training and develop foundational capabilities and knowledge on rehabilitation and protection work. You will also be given the opportunities to rotate to different exciting roles within RPG and broaden your perspectives, skills and experiences.

Description of Division: 
As part of the RPG family, the Protective Service (PSV)/Operations (OPS) Division is dedicated to safeguarding the safety and well-being of individuals vulnerable to abuse, neglect, or exploitation—including children, vulnerable adults, and families affected by domestic violence. We provide statutory interventions and supportive services for those who have been seriously harmed or are at high risk of serious harm, ensuring timely, coordinated responses to meet their needs and uphold their protection.

Additionally, PSV/OPS plays a key role in facilitating the child adoption process, ensuring the welfare of both the child and adoptive family. PSV/OPS adopts a holistic approach through early intervention, comprehensive assessments, case management, and crisis response. Our team works in close collaboration with social service agencies, healthcare professionals, law enforcement, and community partners to identify risks, develop safety plans and provide ongoing support.

Responsibilities:
As an Assistant Manager/Manager, you will:
• Provide statutory intervention and support to children, Vulnerable Adults (VAs) experiencing abuse, neglect or self-neglect, and egregious cases of Family Violence with imminent danger.
• Conduct comprehensive social investigations and provide case management for children who have been abused and neglected, and Vas experiencing abuse, neglect or self-neglect.
• Work closely with the public and people sectors to offer statutory guidance, care, and protection for children who have been abused or neglected, and VAs experiencing abuse, neglect or self-neglect.

jobDescription:
Who we are

The Legal Policy Group (LPG) in the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) plays a critical role in upholding the rule of law, advancing access to justice, and ensuring a sound and progressive legal framework for Singaporeans. 

What the role is

Under LPG, officers at the Civil & Legislative Policy Division (CLPD) do not just review laws — we play an important role in helping to shape the future of legal policy and governance in Singapore. Our team has driven reforms that touch the lives of Singaporeans every day. Some recent initiatives include:

•	Relief for victims of harassment: In 2021, we established the Protection from Harassment Court to give victims of harassment faster, more accessible and affordable relief through simplified court processes. 

•	Modernisation of laws: In 2023, we modernised our laws through legislative reforms that make it possible for statutory declarations, oaths, affirmations, and notarisations to be done through electronic means.

•	Strengthening family therapeutic justice: The Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP) was introduced in May 2023 under the Family Justice Reform Act to improve the enforcement of maintenance orders, deter non-payment, and improve access to justice for maintenance applicants through efficient enforcement procedures and sustainable outcomes. In 2025, the Maintenance Enforcement Division was established within the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office to administer the MEP, with Maintenance Enforcement Officers working to achieve these objectives.

•	Enhancing the management of community disputes: In 2024, we worked closely with the MND and MCCY on enhancements to our Community Disputes Management Framework. The enhancements strengthen our community mediation framework and court processes to address neighbour disputes. Government agencies also worked together to introduce a Community Relations Unit that has powers to intervene in and address serious neighbour disputes.

•	Safer online spaces for Singaporeans: In November 2025, MinLaw and MDDI passed the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act. The Act strengthens online safety and protects Singaporeans from online harms. It empowers victims to seek timely relief and obtain redress through a new Online Safety Commission, and through new statutory torts that provide clear legal basis for victims of online harms to take action against those responsible for such harms. 

We are a small, multidisciplinary team that values thoughtful debate, moves with gumption, and is unafraid of breaking the mould. Officers will have the space to challenge assumptions and propose new ideas.

This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about making a difference, thrives on intellectual challenge, and enjoys working collaboratively in a dynamic environment — and who wants their work to have tangible, national-level impact.
jobResponsibilities:
You will join us in a variety of ongoing and upcoming policy reviews and reforms for the policy areas set out below:

•	Lead legal reform: Work with fellow officers to review laws, propose reforms and pursue new initiatives, tackling both classic and frontier issues. These include civil, family, and community justice issues, access to justice, criminal law and procedure, and more. If you ever wanted to rewrite the rulebook (legally, of course), this is your chance.

Our mission is to empower individuals and families to break cycles of abuse, neglect and offending. You will also be given the opportunities to rotate to different exciting roles within RPG and broaden your perspectives, skills and experiences.

As part of the RPG Protective Service (PSV), the Partner & Capability Development (PCD) division drives partner management and capability building to deliver effective protection services for individuals and families experiencing violence, abuse, or neglect. We strengthen coordination of common services and enable holistic management of services run by social service agencies and vendors. The division advances evidence-based and trauma-informed practices to better support both RPG staff and the social service sector. 

Description of Branch: 
The Trauma-informed Practice (TIP) Branch leads the effort to make PSV a sustainable workplace that better understands and responds to trauma affecting both our staff and clients. We drive strategies and initiatives in PSV and collaborate with sector agencies to embed organisational practices and a trauma-informed culture where everyone feels safer and cared for in their work.
jobResponsibilities:
Brief description of Job Scope:
The Trauma-Informed Practice Branch leads the strategic effort to transform PSV into a sustainable workplace that better understands and responds to trauma affecting both staff and clients. As a Senior Manager in this newly established team, you will drive organisational change initiatives through testing new ideas, building partnerships, and engaging with different teams. This role requires independent leadership in spearheading projects that demand deep thinking, synthesis of ground-level insights, and reflective analysis of organisational needs. You will coordinate cross-divisional efforts and ensure trauma-informed principles are embedded across all levels of service delivery, creating safer, more supportive environments for both staff and the communities we serve.

Responsibilities:
As a Senior Manager, you will report to a Senior Assistant Director and:
•	Lead and manage strategic trauma-informed practice initiatives, ensuring smooth progression and delivery across multiple workstreams whilst maintaining oversight of interconnected organisational change efforts
•	Build and sustain strategic partnerships with diverse internal and external stakeholders including PSV Operations Leaders, RPG leadership, frontline staff, cross-divisional teams, and social service partner agencies to embed trauma-informed approaches and facilitate policy development, consultation, and resource sharing
•	Drive organisational transformation priorities including leadership development, recruitment and onboarding processes, client service journey enhancement, and learning and knowledge management systems through evidence-based approaches
•	Design, convene and facilitate stakeholder engagement activities such as cross-divisional workgroups and focus group discussions, synthesising insights to inform strategic decision-making and organisational development
•	Provide strategic oversight for staff wellbeing initiatives and contribute to crisis response planning, ensuring psychological safety and organisational resilience during challenging periods

This role offers significant autonomy and strategic influence. You'll need good judgement, the ability to see how different parts of the organisation connect, and skills to navigate complex situations while creating meaningful change.

The Environmental Sustainability division in EDB charts the vision and strategy for Singapore to transit to a low-carbon economy and leverage environmental sustainability trends as a growth engine. We also develop and execute national and ecosystem-level strategies to improve Singapore’s competitiveness in energy, chemicals and materials, and identify new green growth opportunities in established and emerging industries.   • Develop and execute: You will work closely with key companies, teams in EDB and relevant external partners in government and industry to design and develop value propositions to anchor Green Growth economic activities in Singapore. jobTitle: Senior / Health Policy Analyst (Finance Policy) – MediSave, MediFund, Strategic
agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
What the role is?

You will be part of a team that formulates healthcare financing policies and maintains strategic oversight of our financing mix, to support our twin objectives of healthcare affordability and fiscal sustainability for Singaporeans.

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.
jobResponsibilities:
-	Shaping of MediSave’s role in making healthcare affordable. This could involve:

     o Reviewing the sufficiency of withdrawal limits and scope coverage as our population ages, chronic disease prevalence increases, and the healthcare landscape evolves with advancements in technology. This in turn would require: 
            	Working closely with Service divisions in the Ministry of Health and healthcare institutions to identify financing gaps as care models transform. 
            	Analysing data from a variety of data sources to identify gaps and appropriate policy responses
            	Close collaboration with other Healthcare Financing teams to assess how MediSave should feature in the solution space vis-à-vis other financing policies (e.g. subsidies, insurance), while accounting for trade-offs.  

    o	Supporting the comms and implementation of MediSave policies, in partnership with other MOH divisions, CPFB and healthcare institutions.

    o	Contribute to the policy-ops feedback loop, by addressing parliamentary questions and public queries/appeals 

-	Maintaining the macro-view of our healthcare financing system, to support long-term policy making. This could involve:

      o	Supporting reviews on the long-term adequacy of MediSave, through quantitative modelling and simulation of MediSave accumulation and usage  

      o	Monitoring and identifying trends behind the growth of National Healthcare Expenditures, reviewing the weights and roles of each lever in our financing mix (Government subsidies, insurance, personal savings, etc)

      o	Benchmarking national and government expenditure on healthcare against other jurisdictions, to inform the design and sizing of interventions
jobRequirements:
•	Strong quantitative skills to analyse data and translate into policy insights. Proficiency in Stata, Python or R is an advantage (on top of Excel proficiency)

•	Meticulous with details but equally able to zoom out and think about issues at a broader system-level

•	Strong writing, communication, and presentation skills

•	Motivated and resilient, able to work independently in a fast-paced environment 


Key Competencies Required:
•	Thinking Clearly & Making Sound Judgements – Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities to support the crafting of sound policy recommendations; ability to grasp timelines, operating context and ground realities.

•	Learning & Putting Skills into Action - Possesses the drive and curiosity to learn and apply new skills, knowledge and new ways of working. 

•	Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the risks involved. 

•	Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective purpose. 

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription:
The Rehabilitation and Protection Group (RPG) undertakes statutory functions in the rehabilitation of adult and youth offenders, and the protection of children, families and vulnerable adults (VAs). RPG’s mission is to prevent harm, protect and rehabilitate individuals & strengthen families.

As part of the RPG family, the Protective Service (PSV) is a statutory service and it leads in the policies and processes to safeguard the safety and well-being of individuals, families and vulnerable adults experiencing violence, abuse or neglect.
jobResponsibilities:
Brief description of Job Scope:

Reporting to the Team Lead, you will be part of a dynamic team of case worker responsible for conducting statutory social investigation and implementing intervention to protect the safety and best interest of individuals, families, children and vulnerable adults (VAs) experiencing violence, abuse or neglect under the Children and Young Persons Act, Vulnerable Adults Act and Women’s Charter.  

Responsibilities:

As a Protective Service Officer, you will:
•	Identify, investigate and respond to allegations of abuse, neglect and self-neglect.
•	Attend timely to enquiries, take on assessment and service monitoring for cases come in through different channels (ie. call centre, emails, form etc). 
•	Work with partners to ensure coordinate case management and safety of vulnerable person(s).
•	Carry out Statutory functions of protection of domestic violence (DV) victims, children/ VAs (e.g. application of court orders and accompanying conditions). 
•	Respond on-site to high-risk cases involving child abuse, domestic violence and vulnerable adults, conduct safety assessment and implement immediate safety planning to ensure their safety, during and after-office hours.
•	Manage cases of DV victims, children/ VAs which include conducting home and agency visits, engaging person(s) causing harm and carers on case directions, developing reintegration plans, implementing case plans and conducting periodic review of cases.
•	Involve in development work to support the protection of DV victims, children/VAs.

This role involves working 12 hour shifts on a rotating schedule, which includes nights, weekends, and public holidays.
jobRequirements:
Requirements:
•	Background in Social Work or related field in Social Sciences e.g. Psychology, Sociology etc 
•	Good interpersonal and communication skills
•	Ability to manage difficult and hostile clients
•	Ability to work in a fast-paced environment in the frontline
•	Is committed to and possesses grit and tenacity in working with vulnerable populations
•	Proficiency in Chinese dialects, Malay or Tamil or Hindi preferred to liaise with clients
•	Prior experience in working with DV victims, VAs, children, elderly, or protection work is an advantage

jobDescription:
The Municipal Services Office (MSO) in the Ministry of National Development (MND) leads the Hoarding Management Core Group (HMCG), an inter-agency committee that coordinates efforts across agencies to resolve protracted and severe hoarding cases. The HMCG supports the New Environment Action Team (NEAT), an Alliance for Action intended to coordinate hoarding management efforts across the public, people and private (3P) sectors to address hoarding issues in a more holistic and sustainable manner. 

In addition, the Community Relations Unit (CRU) in MSO is piloting a new concept of operations to tackle severe neighbour noise disputes and hoarding cases. These include cases where the severe hoarding has affected surrounding neighbours, and cases where the hoarding behaviour could be due to an underlying mental health condition.

Besides providing secretarial support to the HMCG and NEAT, your primary roles will be in case management and hoarding operations policy and planning.

•	Supporting the NEAT members and building the NEAT ecosystem, including through the organisation and running of bi-annual engagement events and training workshops.  

•	Playing a part in developing and strengthening CRU’s systems and processes, such as operational workflows and IT systems to enable operations to run effectively and efficiently.

You may also contribute to reviewing the pilot and shaping how this model could be improved and scaled sustainably.

This is a unique opportunity to shape a pioneering approach to resolving complex neighbour disputes. Your work will directly improve the lives of residents and preserve harmony in the community.

•	A team player who takes initiative
•	Strong interpersonal and communication skills

agencyDescription:
