jobDescription: The Senior / Geospatial Manager is a key member of the Geospatial Services team, driving geospatial capability building across Singapore. The team delivers geospatial solutions, analytics, data fusion and conversion services, and training programmes with the objective of deepening geospatial capabilities within Singapore's public and government sectors. This role carries a strong project and product management focus, overseeing the delivery of geospatial solutions and the ongoing development of the ArcGIS Enterprise Portal, with an eye toward embedding AI and machine learning capabilities into geospatial workflows.
jobResponsibilities:
As a Senior Geospatial Product Manager, you will lead the delivery of geospatial solutions and oversee the ongoing management of the ArcGIS Enterprise ecosystem. You will balance technical platform oversight with the structured management of complex, multi-stakeholder projects, while maintaining a strategic view of how the platform should evolve to meet the needs of the public sector. We are looking for a highly organised, process-driven professional who can drive high-impact geospatial solutions to government agencies and identify future opportunities — including the integration of AI and machine learning — to unlock deeper analytical value.

Key Responsibilities

Project & Product Delivery: Own the full project lifecycle with rigour — from initial requirements gathering and scoping through to final deployment — ensuring all geospatial solutions are fit for purpose, delivered on time, and within scope.

Platform Oversight & Administration: Oversee the technical management of the solutions on ArcGIS Enterprise Portal, including platform administration, user access control, content management, and configuration, ensuring a seamless and secure experience for government users.

Technical Consultation & Solutioning: Engage with senior stakeholders across the Healthcare, Social, Education, and Government sectors to translate organisational needs into structured geospatial workplans and clearly defined technical requirements, including identifying opportunities where AI can augment geospatial analysis and decision-making.

Solution Configuration: Drive the development and configuration of geospatial applications, applying your technical depth to solve spatial problems for agencies across the public sector.

Capability & Training: Lead the design and delivery of geospatial programmes and technical workshops, effectively upskilling both technical and non-technical audiences in modern GIS workflows and emerging AI-augmented geospatial capabilities.

Strategic Communication: Champion geospatial technology as a persuasive advocate, translating technical complexity into clear, value-driven business cases for senior management and decision-makers.
jobRequirements:
The ideal candidate is a technically grounded professional with 8 to 10 years of relevant experience, with a proven track record of bridging technical development and executive-level project and product management. A forward-looking awareness of how AI and machine learning are reshaping the geospatial landscape is strongly desired.

Technical Requirements & Expertise

ArcGIS Platform Knowledge: Advanced, hands-on experience with ArcGIS Enterprise Portal administration and configuration is mandatory. You should be deeply familiar with the ESRI suite, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and associated extension tools, as well as the ArcGIS API for Python for workflow automation.

Development & Automation: Proficiency in Python and JavaScript is required to drive automation and support geospatial solution development. Familiarity with R is an advantage.

Geospatial Analytics: A solid technical understanding of geospatial concepts, data fusion techniques, and advanced spatial analytical methods.

AI & Machine Learning Awareness: A working understanding of how AI and machine learning techniques can be applied in a geospatial context is highly desirable. This includes familiarity with spatial predictive modelling, automated feature extraction from imagery, or the use of Python-based AI/ML libraries. Hands-on experience in this area is a strong advantage, though candidates with a clear aptitude and willingness to develop these skills will also be considered.

Open Source: Experience with QGIS is considered a bonus.

Project Management & Leadership

Process-Driven Management: Strong organisational skills with demonstrated experience managing full project lifecycles and vendor relationships. A formal project management certification (such as PMP, etc) is highly advantageous.

Business Analysis: Strong skills in requirements gathering, solution scoping, and stakeholder alignment, ensuring that technical solutions are grounded in practical business needs.

Communication: Ability to produce compelling, high-quality presentation decks and articulate complex geospatial and AI concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders at all levels.

Collaborative Leadership: Proven ability to build and manage diverse, cross-functional working relationships across multiple government agencies and teams, driving delivery in a collaborative environment.

As a low-lying city state, Singapore is particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change and has a strong interest in shaping effective global climate action. 

The Green Economy and Sustainability (GES) team sits within MTI’s International Trade Division, which is charged with formulating Singapore’s foreign economic policy and advancing Singapore’s economic interests in the internationally. The GES team leads Singapore’s international economic engagement on green trade issues. We also work closely with agencies, such as MSE, MOF, NEA and PMO(NCCS), to formulate and coordinate strategies to chart the path forward for Singapore’s transition to a low-carbon economy.
jobResponsibilities:
As a TIER officer in the International Trade (GES) Division in the Ministry of Trade and Industry, you will be part of a high-performing team operating at the forefront of international economic diplomacy and climate policy, shaping the rules and frameworks that will define the global green economy. You will work on one or more of the following work streams: 

a.	Negotiation of Article 6.2 bilateral/plurilateral agreements. Develop and implement strategies and policies to strengthen bilateral cooperation with like-minded countries on carbon credits aligned with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. Officer will negotiate binding bilateral and plurilateral agreements with foreign governments, drive technical cooperation initiatives, and build robust project development pipelines — directly contributing to Singapore's ability to meet its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).

b.	Global carbon market rules and standards setting. Monitor and analyse evolving global carbon market developments and develop strategies to actively shape the international rules and standards that govern high-integrity carbon markets, positioning Singapore as a credible and influential voice in this space.

c.	Green trade policy development. Synthesise geopolitical, trade, and climate trends to craft Singapore's green trade policy agenda, safeguarding the country's long-term economic competitiveness through the low-carbon transition. The officer’s work will directly inform how Singapore positions itself in an increasingly climate-conscious global trading environment.

d.	Green trade instruments negotiation. Negotiate international instruments across multilateral, plurilateral, and bilateral fronts to advance Singapore's green trade interests. Officer will work with Ministries across the government to tackle complex, cross-cutting issues spanning environmental goods, services and investments, trade-related climate measures (TrCMs), environmental attribute certificates (EACs), and sectoral areas such as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and green buildings.


e.	Multilateral negotiations. Represent Singapore at the highest levels of international climate diplomacy, including at the UNFCCC Conference of the Parties (COP). You will advocate for Singapore's green economy and low-carbon interests, building coalitions and influencing outcomes that have real-world consequences for global climate action.

As the climate space is fast evolving, an officer may be deployed across different workstreams, based on the officer’s development and MTI’s organisational needs.

The Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) is committed to providing Singaporeans with a clean and sustainable environment, and safe and secure supplies of food and water. MSE’s key priorities are to ensure a sustainable, resource-efficient and climate resilient Singapore. Our three strategic directions include economic resilience, resource resilience and climate resilience.

We enjoy challenging and diverse careers, which are bound together by the common cause - making Singapore’s living environment among the best in the world. Everyone who works at MSE has a role to play in helping to shape our environment – not just for now, but for generations to come.

jobDescription:
At MSE and our family of agencies – PUB, NEA, and SFA – we drive sustainability and resilience initiatives that improve the everyday lives of Singaporeans. As part of the MSE Family, you will be at the forefront of innovation, leading efforts to safeguard water resources, protect public health, and ensure food safety. Through partnerships across sectors, we tackle evolving challenges while fostering an inclusive, safe, and supportive workplace. Join us in shaping Singapore’s sustainable future and making a lasting impact on the everyday lives of generations to come.

Environmental sustainability has underpinned Singapore’s policymaking since our independence. As a small city state with limited natural resources, we had to protect our environment to preserve our longer-term developmental opportunities. As early as the 1970s, we started putting in place policies to do so by managing pollution and conserving our water resources. Today, Singapore is widely recognised as a green and sustainable city, and Singaporeans enjoy clean air, water and environment. Environment sustainability remains a key priority for the government. 

The Environmental Policy Division evaluates, reviews and formulates environmental and sustainability policies and strategies. This spans a broad range of areas including Environmental Public Health, Hawker Centres and Markets, Environmental Protection, as well as Zero Waste and Circular Economy. 

We are looking for a Senior Executive/ Assistant Director to be part of the Environmental Public Health Policy team.
jobResponsibilities:
Environmental public health affects all of us every day – whether we notice it or not. It is a dynamic, multi-disciplinary field that spans across policies on public cleanliness, indoor air quality, second-hand smoke exposure, vector control, and after-death facilities and services. As Singapore’s urban and dense setting poses unique challenges to environmental public health, there is a need to push the boundaries of innovative policymaking so that we can harness technology, shape public behaviour, and navigate complex trade-offs to ensure that Singapore remains clean, green, and a liveable home for everyone.  

As part of the Environmental Policy Division, you will play an important role in shaping policies that make a tangible difference to environmental public health. In the role, you will have the opportunity to: 

•	Gain exposure and build expertise in a wide range of topics, including public cleanliness, indoor air quality, second-hand smoke exposure, vector control, and after-death facilities and services
•	Drive and formulate strategic policies and programmes to advance policy objectives in environmental public health and environmental sustainability 
•	Perform research and analysis on environmental public health policies to evaluate and guide policy and programme design and implementation 
•	Review policies and legislation to ensure that policies are effective and continue to meet evolving policy objectives and operational requirements 

You will also have the opportunity to contribute to forward-looking projects on environmental sustainability within the Environment Policy Division.

jobTitle: SCDF Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) - 3 Year Contract
agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

jobTitle: SCDF Fire and Rescue Specialist (Work Study Diploma)
agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.
jobDescription:
The Work-Study Diploma (“WSDip”) programme by SCDF offers an excellent option for individuals navigating the post-ITE graduation phase, providing a blend of academic pursuit and practical work experience, thus offering the benefits of both realms. It enables them to advance their studies without financial worries and receive a monthly salary. 
 
Those holding NITEC or Higher NITEC qualifications and eager to join the Lifesaving Force upon graduation may find enrolling in a WSDip program appealing. This pathway allows them to simultaneously work, earn a salary, and pursue a diploma. 
 
Upon joining SCDF, officers can look forward to securing stable full-time employment with an enticing remuneration package. They can also stand to earn between $2,940 - $4,370, inclusive of monthly frontline allowances.    

As a successful applicant, you will receive a $30,000 sign-on bonus (subject to eligibility) upon emplacement. This sum will be disbursed in two tranches: $12,000 upon signing the contract and $18,000 upon confirmation. 

You will also stand to receive benefits from a range of perks and privileges, including:
•	Competitive salary range, inclusive of frontline / shift allowance
•	Annual increments 
•	Performance bonuses 
•	14 to 18 days’ vacation leave (inclusive of other leave types) 
•	Medical and Dental Subsidies 
•	Employee welfare benefits 
•	Learning and Development subsidy
•	Strategic Payment Scheme
•	Invest Retirement Package
•	Group insurance 
•	Obtain a Fire Safety Manager Certification 
•	Obtain an Emergency Medical Technician Certification 
•	Obtain Class 3, 4 and/or 5 Driving Licenses 

Upon completing the WSDip, trainees will continue to progress in the SCDF with more exciting career opportunities, as they are deployed to specialised roles with higher rank(s).
jobResponsibilities:
Trainees under the course will join SCDF and become Fire and Rescue Specialists tasked with safeguarding lives and property in various emergency situations. As part of their duties, they will utilise their training to respond to fires, medical emergencies, and other rescue missions. Responsibilities include deploying firefighting techniques, conducting rescue operations, and providing medical assistance to those in need. 
 
The hands-on training will comprise 80% of the course, allowing trainees to gain practical experience in real-world scenarios. The remaining 20% will consist of off-the-job training on campus, providing theoretical knowledge and enhancing skill development. Joining SCDF offers not only the opportunity to serve the community but also the chance to make a significant impact by safeguarding lives and property during emergencies. 
 
As a WSDip Programme trainee, you can expect a comprehensive career pathway that includes the Fire and Rescue Section Commander course and Emergency Medical Technical training. After completing the relevant training, trainees will undergo the 2.5-year WSDip Programme while being stationed at a Fire Station. Frontline officers are eligible for allowances of up to $300
jobRequirements:
The WSDip program is a workplace training initiative available for individual who are ITE graduates. 
 
•	NITEC Certification with a minimum GPA score of 2.0; or any Higher NITEC Certification. 
•	Applicants with NS obligations must be medically classified as PES B1 or above
•	Minimum pass standard for IPPT; 
•	For Pre-enlistees, there will be a 5-year Minimum Term of Engagement (MTE) bond in lieu of the National Service’s obligation.

MOM’s Work Pass Division (WPD) is modernising its Work Permit (WP) eServices (known as WINS-WP) to deliver reliable, adaptive, and user-friendly eServices that streamlines WP transactions for our customers. The WINS-WP Policy & Planning Office (WPPO) drives this modernisation effort through formulating a transformation roadmap, conducting thorough business process reviews (BPRs), and driving change management.

As a member of the WPPO team, you will play a key role in shaping and transforming the service delivery of Singapore’s Work Permit policies. Working at the intersection of policy, operations and systems, you will lead complex business process reviews and ground-up policy reviews to support the development of the WINS-WP system. You will also conduct engagements and prepare communications materials to ensure that users are well-equipped to navigate the changes. This role is critical in ensuring that WP workflows are robust, future-ready and user-centric, while remaining aligned with policy intent and operational realities.

The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. agencyDescription:
The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors so as to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

• Civil Aviation and Air Transport
• Maritime and Ports
• Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region.

The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).

If you share our vision and possess the qualities we seek, do join us!
jobResponsibilities:
Our air hub is of strategic and existential importance for Singapore. It supports economic links and people-to-people flows with the rest of the world, and catalyses growth opportunities for the Singapore economy. 

As competition from other air hubs in the region intensifies, we must ensure our air hub’s competitiveness for today and the future. 

You will be part of a team of officers that develops and reviews strategies and policies to strengthen the Singapore air hub’s competitiveness. This includes developing strategies to support Singapore’s air connectivity with other regions and countries, to deepen our passenger and cargo networks in a globally contestable market. This also includes reviewing the development and adoption of forward-looking air navigation concepts and systems, as well as policies to ensure the Singapore air hub remains safe, meets its sustainability goals, prioritises manpower productivity, and is future-ready. 

Looking to the future, the Changi East/ Terminal 5 development is a significant mega-project that will be operational by the mid-2030s. The team works closely with stakeholders on the planning and project management of this critical project. This includes planning for and reviewing its design, financing, and operations, to ensure that Changi will continue to remain competitive, efficient, and a place for Singaporeans. 

Beyond the Changi Air Hub, the team also collaborates closely with partner agencies to shape policy positions and develop strategies to develop a Low Altitude Economy in Singapore that supports citizens and businesses. 

In the course of your work, you will develop and review policies, which will include the collation and analysis of data, and a good understanding of the aviation ecosystem that supports our air hub. You will work closely with the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore and other Government agencies. You will also be required to work with key industry stakeholders such as the Changi Airport Group, airlines, and ground handlers.

•	Data Architecture and Platform Strategy You will assist in the design and implementation of scalable data architectures and platforms that support CSA's cybersecurity and operational requirements. This involves evaluating and recommending data technologies, designing integration patterns, building efficient data pipelines, and ensuring platforms meet security, performance, and governance standards.

•	Data Quality and Metadata Management You will establish data quality frameworks, implement automated quality monitoring systems, and manage enterprise metadata repositories. This includes developing data lineage tracking, creating and maintaining data catalogues, ensuring data accuracy and consistency across systems, and conducting data inventories and security risk assessments.

•	Analytics and Decision Support You will build and maintain analytical capabilities that support strategic and operational decision-making. This involves developing dashboards and visualisations using business intelligence tools, implementing self-service analytics platforms, creating predictive models for analysis, and presenting complex data in accessible formats for various stakeholder groups.

•	Exceptional communication skills with the ability to present technical concepts to non-technical audiences
•	Experience translating business requirements into technical data solutions

Domain Knowledge

•	Experience working in government or highly regulated environments preferred
•	Knowledge of data governance, privacy regulations, and compliance requirements

You will be responsible for building the "intelligence layer" of the CDP, developing systems that not only detect anomalies in complex railway time-series data but also reason about them to provide clear, actionable outcomes for maintenance and operations.

We are seeking a Data Scientist / Senior Data Scientist who excels at converting use cases into a data problem and analyzing data to generate value to support decision making. You should have a proven track record of delivering end-to-end machine learning solutions—from data discovery and feature engineering to model deployment and monitoring. The ideal candidate balances deep technical expertise with a value-driven mindset, ensuring that analytical outputs directly translate to better cost efficiency and improved commuter experience. A degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field is required.

Technical Skills

  • Modeling & Time-Series Analysis: Expert proficiency in Python and SQL. Deep experience in time-series forecasting and anomaly detection (e.g., Z-score, growth rate analysis, and statistical thresholds).

  • Data Engineering Synergy: Competence with modern data stacks (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks) and real-time data ingestion via APIs to build scalable, production-ready pipelines.

  • MLOps & Automation: Experience in managing the full ML lifecycle, focusing on "operational AI" that triggers automated workflows or maintenance alerts.

  • Visualization & UI Collaboration: Ability to translate complex model outputs into requirements for UI/UX designers to create intuitive, data-rich enterprise dashboards.

  • Decision Intelligence: Proven ability to build autonomous systems that go beyond simple detection, including experience with AI agents that combine statistical triggers with LLM-based reasoning to automatically categorise, prioritise, and/or escalate operational issues.

Key Attributes

  • Analytical Problem Solver: Strong ability to take vague operational "pain points" and structure them into rigorous analytical frameworks that drive ROI.

  • Stakeholder Management: Exceptional communication skills to explain algorithmic logic and "uncertainty" to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Proactive Learner: A self-starter who stays updated on the latest in Agentic AI and can independently drive design initiatives end-to-end.

  • Collaborative: High comfort level working in a "squad" format alongside UI/UX designers, Product Managers, and Railway Engineers.
jobRequirements:
• Background knowledge in Computer Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field is required.

  • At least 2 years of proven relevant experience in data science, preferably with data-heavy industrial or enterprise products.

  • Experience in transportation, IoT, or large-scale condition-monitoring systems with AI agents is advantageous.

  • Those without working experience but has strong interest in quantitative fields are welcome to apply

jobResponsibilities:
As an investigator in the Enforcement Department, your primary responsibility is to investigate into offences and/or regulatory breaches under all MAS-administered Acts. You will be gazetted as a Commercial Affairs Officer with criminal investigative powers under the MAS-CAD Joint Investigation Arrangement, where you will exercise comprehensive criminal investigative powers, including searching premises, seizures of evidence and effecting arrests during raid operations.

Your responsibilities encompass thorough evidence gathering, conducting interviews, handling of bail procedures and preparing detailed case files as well as providing litigation support to the Attorney-General's Chambers in both criminal prosecutions and civil penalty court actions. Additionally, you will be involved in enforcing regulatory actions, such as issuing prohibition orders to not allow offenders from working in Singapore's financial industry and handling regulatory appeals.

Specifically to the current role, you will specialise primarily in market abuse cases such as insider trading, market manipulation, and breaches of continuous disclosure requirements under Part XII of the Securities and Futures Act. As financial crimes are often complex and multi-faceted, you would be working closely with fellow investigation officers, and other specialists within the Enforcement Department such as market surveillance analysts, computer forensic specialists, legal officers, as well as officers from the Commercial Affairs Department, market experts/professionals and Deputy Public Prosecutors from the Attorney-General's Chambers.

• At least 3 years' working experience.

  • Strong analytical, communication and writing skills.

  • Ability to be innovative and creative in solving problems.

jobTitle: Manager/Assistant Director/ Senior Assistant Director (Service Quality)

The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.
jobDescription:

In this role, you will coordinate stakeholders to improve municipal service delivery through feedback management and citizen-centric solutions.

You will manage municipal feedback and ensure citizen-centric solutions by leading, coordinating, and facilitating collaboration among relevant stakeholders to improve the delivery of municipal services in Singapore. Beyond feedback management and coordination, you will also identify trends of systemic issues across different and intersecting scopes of work (infrastructure, environment, social etc.) underlying the delivery of municipal services, and work with relevant stakeholders to co-create sustainable and impactful solutions through performance management, digital platforms, capability development initiatives, new protocols and frameworks, etc. 

DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES

This includes preparing management papers and presentations, coordinating and supporting stakeholder engagements, supporting implementation, documenting learning points, and assessing and scaling successful pilots.

•	Develop recommendations for sustainability, scale-up, or integration into business-as-usual operations where appropriate.

• Experience working across multiple stages of project or innovation lifecycles, from planning and development to implementation and evaluation.

jobDescription:

This role is responsible for the forward planning and coordination of Singapore’s energy and utilities infrastructure, in close collaboration with government agencies and industry partners. jobResponsibilities:
2 main areas:

Area 1:

  • To work with Government Agencies and Transmission Licensee (SP PowerGrid) on the forward planning and implementation in the routing of gas/electricity services major infrastructure projects; ie electricity cables, tunnels/ducts, Gas pipelines, Underground Service Ducts, Common Service Ducts, Utilities Service Tunnels, etc. This includes conceptual planning studies which comprises budget estimation, optimising/reviewing of utilities requirements, service plans studies (e.g. space optimisation, co-location, alternative implementation strategy). Review utilities requirements, service plans (eg. space optimisation, co-location, alternative implementation strategy).

  • Engagement with other Government ministries/agencies (MTI, MND, URA, JTC, HDB, LTA, PUB, IMDA, NEA, NPark, etc) and relevant stakeholders (nature group, welfare organization, etc)

jobTitle: Assistant Manager/Manager, Brand & Content, Singapore Global Network

jobDescription:
About Singapore Global Network

Singapore Global Network (SGN) is a division under EDB that grows and engages a 220,000-strong international community of overseas Singaporeans and friends of Singapore. Our mission is to grow Singapore’s global networks by fostering meaningful relationships and communities among international talent, entrepreneurs, students and partners worldwide, while strengthening Singapore’s position as the ideal place to work, live and play.

You will be part of SGN’s Brand & Content team, supporting the development and execution of brand and content marketing initiatives that promote SGN as an international networking community among target audience segments, and building a positive experience with members. Using compelling storytelling techniques, you will creatively convey Singapore value propositions in a way that gets target audiences excited about the prospects and opportunities that Singapore has to offer.

Brand & Campaign Management

  • Drive the ideation, development and execution of brand initiatives and marketing campaigns aimed at growing SGN’s digital following, network membership and brand experience.

  • Work with marketing agencies to develop and execute campaigns across online and offline channels.

  • Serve as the custodian of the SGN brand, responsible for reviewing the effectiveness of existing brand toolkit and proposing recommendations that help foster a stronger brand identity and affinity among audiences.

  • Identify brand partners for collaboration to enhance SGN’s value offerings to members.

Content Development & Marketing

  • This includes working with content agencies, media publishers and partners to develop content initiatives and partnerships.

  • Collaborate with product and regional teams to drive content and campaigns aimed at promoting opportunities in Singapore among global talent and entrepreneurs.

  • Identify relevant content creators and key opinion leaders to collaborate on content and campaigns.

  • Help translate data and insights into learnings and recommendations for improving future campaigns and content.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.
jobResponsibilities:
The Municipal Services Office (MSO) was set up in Oct 2014 to improve the coordination, delivery, and quality of municipal services by Government and Town Councils. These services include the upkeep and improvement of common areas in public and private housing estates, and the upgrading or provision of neighbourhood infrastructure.

Having reaped these early, low-hanging fruits, MSO and our partner agencies are now on a multi-year effort to more fundamentally integrate and optimise decision-making and ground operations across the sector. Specifically, we are transforming the way works are scheduled and manpower deployed on the ground, multi-skilling workers to perform multiple, adjacent job functions, and using operations-technology and Command, Control and Communications (C3) concepts to enable more pre-emptive action that meets residents’ needs. 

The outcomes for residents and Government from this new service delivery model have been promising.
jobRequirements:
You will be part of a 10-man (and growing!) team steering the full spectrum of municipal operations transformation viz. ground sensing, pre-emptive and reactive case management, consolidation of customer service touchpoints, technology deployment, resource optimisation, contract management and post-implementation reviews.

Central to this role is sensitivity to public needs, the translation of these needs into concrete activities with clear business outcomes and working with diverse stakeholders to deliver these outcomes on time and within budget.

[Key Competencies] 
•	[Serving with Heart, Commitment and Purpose] Curious about what is happening in our neighbourhoods. Sensitive to public needs and able to think from lay person’s perspective. Adept at translating these needs into clear, concrete deliverables for team members and partner agencies.
•	[Working as One Public Service] Possess strong track record of peer leadership, project and/or contract management and delivering results in Ops-Policy roles. 
•	[Keep Learning and Putting Skills into Action] Keen to explore a service delivery focus for next posting (with exposure to project and contract management, ground operations, ops-tech development and deployment, etc).
•	[Improving and Innovating Continuously] Driven, has grit and is attentive to detail.
•	Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
•	Experience in the following is preferred but not mandatory:
o	3-5 years of ground operations
o	IT systems and project management
o	Industry transformation and process reengineering
o	Contracting and procurement
o	Planning and policy

We are looking for driven, like-minded colleagues that can work with the sector to take this progress to greater heights. If you have what it takes, send in your application now!

jobDescription:
The Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City (TEC) is a bilateral project established in 2008 by the Governments of Singapore and China to build a model city for sustainable development. The Ministry of National Development (MND) is Singapore’s lead agency for the project.

Singapore and China have been working closely to drive the further physical development of TEC and promote the growth of its green and low-carbon sectors. MND is also partnering the Tianjin Municipal Government to leverage TEC as a base for our bilateral cooperation, to promote stronger economic ties between Singapore and Tianjin.

MND is seeking a Chief Representative to TEC, based in TEC as MND’s bridge to stakeholders in the project, to advance MND’s interests and help shape the city’s future development.
jobResponsibilities:
The Chief Representative’s key responsibilities will include the following:

•	Network, engage and build relationships with stakeholders in TEC and Tianjin from the government, private and people sectors. 

•	Monitor, analyse and obtain on-the-ground knowledge and information on key developments in TEC and Tianjin, filing timely reports and updates to MND.

•	Help plan, coordinate and implement bilateral programmes and initiatives between MND and our partners in TEC and Tianjin. 

•	Plan, coordinate and run visits to TEC and Tianjin by senior government officials and political office-holders from Singapore; and provide support to Tianjin authorities in organising visits by Chinese officials to Singapore.  

•	Represent MND at events to promote TEC, including those organised by MND and other Singapore government agencies.

jobTitle: Senior Manager / Manager (Specialised and Step-down Care)
agencyDescription:

MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.

o	developing and implementing a strategy to enhance and increase capacity and access to psychiatry and behavioral services for the intellectually disabled and those with neurodevelopmental disorders
o	developing and implementing a strategy for psychiatric long term care services

•	A professional degree
•	At least 2 years of relevant work experience in public policy development

•	Ability to work on multiple projects at the same time

•	Generate evidence through outcomes and evaluation – to work with stakeholders in the research ecosystem to coordinate the evaluation of innovative pilots and programmes and methods to establish holistic child outcomes
•	Translate research to inform policy and practices – translate research into resources that can inform policy (e.g. horizon scans) and practice in the Early Childhood sector (e.g. guides, frameworks). agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobResponsibilities:
You will:

1.	Review Care Transformation (CT) priorities and care model innovation to inform Singapore’s healthcare transformation strategy. This includes reviewing major care model innovations and pilots across MOH, Clusters, community care providers and MOH Office for Healthcare Transformation (MOHT). 

2.	Assess and support mainstreaming of successful pilots to encourage sector-wide adoption. This includes working through financing, regulatory and IT enablers with relevant stakeholders in support of national-level CT efforts.

3.	Drive and oversee Clusters’ efforts and commitment towards meeting national CT targets. Work with Clusters to implement the CT agenda required to close remaining gaps.

4.	Drive and oversee capacity planning for the public healthcare system, over both medium- and long-term horizons, factoring in the impact of CT, care integration and inter-dependencies across settings when assessing healthcare demand at the national and regional level.

5.	Review and refine our capacity monitoring capabilities and frameworks at the public healthcare system level, beyond individual settings, to identify system-level bottlenecks and develop relevant solutions to address system-wide challenges.

• A degree in healthcare management, public health, health analytics, or a related field.

• Proficiency in analysing and interpreting datasets to identify trends and develop actionable insights.

• Ability to manage projects and coordinate efforts across multiple internal and external stakeholders.

sound policy recommendations; ability to grasp timelines, operating context and ground realities.

new ways of working.
• Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the
risks involved.
• Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective
purpose.

jobDescription:
Singapore is studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy as part of its long-term energy strategy. This initiative involves conducting comprehensive studies and developing in-house nuclear energy capabilities to support a well-informed national decision.

You will be a key member of the team that will play a pivotal role in engaging our industry as well as public stakeholders to understand their concerns and potentially co-create a domestic nuclear ecosystem. You will help us strategise industry development roadmaps and foster collaboration with both domestic and international industry partners. You will also plan and implement initiatives to engage stakeholders and develop local human resources.

This is a rare opportunity to be at the forefront of Singapore’s nuclear energy journey, contributing to its energy security and sustainability goals.

Why These Roles Matter

Nuclear is a complex and emotive topic, and require a diverse range of expertise to fully assess its implications for Singapore. These roles are integral in enabling us to make a well-informed decision on nuclear.

By joining this team, you will have the opportunity to shape Singapore’s nuclear energy roadmap, collaborate with international experts, and contribute to a sustainable, low-carbon energy future.

If you are passionate about clean energy, advanced technology, industry engagement and large-scale project management, we invite you to apply.
jobResponsibilities:
Responsibilities

Role Summary (Individual Contributor)

Develop national nuclear energy ecosystem, focusing on human resource development, R&D, and stakeholder engagement. You will implement strategies that foster collaboration across academic, industry, and public stakeholders to support the assessment of nuclear energy deployment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Develop and implement a national roadmap for building Singapore’s nuclear ecosystem, encompassing R&D, human resource development and industrial capabilities.

  • Identify gaps and opportunities across R&D, human resources, and local industrial development to inform roadmap priorities.

  • Develop and implement the long-term strategy for developing Singapore’s nuclear ecosystem in partnership with government agencies, industry, and research institutes.

  • Conduct landscape studies on emerging nuclear technologies, supply chain opportunities, and international trends/policy shifts relevant to Singapore’s deployment consideration.

2. Conduct engagements with external partners such as research institutes, academia, local and international experts, industry, and government agencies for information exchange and cooperation with respect to nuclear energy.

  • Establish relationships with international partners to support domestic capability building.

  • Prepare briefs, reports, and presentation materials for engagements.

  • Organise and follow up on engagement activities such as workshops and seminars.

  • Monitor developments in the local and international nuclear energy sector and provide timely insights to the team.

3. Support the implementation of public engagement plans in communicating complex technical concepts and policies in clear and easy-to-understand manner.

  • Identify key stakeholders and support design of engagement and communication approaches for capability building and public understanding.

  • Candidates with qualifications in Business, Human Resource, Public Policy, Economics, or related fields with exposure to technical or technology policy domains will also be considered.

  • Fresh graduates are welcome to apply.

Experience:

Candidates with prior experience in any of the following areas will be considered favourably:

  • Human resource development

i. Designing competency frameworks, training roadmaps or talent pipelines (ie. scholarships, attachments, training or programmes);

ii. Implement programmes to develop, retrain, or transition workers into new roles or industries;

iii. Engaged universities, polytechnics, professional bodies, and employers on capability-building initiatives.

  • Research & Development / Technology Road-mapping

i. Developed R&D or technology roadmaps at the national, sectoral, or institutional level;

ii. Managed R&D programmes or portfolios, including grant-making or research prioritisation;

iii. Coordinated with universities, research institutes, funding agencies, and industry partners to align R&D agendas.

jobTitle: Senior/Assistant Director, Supply Chain and Economic Resilience Division
agencyDescription: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) seeks to transform Singapore into a leading global city of talent, enterprise and innovation. Our mission is to promote economic growth and create good jobs to enable Singaporeans to improve their lives. In MTI, you can expect an exciting, challenging and rewarding career!
jobDescription:
With the shifts in the global order and deepening geopolitical tensions, we live in a world which is less predictable and secure. In recent years, global supply chains are increasingly being scrutinised for their ability to withstand shocks. Countries are reconfiguring trade networks and supply chains in the name of resilience and security. As a small and open economy with limited natural resources, Singapore needs to be prepared and reacts nimbly in the face of such changes .

jobDescription:

c)	Rehabilitate individuals from social dysfunction.

You will be part of a team of officers who will be working with other Ministries and Divisions within MSF and our stakeholders to formulate and conceptualise comprehensive family service policies and programmes. Your responsibilities as a Assistant Director (Family Intervention) will include:
•	Collaborate with external stakeholders and partners across Ministries and Divisions to formulate, implement and evaluate family service policies targeting moderate-to-high-risk vulnerable families.
•	Work closely with policy, operations and practice divisions within MSF to ensure seamless integration between policy development, service delivery and frontline practice, facilitating regular coordination and alignment across different functional areas.

jobDescription: [LTA-T&ID] MANAGER / DEPUTY/ ASSISTANT MANAGER, DEPLOYMENT OPERATIONS
jobResponsibilities:
The Centre for Autonomous Mobility (CAM) leads Singapore’s national effort to deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) safely and at scale. AVs will reshape how Singapore moves — across use cases spanning passenger cars, public buses and goods vehicles. In the Deployment Ops team, you take each AV deployment from plan to operating service – owning the programme schedule, driving delivery across workstreams, and managing the operators, developers, infrastructure stakeholders, to ensure AVs are deployed smoothly.

Responsibilities

Plan and manage each deployment programme

  • Work with operators and developers to evaluate, review and fine-tune service routes and concepts of operations.
  • Build and own the programme plan, schedule and milestones for each AV deployment, tracking progress against baseline and reporting status.
  • Identify risks, dependencies and bottleneck early, to develop mitigation plans to keep deployments on track.
  • Align deployment operational plans with longer-term AV deployment strategy and transport plans, so that AV services improve overall transport connectivity.

Drive deployment operations on the ground

  • Run deployments end to end — from planning through AV applications, vehicle approvals, testing and service launch — keeping multiple workstreams on tight timelines.
  • Work with industry and technology partners to resolve issues quickly and get vehicles tested and deployed on schedule.
  • Oversee operational readiness and develop standard operating procedures for the smooth running of AV services once launched – monitor performance, surface issues, manage incidents, and drive continuous improvement.

Coordinate across stakeholders

  • Bring together industry players, operators, government agencies and internal teams, aligning their requirements, securing their support, and resolving operational issues.
  • Partner with Corporate Communications, industry media teams and CAM’s Engagement team to align public announcements and high-signature events around key deployment milestones.

Communicate deployment progress to leadership

  • Prepare clear progress reports on deployment plans, and statuses for senior management, including distilling complex operational detail into clear recommendations.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge preferably in Engineering or a related field
  • Has a strong programme or project management track record — preferably at least 2 years planning and delivering medium-to-large-scale projects or programmes.
  • Organised and meticulous — comfortable owning detailed plans, tracking progress against baseline, and keeping many moving parts on schedule while working independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Works well across stakeholders — listens, builds alignment across cross-functional teams and external partners, and drives to outcomes independently while having the right instincts to know when to escalate for decision-making.
  • Communicates clearly — writes and reports well, with an eye for detail.
  • Takes initiative and stays calm in ambiguity — AV deployment is new ground, so plans will change and you’ll help shape them.
  • Hands-on programme management and project planning.
  • Experience in operations management, contracts or vendor management.

  • As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and /or undergo further assessment.

jobTitle: Senior Manager / Senior Economist (Chief Health Economist’s Office)
agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
As a Senior Manager/Senior Economist in the Chief Health Economist’s Office, you will deliver timely and in-depth analysis of the immediate and longer-term impact of our healthcare policies on healthcare utilisation, expenditure, and outcomes. You will communicate research findings to policymakers to drive policy changes and decision making. The goal is to provide evidence-based recommendations to assist in the allocation of healthcare resources so as to maximise economic efficiency, health outcomes, and to achieve the Ministry’s objectives.

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.
jobResponsibilities:
You will work on the following key areas:

1.	Establishing and maintaining a framework for the use of health-economics and cost-effectiveness analysis to prioritise and allocate resources within the Ministry.
2.	Developing quantitative models to estimate the downstream impact of measures, and estimate the marginal value of healthcare resources, to guide resource prioritisation.
3.	Assess currently available cost effectiveness models and develop new models to generate the cost effectiveness of programmes and policies.
4.	Using econometric and machine learning methods to evaluate the impact of past and existing healthcare finance and manpower policies on healthcare utilisation, expenditure, and health outcomes.
jobRequirements:
Key Competencies Required:
•	Thinking Clearly & Making Sound Judgements – Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities to support the crafting of sound policy recommendations; ability to grasp timelines, operating context and ground realities.
 
•	Learning & Putting Skills into Action - Possesses the drive and curiosity to learn and apply new skills, knowledge and new ways of working. 

•	Background in Data Analytics, Statistics and Economics - Experience and ability to utilise data analytics tools to manipulate, cleanse and analyse data (e.g. R, Python, STATA). Strong background in Health Economics, Econometrics, Economic evaluation and statistical modelling techniques is an advantage.

•	Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the risks involved. 

•	Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective purpose. Able to explain research findings simply and logically to a non-technical audience.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription:
The National Heritage Board (NHB) is responsible for preserving and promoting Singapore’s cultural heritage. The Heritage Institutions division includes Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall (SYSNMH), Malay Heritage Centre (MHC) and Indian Heritage Centre (IHC), focused on safeguarding and sharing the stories of Singapore’s diverse communities.

You will lead the Research Unit (RU) for the Malay Heritage Centre (MHC) and Indian Heritage Centre (IHC). This unit will strengthen research capacity, support exhibitions, education, and public programmes, and ensure long-term, cultural and community-driven heritage documentation. The role is central to creating research outputs that support MHC and IHC's goals and enrich public understanding of Singapore Malay and Indian heritage.
jobResponsibilities:
You will report to the Director of Heritage Institutions and manage the research agenda for both MHC and IHC. You will lead a team, advised by a panel, and manage research projects, ensure high academic standards, and align research with institutional programmes. Your work will involve guiding research teams, collaborating with external stakeholders, and ensuring that findings contribute to exhibitions, education, and outreach.

Key Areas of Responsibility

  • Develop, implement, and periodically review a comprehensive research strategy for MHC and IHC that aligns with institutional programmes and NHB’s broader organisational goals.

  • Ensure that the research agenda prioritises both in-depth exploration and the effective dissemination of Singapore Malay and Indian heritage narratives.

  • Oversee and refine research methodologies to ensure that all outputs maintain high academic rigour, adhere to ethical practices and include innovative, community-driven approaches.

  • Facilitate collaboration between MHC and IHC, ensuring that research activities are mutually reinforcing.

  • Integrate research insights into exhibitions, public programmes, educational initiatives and digital content through clearly defined frameworks and shared calendars.

  • Strategically manage projects and manpower to maximise impact on both centres.

  • Implement monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to track project milestones, resource utilisation and ensure that objectives are met in a timely manner.

  • Engage with academic, community, and cultural stakeholders to build enduring partnerships that enhance the quality, diversity, and relevance of research

  • Develop and lead mentorship programmes to build capacity among junior researchers and foster community-based research initiatives.

  • Ensure that research findings are effectively translated into tangible outputs such as exhibitions, publications, digital archives, and public events.

  • Champion initiatives to widen accessibility, ensuring that complex research insights are communicated clearly to diverse audiences.
jobRequirements:
• Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements

Demonstrates sound judgement in setting research priorities and making well-reasoned decisions. Balances academic rigor, feasibility, and organisational goals

  • Serving with Heart, Commitment and Purpose

Leads with a strong sense of public service, demonstrating care, integrity, and commitment to heritage, especially for under-documented or sensitive histories.

  • Research Excellence & Innovation

Expertise in heritage research methodologies, including community-driven approaches. Continuously seeks innovative practices, ensuring research aligns with strategic priorities

  • Stakeholder Management & Collaboration

Builds effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Ensures research reflects diverse perspectives and supports broader institutional goals

Work Experiences and Knowledge

  • At least ten years of relevant experience in heritage research or cultural history, with at least five years in a leadership role

  • In-depth knowledge of research methodologies, preferably in intangible cultural heritage and community-driven research

  • Strong leadership, mentoring, and communication skills, with experience fostering collaboration across teams and with external partners

Other Traits

  • Ability to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced, dynamic environment

  • Comfortable with fluctuating priorities and tight deadlines

  • Passionate about preserving and sharing cultural heritage, with an understanding of Singapore’s diverse communities

jobDescription:
We are looking for a motivated and driven person who enjoys working in a collaborative and dynamic environment to be part of the Data Team, under Transformation division within the Strategy and Organisation Excellence (SOE) Pillar in the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA).

As part of the Strategy and Organisation Excellence (SOE) pillar, you will collaborate with pillar divisions and across ECDA to support organisational transformation and strategic initiatives, including data strategy implementation, which aims to drive operational excellence and evidence-based decision making. Your role will focus on supporting data capability within divisions through use case development, dashboard creation, and analytics. You will work closely with DGO, IT vendors, and policy/operations teams to manage ECDA's data repository platform, provide technical and consultancy support to enable evidence-based decision making across divisions. You will also support teams to develop processes that can monitor operational performance and key performance indicators.

 If you are passionate about leveraging data to make a difference in the early childhood sector while demonstrating strong technical capabilities and stakeholder management skills, this role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to ECDA's mission through gathering of data-driven insights and solutions.

Data Strategy and Governance Implementation

•	Support management of access controls in systems or division to facilitate cross-divisional data sharing. Where appropriate, review and streamline data sharing workflows 
•	Consolidate data inventory list within Divisions, manage Metadata, and identify critical data elements/data gaps for analytics

Analytics & Consulting Services 
•	Support building and development of thematic/operational dashboards, reports and analytical output for ECDA divisions for reporting and analytics
•	Provide advisory support and guidance to divisions on effective data utilisation and interpretation to translate complex business questions into actionable data solutions and insights

•	Develop and implement automation initiatives to improve efficiency of data processes

•	Curate use cases and manage datasets within Early Childhood Datamart (ECDM) ensuring established data standards such as SG-Data Reference Model (SG-DRM), MSF-DRM and data quality standards are adhered to within ECDA divisions and data ecosystem.
•	Maintain data quality and integrity across ECDA's data ecosystem through proactive monitoring of ECDM job statuses, systematic troubleshooting of failures, and validating data accuracy and system performance

agencyDescription:
The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors so as to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

• Civil Aviation and Air Transport
• Maritime and Ports
• Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region.

The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).
jobDescription:
Singapore is internationally renowned for our transport infrastructure and for being a global aviation and maritime hub. At the Ministry of Transport (MOT), we spearhead developments in our air, land and sea transport sectors to advance Singapore’s economic competitiveness and Singaporeans’ quality of life. We seek dynamic, analytical and committed individuals to join our able MOT team in realising our vision of a global interconnected transport hub.

If you share our vision and possess the qualities we seek, do join us!
jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of the Strategic Planning team within MOT’s Strategic Planning & Organisational Transformation Division. The job will require you to:

a)	Plan, coordinate and implement the MOT Family strategic planning agenda by collaborating with senior leaders, MOT’s Divisions and our Statutory Boards as well as other government agencies to align with the Whole-of-Government (WoG) objectives and outcomes.

b)	Plan, review and coordinate the annual strategic planning, resource planning and reporting cycle to ensure accountability, drive alignment and achievement of WoG and MOT Family strategic objectives and priorities. 

c)	Analyse data and information to identify patterns, trends, outliers, insights and threats to better support evidence-based decisions and policy development, as well as undertake foresight-related environment scanning and develop a portfolio of up-to-date foresight capabilities and products. 

d)	Coordinate and track the development and implementation of policies and programmes by business units to ensure that resources, capabilities and structures enable us to deliver well.

e)	Oversee Ministry Family Parliamentary Matters with the objective of enhancing parliamentary engagement and coordination, support coherence in policy positions and narratives, and strengthen institutional capability across the MOT on Parliamentary matters.
jobRequirements:
You should be a Singapore citizen with at least 4 years of relevant working experience in a policy/corporate/strategic planning role. You should be results-oriented, highly self-motivated, resilient and possess the ability to connect effectively with diverse stakeholders both at the individual and group level. You should also be a good team player, possessing excellent analytical, communications and organisational skills, with the ability to distil complex information into actionable insights. Meticulous attention to details is necessary as well as the ability to multi-task and work well under tight deadlines.  

Job holders would have the opportunity to work in different or multiple sections within the Division, taking into consideration the officers’ competencies and development needs, as well as the needs of the Division.

jobTitle: Senior Manager / Manager, Research, Communications and Engagement Department
agencyDescription:
Championing Human Potential for a Thriving Singapore
Singaporeans are at the heart of what we do. The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) empowers our people and fosters a thriving, inclusive workforce that drives Singapore's growth and prosperity. By working closely with our tripartite partners, industry and community stakeholders, we strive to create workforce and workplace policies that foster resilience, adaptability, and a bright future for a thriving Singapore. 

As an MOM officer, you will be part of this meaningful mission, contributing across diverse and impactful areas - from shaping forward-looking and effective manpower policies and strengthening industrial relations, to enhancing workplace safety standards and ensuring balanced local and foreign workforce regulations. Here at MOM, we are committed to creating an inclusive experience not just for our national workforce, but also for our officers who work tirelessly to champion human potential for a thriving Singapore.
jobDescription:
The Communications and Engagement Department leads MOM's efforts in developing evidence-based communications strategies that enhance public understanding and engagement across all policy areas. Within the department, research plays a critical role in measuring communication effectiveness, understanding public sentiment, and providing insights that inform strategic decision-making to better serve Singaporeans.

You will help develop comprehensive research studies to support communications effectiveness across MOM's diverse policy portfolio. This involves leading both quantitative and qualitative research projects, including message testing, campaign evaluation, sentiment analysis, and awareness tracking, whilst working closely with external research vendors and internal stakeholders including policy teams and communications specialists across various MOM departments.
jobResponsibilities:
This role involves designing and executing both quantitative and qualitative research projects to support communications effectiveness across MOM. You will work with multiple stakeholders across MOM departments and CED colleagues to develop robust research methodologies, conduct message testing and campaign evaluation, and provide critical insights that enhance public engagement with government policies and programmes.

You will manage research projects from conception through to final reporting, including focus group discussions, surveys, sentiment analysis, and awareness tracking. The role requires adapting research approaches to suit the specific requirements and sensitivities of different policy domains whilst building productive relationships with internal teams and external research vendors. You will also monitor public sentiment across various channels and develop tracking systems to measure policy awareness and identify emerging communication trends.
jobRequirements:
•	A tertiary qualification in a relevant field such as Business, Psychology, Social Science, or Public Policy
•	Fresh graduates welcome; candidates with 2-3 years of working experience in qualitative and/or quantitative research preferred
•	Strong interest in using research to help stakeholders make data-driven decisions regarding government communications
•	Excellent interpersonal and stakeholder management skills with ability to work effectively across multiple teams
•	Strong communication and writing skills with ability to translate research findings into actionable recommendations
•	Comfortable using statistical analytical tools such as SPSS, R, or Python, and data visualisation software such as Tableau or Power BI, or keen to develop these skills
•	Self-driven and resourceful with strong project management capabilities
•	Takes initiative and ownership to deliver quality research that serves the public good.

PWDs are welcome to apply

jobDescription:
As a Senior Software Engineer in our AI Product Team, you will play a critical role in transforming how analysts process and analyse information. You will work at the forefront of applied AI, building intelligent systems that enhance sense-making, information discovery, and decision-support for national security.
 
In this role, you will design and develop AI-driven applications, such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems and intelligent automation workflows, as well as the supporting web systems and data processing pipelines that power these capabilities. You will contribute across the full technology stack, from backend services and data retrieval layers to frontend interfaces that bring AI functionalities to users. Our team focuses on applying and integrating AI technologies rather than model training or fine-tuning, emphasizing innovation, rapid experimentation, and real-world impact.

Why join us?
• You are, and can continue to be, one of the sharpest engineering minds that builds, innovates, and translates technologies into future-proofed digital solutions with precision and agility.
• You will have plenty of opportunities to deepen your domain expertise while developing adjacent areas of interest and competencies as part of this diverse community
• The products you lead to develop, together with us, will lay one of the core foundations for the next-generation digital products for our business users.
• You, too, believe in harnessing data and best-in-class technologies to deliver simple, yet sophisticated products that power our analysts and leaders for the long run.
