Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today!

Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg.

Who We Are

CCYC (Culture, Community and Youth Cluster) is part of GovTech’s Government Digital Transformation team. We partner with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and its statutory boards — including the National Arts Council (NAC), People’s Association (PA), Sport Singapore (SportSG), and MUIS — to deliver digital products that strengthen social cohesion, cultural participation, and youth engagement.

Our product ecosystem spans community engagement platforms, cultural and arts enablement tools, youth development products, and sports and active lifestyle services — used by hundreds of thousands of Singaporeans.

[What you will be working on]

Lead Across the Ecosystem

Where a Senior Designer owns a product, you own the design layer across CCYC’s product portfolio. You see across product lines, identify gaps and inconsistencies, and make deliberate decisions about where to invest design effort for the greatest cross-cluster impact. You bring coherence to an ecosystem of products — without flattening the distinctive needs each one serves.

Mentor and Grow the Team

You actively invest in the development of the designers around you. You give feedback that is specific, actionable and grounded in the work. You create the conditions for others to do their best work — clearing blockers, sharing what you know without being asked, and treating every critique or check-in as an opportunity to build someone’s capability, not just improve a screen.

You notice when a designer is stuck, stretched or struggling, and you engage — not to take over, but to help them find their footing. You don’t measure your success by the quality of your own work alone. You measure it by the standard of the work the whole team produces.

Shape Design Strategy

You work at the intersection of design and product strategy. You contribute to roadmap discussions, bring design’s perspective to prioritisation, and articulate the value of good design in terms that resonate with product managers, engineers and senior leadership. You know when to advocate and when to adapt — and you rarely confuse the two.

You can hold a long view alongside the short one: thinking about where the ecosystem needs to go in 12 to 18 months, while staying close enough to the current work to course-correct in the next sprint.

Own ResearchOps

Research here is not a phase — it’s a discipline that needs infrastructure. You will design and steward the systems that make research sustainable and accessible: participant recruitment pipelines, consent and data governance practices, shared repositories, and frameworks that help the whole team synthesise and apply what they learn.

You ensure that insights don’t live in decks or individuals’ heads — they become institutional knowledge that informs product decisions across the cluster.

Build and Sustain DesignOps

You take responsibility for how design works — the processes, rituals, standards and tooling that determine whether the team can do good work at pace. This includes: maintaining design system governance, running effective critiques and design reviews, managing handoff quality with engineering, and establishing shared norms around file hygiene, documentation and version control.

You treat operations as a design problem: how do we structure the way we work so that quality is the default, not the exception?

Communicate with Clarity and Purpose

Every artefact you produce — a presentation, a brief, a feedback comment, a Slack message — is communication. You are deliberate about what you say, how you say it, and to whom. You match your communication to your audience and your objective. You don’t over-explain and you don’t under-specify.

You are especially clear when things are uncertain or complex. In moments of ambiguity, your communication creates alignment rather than adding noise.

[What we are looking for]

We are looking for a Lead UX Designer to take on both strategic and operational ownership of design across the CCYC product ecosystem. This is a step up from being a strong individual practitioner: you will shape how design is done here, not just what gets designed.

You bring deep craft, but you no longer keep it to yourself. You see the whole ecosystem and the people inside it — and you understand that the quality of the work is inseparable from the health of the team producing it. You make the people around you better, not by pushing them, but by showing them what good looks like and making it easier for them to get there.

You think clearly and communicate with intention. Whether you’re presenting a design direction to senior stakeholders, writing a research brief, or giving feedback in a crit, you say what matters and leave out what doesn’t. You can shift register — from a strategy conversation with leadership to a pairing session with a junior designer — without losing clarity in either.

This is a player-coach role. You will continue to do hands-on design work on complex, high-stakes parts of the product — but you will also be responsible for growing the practice, mentoring others, and owning how design operates at scale across the cluster.

  • Experience: 8+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio that spans product lifecycle ownership, ecosystem-level thinking, and measurable outcomes — not just polished screens.
  • People Development: Demonstrated experience mentoring or managing designers, with clear examples of how you’ve helped others grow their craft, confidence or career trajectory.
  • Strategic Range: Ability to think and operate at both the strategic and execution layer — you can set direction and get into the details when it matters.
  • ResearchOps: Hands-on experience establishing or significantly improving research operations: recruitment, repositories, governance, or synthesis practices at team or organisational scale.
  • DesignOps: Experience owning design operations: design systems governance, crit culture, handoff processes, tooling standards, or documentation frameworks.
  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills. You write clearly, present confidently, and can adapt your communication style to different audiences without losing your point.
  • Craft: Strong UX fundamentals — research, information architecture, interaction and visual design — applied with rigour and pragmatism in a live product environment.

jobTitle: Principal / Lead Product Manager, TradeNet, DEP
jobDescription:
GovTech is Singapore's lead agency for digital government and the Smart Nation initiative. We build and deploy technology that meaningfully improves lives — for citizens, businesses, and the public sector.

Digital Economy Products (DEP) is a division within GovTech that operates with the pace and rigour of a modern product company. Our teams tackle high-stakes problems across Singapore's public sectors — Healthcare, Manpower, Trade and Finance, National Development, Sustainability, and more — and build digital products that serve millions.

Many of Singapore's most critical government systems were built decades ago — pioneering for their time, but now running on aging technology, tightly bound to vendor dependencies, and struggling to keep pace with evolving policy and industry demands. We are bringing these platforms in-house and rebuilding them from the ground up — rethinking not just the technology, but the operating models, user experiences, and regulatory workflows they underpin.

Two flagship programmes are currently underway:

TradeNet — Singapore's National Single Window for trade permit processing. Launched in the late 1980s, it processes over 9 million permit applications annually across import, export, and transshipment, contributing to approximately 10% of national tax revenues. Designated as critical IT infrastructure, TradeNet is being brought in-house to secure Singapore's technology sovereignty over one of its most consequential trade systems.

CoreNet X — Singapore's national digital platform for regulatory approval of building works. It unifies eight regulatory agencies into a single BIM-based submission and processing system, transforming how the built environment sector interacts with government.

Both programmes sit at the intersection of complex regulation, enterprise-scale technology, and high public-sector impact. As a Principal Product Manager at DEP, you will be at the centre of this transformation — working at the frontier of how government systems are redesigned, rebuilt, and reimagined for the future.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own the product strategy for modernisation of your key system(s).
  • Translate complex business, technical, and policy insights into clear roadmaps that align teams and drive measurable outcomes.
  • Establish success metrics (OKRs, KPIs) and ensure alignment with the policy, business, and operational objectives.
  • Build strong stakeholder alignment through evidence, trust, and well-earned relationships — resolving complex dependencies and securing senior management support for product strategy and investments.
  • Develop deep system and domain expertise, serving as the subject-matter expert for your product(s) — bringing informed perspective to agency escalations, regulatory tradeoffs, and decisions that shape product approach across government and industry stakeholders.
  • Champion adoption of emerging technologies and industry best practices to improve team effectiveness and impact.
  • Lead and mentor a team of talented product managers, setting the bar for product thinking, execution rigour, and professional development of each team member.
  • Lead hiring of other product leaders for your team and outside, identify and coach future leaders
  • Lead end‑to‑end product execution of a major product —from ideation to launch to iteration—ensuring high standards of quality, security, accessibility, and compliance.
  • Collaborate with engineering, design, research, operations, and data teams to deliver cohesive, scalable user experiences.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years of product management or equivalent experience with strong demonstrated impact in the consumer/enterprise/platform ecosystem.
  • Track record of delivering complex products at scale with measurable business impact.
  • Excellent communication and leadership skills, capable of inspiring teams and influencing senior leaders.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills — ability to navigate complex, multi-agency environments and build alignment across government agencies, vendor partners, and industry players.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to leverage data to inform product decisions.
  • Proven experience hiring, managing, mentoring, and coaching a team of product managers.

jobTitle: Principal / Lead Software Engineer (Cybersecurity Specialist) — TradeNet CII
jobDescription:
About GovTech

The Government Technology Agency (GovTech) transforms the delivery of Government digital services by taking an "outside-in" view, putting citizens and businesses at the heart of everything we do. We build the Smart Nation infrastructure and the platforms the public sector runs on, and we partner agencies to engineer trustworthy, resilient digital services at national scale.

What is this role?

TradeNet is Singapore's national single-window trade platform and a legislated Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). Its availability and integrity underpin national trade continuity; disruption is an economic event, not a system outage.

We are seeking a Principal / Lead level Software Engineer (Cybersecurity Specialist) to be the technical design authority for the modernised TradeNet CII rebuild, focusing on architecture security and resilience.

This is an architect-and-build mandate, not an assurance or operations role. As a first-line engineering role, you will

  1. Design and embed security and resilience controls into the platform starting from the architecture and down to the implementation details.
  2. Decide what is inherited from the GovTech security tech stack versus built and owned by the product team.
  3. Design the defensive terrain jointly with the Singapore Customs Agency CISO (ACISO) so that the agency can defensibly discharge its CII regulatory accountability to Cyber Security Agency (CSA).

You will be measured on the delivery of TradeNet CII that is secure and resilient by design and construction — not on the volume of findings triaged or evidence produced after the fact.

Impact and outcomes

You will be successful when:

  • TradeNet's security architecture is conformant with CSA CCoP v2 and WOG IM8 by design, not by downstream remediation, and the conformance basis is clearly documented and defensible to CSA.
  • The Customs ACISO can stand behind a coherent, evidenced security and resilience architecture for the CII without reconstructing it from operational artefacts.
  • The platform has an engineered national trade-continuity posture — recoverability, degraded-mode operation, and containment of blast radius are designed properties, not aspirations.
  • The boundary between controls inherited from the GovTech security tech stack and controls owned by the TradeNet product is explicit, maintained, and used to scope CII audit and attestation.
  • Security control intent is expressed as code and continuously monitored, reducing reliance on point-in-time attestation.
  • There is a strong culture of security in the organization through your leadership, mentorship and coaching.

What you will be working on

Secure and resilient architecture (core mandate)

  • Own the reference security architecture for the TradeNet CII: trust boundaries, identity architecture, segmentation and trust-zone strategy, east-west controls, encryption and key management, and blast-radius containment for the CII boundary.
  • Embed secure-by-design controls by working inside product and engineering teams through the delivery lifecycle — at design, solutioning and implementation time, not as post-build validation.
  • Maintain a living threat model per system and trust boundary, referenced to MITRE ATT&CK and to relevant adversary classes (including supply-chain and nation-state), and use it to drive architecture and segmentation decisions — not merely to prioritise remediation.

Resilience and national trade continuity

  • Engineer the platform's recoverability and graceful degradation: degraded-mode operation, recovery objectives appropriate to a national single-window, and containment design that preserves trade continuity under attack.
  • Map and treat dependency and concentration risk across the TradeNet ecosystem (traders, brokers, ports, and partner agencies), including third-party and supply-chain integration risk.
  • Design for, and participate in, CSA-mandated cyber resilience exercising for the CII, feeding findings back into the architecture.

Defensive terrain (with the Customs ACISO)

  • Partner the Customs ACISO as the technical design authority enabling the agency to discharge CII accountability to CSA: design the Customs digital terrain and CII boundary with multi-layered defence, and translate regulatory obligation into architecture rather than into compliance tasks.
  • Co-develop the defensible architecture and resilience narrative the ACISO relies on for CSA engagement, audits, and CII regulatory submissions.

Platform leverage and control inheritance

  • Determine and document what the CII inherits from the GovTech security tech stack (e.g. GCC, central SOC/monitoring, ShipHats pipeline guardrails, IM8 baseline controls) versus what the TradeNet product team must build and own.
  • Maintain the shared-responsibility delineation as an architectural artefact that also scopes CII audit boundaries, so inherited controls are not re-attested.

Continuous assurance and secure delivery

  • Express security control intent as code: pipeline guardrails, policy-as-code, and continuous control monitoring designed into the platform so conformance is observable continuously rather than reconstructed for audits.
  • Champion secure SDLC and agile security practice within the delivery cadence, embedded in engineering teams rather than gating them.

Transitional / Day-2 scope (explicitly secondary)

The following are transitional and not the primary remit. Operational validation of the CLE's own designs sits with an independent assurance line to preserve control independence; the CLE provides engineering guidance, not self-validation:

  • Advisory and incident-response engineering support in coordination with SIRO, ACISO, and GCSOC.
  • Scoping and engineering guidance for external VAPT and vulnerability assessment, with closure validation performed independently.

What we are looking for

  • 10+ years in Cybersecurity as a Software Engineer and not just in the capacity of auditing, pen-testing, operational triage, etc….
  • We need someone that is hands on where the ideal candidate is someone that can design systems to be secure and can sit down to write code if they need to, someone that can coach our engineering teams on how to write better and more secure code, and someone that understands the cybersecurity tooling landscape to help us choose the right tools, we are not looking for a high level theorist / academic.
  • Demonstrated experience with designing security architecture into regulated / critical systems and platforms at the national or whole enterprise level, not just providing testing and assurance but actually designing and implementing.
  • Working command of Singapore regulatory frameworks for critical systems: CSA CCoP v2 for CII and WOG IM8 (Reform), with the ability to translate obligation into architecture and to delineate control inheritance for audit scoping.
  • Strong systems thinking: able to reason about a national platform as an interdependent whole — boundaries, failure modes, recoverability, and concentration risk — not as a checklist of controls.
  • Depth across cloud and platform security architecture (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS), identity, encryption and key management, segmentation and zero-trust patterns, and secure SDLC / policy-as-code.
  • Fluency with architectural and adversary frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, ISO 27001, CIS benchmarks) used to drive design decisions.
  • Ability to operate as a technical design authority alongside a CISO, clearly within the first line, and to produce architecture that withstands regulatory and audit scrutiny.
  • Proficiency in at least one scripting/automation language (e.g. Python, TypeScript, Shell/Bash, etc…) for policy-as-code and tooling.
  • Preferably proficient in both Kotlin/JVM stack and TypeScript.
  • Architecture-leaning certifications are advantageous (e.g. CISSP / CISSP-ISSAP, SABSA, cloud security architecture). Incident-response and offensive certifications are useful but not the primary signal for this role.
  • Subject to personnel security clearance / CII vetting appropriate to access to a national CII.
  • Subject to the nature of the role, onsite presence during fixed hours may be required.

How this role sits in our assurance model

This is a first-line engineering role. The Customs ACISO holds CII risk accountability; an independent assurance function validates and attests. The CLE provides the engineering and architectural substance both rely on, and does not validate or attest to the controls it designs. This separation is deliberate and protects the integrity of the CII assurance chain.

[About This Role]

We are looking for a Product Manager to work on the development and adoption of a centralised data discovery platform that serves as the single authoritative entry point for public officers across the whole of government to find, evaluate, and request access to government data.

Today, data discovery is fragmented across multiple platforms, each with its own go-to-market effort, onboarding process, and user experience. This creates confusion, duplication, and missed opportunities for data reuse. Your role is to change that — by building a product that becomes the definitive "first stop" for any public officer looking for government data, and by driving the ecosystem-level coordination needed to make that vision real.

This role that sits at the intersection of product, data governance, and cross-agency coordination. You will be responsible for both the strategic positioning of the platform and the day-to-day execution of product improvements — from search experience and catalogue coverage, to request workflows and integration with downstream delivery systems.

[What you will be working on]

As a Product Manager, you will hold significant ownership over your product domain, driving it from concept to reality while aligning with the broader programme goals. Your core responsibilities include:

Establishing and Communicating a Clear Product Vision

  • Execute Own and articulate the product vision for a centralised data discovery platform, ensuring alignment across engineering, design, policy, and senior stakeholders

  • Contribute to Define and maintain a coherent product strategy that positions the platform as the single entry point for government data discovery, replacing fragmented multi-platform behaviour

  • Collaborate with programme leadership and agency partners to secure buy-in and drive adoption at scale across government

Driving Catalogue Growth and Coverage

  • ExecuteLead the strategy to expand the platform's central catalogue by working with agency data owners and platform teams to surface more government data in one place — without necessarily requiring agencies to migrate their underlying systems

  • Identify and resolve the technical, operational, and incentive barriers that prevent agency datasets from being discoverable centrally, and develop scalable approaches to address them

  • Work with agency data owners to improve metadata completeness and quality so that datasets are genuinely useful to discover, not just listed

Improving Search, Discovery, and Request Experience

  • Own the end-to-end user experience for data discovery, from search and browse to dataset evaluation, access request, and approval

  • Use search analytics and user research to identify where the discovery journey breaks down — and drive iterative, evidence-based improvements

  • Explore how emerging technologies, including AI, might fundamentally reimagine how users find and evaluate data relevant to their needs — going beyond conventional search to ask what a great discovery experience could look like

  • Ensure that data consumers can assess dataset fitness-for-purpose directly within the discovery experience, without needing to contact data owners separately

Streamlining the Request and Approval Workflow

  • Drive consolidation of the inter-agency data request process into a single, trackable workflow within the platform, reducing fragmentation and improving visibility for both requestors and approvers

  • Work with policy and governance teams to digitalise and simplify approval processes, reducing time from request creation to first data access

  • Enable data providers to manage their sharing obligations — including approvals, rejections, and monitoring — through a single console experience

Reducing Friction Between Discovery and Data Use

  • Investigate and address the gap between a user finding a dataset and being able to actually use it in their work — understanding where friction exists in how data is accessed, integrated, and consumed across different working environments

  • Define and validate approaches that reduce the effort required for users to go from discovery to productive use, without prescribing a fixed technical solution upfront

Driving Adoption and Go-to-Market

  • Develop and execute a go-to-market strategy that consolidates user mindshare around a single discovery platform, replacing fragmented awareness across competing products

  • Build and maintain relationships with key agency stakeholders — both data providers and data consumers — to drive onboarding, usage, and feedback loops

  • Use consolidated user activity data to generate insights that improve the product and demonstrate value to programme leadership and agency partners

Monitoring, Measuring, and Iterating

  • Define and track product metrics that reflect real discovery success (e.g. search success rate, time from request to first access, catalogue coverage) rather than vanity metrics

  • Run structured experiments and user studies to validate product decisions and prioritise the roadmap

  • Maintain a clear, well-reasoned product backlog and communicate trade-offs transparently to stakeholders

Compliance and Governance

  • Ensure the platform meets security, performance, and data governance requirements applicable to a whole-of-government system handling sensitive metadata and access workflows

  • Adhere to compliance requirements and audits (IM8, AGO, QMS, etc.)

A disciplined approach and strong problem-solving instincts are fundamental to succeed. Your aptitude for completing the tasks and attitude to continuous learning are more valued than any formal certification.

About the Team

The Data Programme team's mission is to deliver high-quality, reusable data assets and services that support policy-making, service delivery, and operations across the whole-of-government (WOG). We build platforms and products that incorporate data science, machine learning, and AI — and we believe that the ability to integrate engineering rigour with data science thinking is what separates good products from great ones.

We work on problems that matter: from transportation to education to healthcare, even the simplest well-built software can have a meaningful impact on how Singapore functions as a society.

What the Role Is

Product Managers make sure the right things get done. At a high level, this means establishing a clear vision for what a product should be and charting the path to get there. Day-to-day, it means handling all the different facets of a product — user needs, technical constraints, and design goals — and keeping them coordinated.

In the Data Programme, this role sits at the intersection of policy, engineering and data science. You will need to be technically credible enough to work closely with engineers and data scientists, while being user-focused enough to translate complex capabilities into products that agency users actually find useful and intuitive.

What You Will Do

Understand users deeply

You will conduct user studies to understand the needs and problems of agency users, analyse usage data to uncover patterns that inform product decisions, and research the landscape to understand existing and competing solutions. The goal is to know your users better than anyone else on the team.

Make good product decisions

You will work with designers to create intuitive user experiences, develop multiple proposals for how a product could take shape, and lead the team to a balanced, well-considered position on what the product should be. This includes creating interfaces and data narratives that make insights immediately accessible to users who may not have technical backgrounds.

Work closely with the engineering team

You will translate product strategy into technical, detailed, and actionable plans for both business and engineering teams. You will understand developers' needs and, where necessary, explore emerging tools and techniques that can meet them. Experience with modern software development practices — CI/CD, DevOps, microservices, TDD/BDD — will help you engage credibly and move work forward.

Drive product growth and adoption

You will drive user adoption through increased engagement, expanded features, and sustainable usage growth. This includes maintaining a network with key user agencies and central government product teams to identify collaboration opportunities, and participating in public-speaking engagements to raise awareness of the product.

Manage resources and planning

You will develop workplans with the product team, manage the product budget through expenditure monitoring and cashflow management, and secure funding where needed. This includes co-creating budget papers with the Product Owner and procuring necessary software, hardware, and ICT professional services.

Communicate across teams and stakeholders

You will explain technical considerations to non-technical audiences, identify and engage key stakeholders — including government agencies, industry partners, and the broader tech community — and coordinate efforts across functions including marketing, legal, and finance. You will also represent the product through presentations and written papers.

Keep things organised

You will run efficient meetings to keep stakeholders and team members updated, prioritise and track what needs to be done, and document key decisions and product information clearly.

Ensure compliance and governance

You will ensure the product meets security and performance requirements (SSAT, VAPT, Performance Testing) and adhere to compliance requirements and audits (IM, AGO, QMS, and others).

[What we are looking for]

We value your aptitude for getting things done and your commitment to continuous learning over formal certifications. That said, the following reflect the genuine hiring signals for this role.

You should have a degree or diploma in Computer Science, Infocomm Technology, Engineering, or a related field, with at least five years of relevant experience. Candidates with more experience will be considered for senior roles.

  • Has worked directly with engineers, designers, and data scientists — and can engage credibly with all three

  • Is familiar with modern software development practices such as Agile, CI/CD, DevOps, microservices, and TDD/BDD

  • Has awareness of and experience with cloud service offerings

  • Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and can evaluate trade-offs clearly and communicate them well

  • Has good design sense and can distinguish between a product that works and one that users actually want to use

  • Communicates well — in writing, in presentations, and in stakeholder conversations — and can adapt their register for technical and non-technical audiences alike

  • Takes initiative and sees things through without needing to be managed closely

Through the GreenGov initiative, the government has committed to reaching net zero across the public sector by 2045, with clear and measurable milestones along the way. The Public Sector Sustainability Office (PSSO) reviews the progress of agencies, provides updates to the Cabinet, and produces the annual GreenGov report championing the GreenGov initiative. Job Summary

GovTech is seeking a strategic and mission-driven Lead/Senior Product Manager to spearhead the AI Safety and Governance pillar within PlatformAI. As AI adoption scales across the public sector, your mission is to ensure that every AI-enabled application is secure, fair, and accountable by design.

You will own a dual-track roadmap:

  • For Developers: Building the "Safety Stack"—a suite of automated Evals, Guardrails, and Red-teaming tools that allow teams to deploy LLMs with speed and confidence.
  • For Governance and Observability: Architecting the "Governance Layer"—observability tools and risk-posture dashboards that provide a unified view of AI compliance across the whole-of-government (WOG) ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

1. Defining the Sovereign Safety Standard

  • Define the long-term strategy for AI Safety-as-a-Service, transitioning governance from a manual checklist to an automated platform feature.
  • Synthesize emerging global frameworks and local AI governance policies into platform features that make compliance "invisible" for developers.
  • Establish the government’s standard for AI risk levels, determining the safety benchmarks required for different use cases (e.g., citizen-facing vs. internal productivity).

2. Building the Guardrails & Audit Trails

  • Lead the development of automated evaluation engines that stress-test products and models for prompt injection, PII leakage, toxicity, and hallucination before and after deployment.
  • Partner with Engineering to integrate safety checks directly into CI/CD pipelines, ensuring that "Safety-by-Design" accelerates rather than hinders deployment.
  • Build real-time monitoring tools to detect "jailbreak" attempts and model drift, ensuring rapid mitigation of live AI risks.

3. Bridging Policy & Code

  • Act as the primary liaison between Policy/Legal teams and Engineering teams to ensure technical tools meet policy and legal intent.
  • Cultivate a culture of safety across GovTech by publishing playbooks, standardizing red-teaming exercises, and educating teams on the evolving LLM vulnerability landscape.

4. Trust-Centric Metrics & Accountability

  • Define and track KPIs such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) vulnerabilities, Policy Coverage %, and Guardrail Efficacy Rates.

What You Will Bring

  • Senior Product Leadership: Proven experience managing complex technical products, specifically those focused on Security, Governance, or AI/ML infrastructure.
  • AI Safety Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of Generative AI risks (e.g., prompt injection, training data poisoning, algorithmic bias) and the current state of AI safety research.
  • The "Translator" Skillset: Exceptional ability to distil abstract ethical principles into concrete technical requirements and APIs.
  • Analytical Rigor: A background in using data-driven evaluation frameworks (e.g., RAG evaluation, perplexity scoring, or model benchmarking) to measure performance and risk.
  • Developer Empathy: A deep understanding of developer workflows and a commitment to making safety tools an "accelerant" rather than a "roadblock."

GeBIZ X is the MOF product that would transform the procurement and business experience for WOG public officers and external suppliers.

[Who we are looking for]
We are seeking a dynamic and driven Product Operations Specialist to support the delivery, operations, and continuous improvement of the GeBIZ X product.
You will operate at the intersection of product, engineering, policy, and operations to ensure the reliability, scalability, and effectiveness of the platform. This role plays a critical part in translating user needs into functional solutions, strengthening operational processes, and driving data-informed decision-making to improve user outcomes.
Decision-making
• When making important decisions, we identify overarching goals, weigh up our options, identify impact, and clearly communicate and manage the risks and trade-offs of our decision.
Ownership
• In addition to technical responsibilities, this means having opinions on what is being done and having ideas on what should be done next. Building something that you believe in is the best way to build something good.
Continuous Learning
• Working on new ideas often means not fully understanding what you are working on. Taking time to learn new architectures, frameworks, technologies (AI/ low code/ automation scripting) is not just encouraged but essential.
Our Team
Our team is made up of passionate individuals committed to solving challenges and driving meaningful change. We embrace diversity of thought, encourage experimentation, and foster a culture of continuous learning. As part of this team, you will collaborate with Business Owner, Product Director, Product Managers, UX Designers, Engineers and Business Users to execute the product strategy of GeBIZ X and deliver impactful outcomes.

[What you will be working on]
Product Operations & Stakeholder Engagement
• Engage agencies and suppliers to understand challenges, refine user stories, and identify opportunities to improve user outcomes using metrics (e.g. leading/lagging indicators, value-cost ratio).

• Operationalise agency onboarding and engagements, including coordination of processes, documentation, and testing.
• Act as a bridge between frontline users and technical teams to ensure effective issue resolution and strong feedback loops.
• Facilitate functional design discussions and translate business requirements into system configurations.
Data, Systems & Integration
• Map end-to-end user journeys and data flows across systems to ensure coherence and efficiency.
• Identify inter-agency data and integration dependencies, risks, and optimisation opportunities.
• Manage and triage operational issues (e.g. configuration errors, data inconsistencies, integration gaps) to maintain system integrity.
Product Delivery & Continuous Improvement
• Analyse operational and product data to identify trends, inform prioritisation, and drive continuous improvements.
• Develop and maintain playbooks, SOPs, and documentation using tools such as JIRA and Confluence.
• Support product delivery through testing activities including defect triage and User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
Operational Excellence & Process Improvement
• Drive best practices in product operations across one or more problem spaces.
• Conduct user research and translate insights into operational and product improvements.
• Develop and implement data-driven strategies to improve operational efficiency and product outcomes.
• Support procurement and setup of DevOps tools and platforms.
Risk Management & Governance
• Develop and implement risk and incident management strategies for operational issues.
• Support audit activities and ensure compliance with relevant policies and governance requirements.
User Support & Engagement
• Drive user support and engagement strategies to enhance adoption and satisfaction.
• Establish feedback management practices and continuous improvement loops.
• Ensure operational readiness for product launches, including communications and go-to-market support.
Ivalua Configuration & Functional Delivery
• Configure Ivalua modules (e.g. Sourcing, Contracts, Supplier Management, Procurement, Invoicing, Catalogues).
• Implement and maintain integrations (e.g. ERP systems, e-signature tools), ETL processes, and system interfaces.
• Support data migration and backend configurations.
• Troubleshoot issues related to workflows, configurations, and system performance.
• Develop and maintain configuration documentation, test scenarios, and training materials.
• Collaborate with Solution Architects, Technical Leads, and Product Managers to deliver solutions.
• Facilitate system demonstrations, walkthroughs, and end-user training sessions.
• Ensure configurations align with procurement policies and best practices.

[What we are looking for]
Experience & Education
• Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
• At least 3 years of experience in product operations, business analysis, or product/project management in IT environments.
• Experience working in Agile environments; relevant certifications (e.g. CSPO, CSM) are advantageous.

• Must obtain Ivalua Level 3 certification within 6 months of appointment (e.g. L3 S2C, L3 INT).

• Proficiency in SQL and database concepts.
• Practical understanding of APIs, integrations, and system architecture.
Core Competencies
• Strong analytical thinking with the ability to translate business needs into functional solutions.
• Ability to break down complex systems into clear operational processes and identify risks.
• Excellent communication skills to engage both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Structured, detail-oriented, and strong in documentation and follow-through.
• Strong collaboration skills across cross-functional teams (product, engineering, policy, operations).

Please note that this will be a 2-year fixed term contract.

[What you will be working on]

The DV module is a centralised, reusable document verification capability built within the Work Pass Integrated System (WINS). It consolidates what was previously fragmented verification logic spread across independent systems for Employment Pass, S Pass, Work Permit, and Migrant Domestic Worker applications into a single, shared module.

The key goals of the module are to eliminate duplication of verification workflows and maintenance effort, standardise and harmonise DV processes across pass types, and enable verified documents to be shared across applications so that applicants do not need to resubmit the same documents for different pass types. This improves efficiency for both MOM officers processing applications and applicants going through the work pass application journey.

Understanding and Defining Requirements

Product Ops is responsible for deeply understanding the current state of Document Verification across the various pass types and documenting the pain points — such as duplicated verification logic, workflow discrepancies, and the need for applicants to resubmit the same documents across different pass applications. They translate these into clear, structured business and functional requirements for the centralised DV module, ensuring it meets the needs of all pass types without compromising on pass-type-specific rules or validations.

Stakeholder Engagement and Alignment

Product Ops acts as the bridge between MOM policy owners, operations teams, and the technical development team. This involves facilitating workshops and interviews with stakeholders from each pass type domain to surface existing workflows, identify divergences, and agree on a common, harmonised process. Given that DV currently exists independently across multiple systems, managing stakeholder alignment and buy-in for a shared module is a significant part of the role.

Process Mapping and Gap Analysis

A core responsibility is mapping out the as-is DV workflows for each pass type and conducting a thorough gap analysis to identify where processes diverge and where they can be standardised. Product Ops would document these in process flow diagrams and use them to define the to-be state — a unified DV workflow that is flexible enough to accommodate pass-type-specific requirements while eliminating unnecessary duplication.

Defining the Shared Document Repository Logic

One of the key features of the new DV module is the ability to share verified documents across pass type applications, so applicants do not need to resubmit the same documents. Product Ops is responsible for defining the business rules around this — for example, what constitutes a valid previously verified document, how long a verified document remains valid, and under what conditions a document must be re-verified. These rules need to be clearly articulated before development begins.

User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

Product Ops translates requirements into well-defined user stories and acceptance criteria that the development team can work from. For a reusable module like DV, this includes stories covering document upload, verification workflows, document sharing logic, exception handling, and integration touchpoints with the various pass type systems.

Integration and Dependency Management

Since the DV module needs to integrate with multiple existing systems across the different pass types, Product Ops plays a key role in mapping out integration requirements and dependencies. This includes working with technical architects to understand API contracts, data flows, and how the centralised module will be consumed by each downstream system.

Supporting UAT and Change Management

Product Ops supports user acceptance testing by preparing test scenarios that cover the full range of pass types and document verification scenarios, including edge cases. They also play a role in change management — helping operations and policy teams understand how the new centralised module changes their workflows, and ensuring that training and communication materials accurately reflect the new processes.

Metrics and Success Criteria

Product Ops helps define what success looks like for the DV module — for instance, reduction in duplicate document submissions, reduction in maintenance overhead across systems, and improvement in processing time. Tracking these metrics post-launch also falls within the Product Ops remit, helping the team iterate and improve the module over time.

[What we are looking for]

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Proven experience in software development, system analysis, or a similar technical role.
  • Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Java, Python, Go, C#).
  • Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP) and containerization technologies (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) is highly desirable.
  • Strong understanding of database concepts and experience with SQL/NoSQL databases.
  • Familiarity with API design and development principles.
  • Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and critical thinking skills.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.

You will serve as the primary point of contact between vendors, the development team, and MOM stakeholders, ensuring that these systems remain reliable, compliant, and continuously improved. System Maintenance & Operations

You will oversee the health and performance of the Appointment@MOM and Special Pass systems, coordinating with technical teams and vendors to resolve incidents, manage system updates, and ensure minimal disruption to operations. You will establish and maintain monitoring routines, track system issues, and drive timely resolution of bugs and service requests.

Drive Operational Excellence

You will implement automated workflows to reduce manual processes and improve team efficiency. You will establish and track metrics that measure both product and operational performance, providing the team with clear visibility into system health and service quality. You will also design and maintain internal knowledge bases to ensure consistent and well-documented support practices across the team.

Vendor, Procurement & Budget Management

You will manage relationships with third-party vendors supporting the systems under your charge. This includes overseeing vendor deliverables, tracking service level agreements (SLAs), conducting performance reviews, and escalating issues where vendors fall short of expectations. You will also support procurement and contract renewal processes, ensuring that vendor engagements remain compliant with government procurement policies and deliver value for money.

Alongside vendor management, you will be responsible for tracking and managing project and operational budgets. In this capacity, you will support the end-to-end delivery of the transformation effort — from requirements gathering and process re-engineering to solution evaluation, testing, and rollout. We are looking for a Product Ops specialist to support STARS2.0's Phase 2 delivery squads and the parallel discovery into the platform law firms use to submit property transactions. This role sits at the intersection of business analysis and product delivery: you will analyse existing business processes, translate business and regulatory requirements into clear product requirements, and help the delivery squads avoid simply replicating STARS1's existing business rules where those rules can instead be rationalised and simplified.
This is a forward-deployed role: you will be embedded within the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), working day-to-day alongside Registration Officers, business stakeholders, and the engineers, designers and Product Managers across both Phase 2 squads.
You will be shared across both delivery squads and into the parallel discovery workstream, giving you visibility into how requirements and business logic connect across the whole programme rather than being scoped to a single team's backlog.

[What you will be working on]

About the programme
STARS2.0 is the programme to modernise STARS, Singapore's Land Titles Registry system, which has been in operation since 1993 and today manages approximately 2 million live titles. It is operationally critical infrastructure: it processes 500,000 property transactions a year and is the single source of truth by which the Government records and guarantees land ownership in Singapore.
STARS2.0 is not a standalone technology project. It sits at the centre of a wider Land Titles Registry transformation that extends beyond the registry itself - to the digital platform through which law firms submit property transactions, the Digital Conveyancing Portal, and adjacent systems. This role spans both the core registry modernisation and a parallel discovery into that wider ecosystem.

Business process analysis
You will analyse how STARS1's existing business processes and rules actually work today, identifying which are genuinely load-bearing regulatory logic and which are legacy implementation artefacts that can be simplified in STARS2.0. This is central to the programme's approach: STARS1's business rules were, in places, hardcoded for implementation convenience rather than reflecting the underlying regulation, and a key goal of STARS2.0 is to rationalise rather than replicate that logic.

Requirements translation
You will work with Registration Officers, policy stakeholders and Product Managers to translate business needs, operational realities and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable product requirements that engineering and design can build against. You will help ensure requirements are documented with enough precision that squads can build from defined criteria rather than discovering constraints mid-delivery.

Cross-squad and cross-track support
Because you sit across both Phase 2 squads and the parallel platform-discovery workstream, you will help surface where requirements, business rules or dependencies in one area affect another, so decisions are made with the full picture rather than in isolation.

[What we are looking for]

  • Experience in business analysis, business process re-engineering, or a similar requirements-focused role, ideally on enterprise, platform, or legacy-modernisation programmes
  • Ability to read and interpret complex, rules-heavy legacy business logic and distinguish genuine regulatory requirements from legacy implementation artefacts
  • An open, curious mind, with a genuine drive to spot inefficient processes and challenge them - whether through automation, AI, or simply better-designed workflows
  • Strong requirements-writing and documentation skills; comfort translating ambiguous stakeholder input into clear, buildable requirements
  • Comfort working across multiple concurrent workstreams and squads without losing rigour or consistency
  • Effective stakeholder communication, particularly with operational staff (Registration Officers) and policy owners
  • Basic technical literacy sufficient to work effectively with engineers on how requirements translate into system design.

  • Experience with business rules rationalisation or legacy system modernisation
  • Government or public-sector experience, particularly in regulatory or licensing domains
  • Domain knowledge in land administration, conveyancing, or legal/regulatory systems
  • Familiarity with agile delivery practices and working within cross-functional squad

As the Senior AI Security Consultant for the BusinessSG initiative, you will be the primary security architect guiding our transition to a proactive AI-driven platform. You will be embedded within a 10-man Discovery Squad, working alongside AI engineers and product leads to ensure that autonomous AI workflows—operating via messaging interfaces and a unified data hub—are secure, transparent, and resilient.

Your mission is to ensure every AI action is auditable and non-repudiable, protecting multi-agency data sources while maintaining the highest standards of public trust.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Security Architecture & Threat Modeling
  • System Design: Lead the design of security guardrails for AI agents to prevent them from taking unauthorized legal or financial actions.
  • Threat Modeling: Map out potential risks for autonomous AI, such as users trying to "hijack" the agent's intent or tricking it into accessing data it shouldn't.
  • Human-in-the-Loop: Design workflows that ensure high-stakes AI decisions (like grant recommendations) cannot proceed without explicit, authenticated human approval.
  1. Reliable Audit & Explainability
  • Audit Trails: Build a "Chain of Custody" for AI decisions by logging what the agent "thought," what specific data it retrieved, and which model version was used.
  • Reproducibility: Ensure that AI actions are documented well enough to be reconstructed and explained to auditors or stakeholders.
  • Data Governance: Ensure the AI only accesses integrated agency data on a strict "need-to-know" basis.
  1. Testing & Advanced Privacy (Preferred)
  • Security Testing: Conduct proactive testing to find vulnerabilities in how the AI processes instructions or uses external tools.
  • Advanced Privacy: Implement specialized privacy technologies to protect sensitive business information within our unified data hub.

Required Competencies & Experience

Experience Profile

  • 6–10 years of experience in Cybersecurity, with at least 2–3 years focused on AI/ML systems or securing LLM-based applications.
  • Proven track record in Cloud Infrastructure Security, specifically securing serverless compute, API gateways, and cloud-native databases.

Core Technical Foundations

  • Agentic System Design: Experience architecting or securing systems where AI moves beyond "chat" to performing actions through APIs.
  • LLM Security Foundations: Strong understanding of current LLM/ASI security risks, including prompt injection and data privacy in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) setups.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: In-depth knowledge of Singapore’s public sector security standards, including:
  • IM8.
  • Model AI Governance Framework.

Strategic & Soft Skills

  • Discovery Squad Collaboration: Ability to thrive in a high-velocity "sandbox" environment where you must balance rapid prototyping with security rigor.
  • Adversarial Mindset: Ability to anticipate how users might try to "game" the system to gain unfair advantages.
  • Risk Communication: Translating complex technical AI risks into clear, actionable advice for senior leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Policy-as-Code or logic-based authorization systems (e.g., ABAC).
  • Knowledge in Digital Forensics or building immutable logging architectures.
  • Prior experience in a Public Sector or "Smart Nation" project context.

Why this role?

This is a unique opportunity to join a specialized squad at the ground floor of agentic AI adoption in government. You will move from defending static applications to securing autonomous intelligence that directly impacts the Singapore business community.

Governance, Risk & Compliance

People & Capability Development

About Ministry of Transport (MOT)

  • Maritime and Ports
  • Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region. MOM's Enforcement Division ensures regulatory compliance across work pass licensing, migrant worker address management, and enforcement operations. The systems supporting these functions are critical to MOM's regulatory mandate, balancing policy objectives with operational efficiency and user needs across employers, enforcement officers, and migrant workers.

Design in Enforcement plays a strategic role in transforming fragmented legacy systems into coherent, efficient digital services that support complex workflows while maintaining regulatory rigor.

[What you will be working on]

As a Senior Designer for MOM Enforcement Division, you will shape end-to-end experiences across critical regulatory systems including license management, migrant worker address management, and enforcement workflows.

You will work closely with product managers, operations teams, policy officers, and engineering to translate complex regulatory requirements into usable, scalable digital experiences. This role requires balancing compliance constraints with user-centered design, operational efficiency, and long-term system coherence.

Your portfolio will include:

  • Licence management systems for work pass compliance
  • Migrant worker address management workflows
  • Enforcement operations and case management tool

Lead end-to-end design delivery across systems

  • Own product-level design from discovery through post-launch optimization, ensuring that enforcement systems are usable, coherent, and operationally effective while meeting policy and compliance requirements.

  • Conduct discovery using appropriate methods - user interviews, stakeholder workshops, operational shadowing, journey mapping, and data analysis to deeply understand enforcement workflows, pain points, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Map service ecosystems and end-to-end journeys across multiple systems and touchpoints, identifying systemic gaps, friction points, and opportunities to improve both user experience and operational efficiency.

  • Bridge business, operations, policy, and technology by facilitating alignment across cross-functional teams. Translate complex regulatory, operational, and technical constraints into clear design direction and actionable solutions.

  • Drive design direction by analyzing research findings, synthesizing insights, and defining design principles that guide product decisions while balancing user needs with regulatory and operational realities.

  • Rapidly prototype and iterate using modern tools and AI-assisted workflows (e.g., Figma, Claude for design assistance, AI prototyping tools) to accelerate concept validation, stakeholder feedback, and learning cycles.

  • Establish and maintain design standards for enforcement products, ensuring consistency, accessibility, and quality across all touchpoints while contributing to GovTech's broader design system.

  • Define and track success metrics for design solutions, measuring impact on user outcomes, operational efficiency, and policy objectives. Use data to drive continuous improvement.

Shape systems-level thinking and design excellence

  • Maintain strategic perspective at the programme level, ensuring individual product decisions align with broader enforcement division goals and contribute to MOM's service transformation vision.

  • Connect design work across multiple products and touchpoints, identifying opportunities for shared patterns, reusable components, and common capabilities that reduce duplication and increase efficiency.

  • Strengthen design quality through critique, review, and knowledge sharing, raising the overall standard of work and fostering a culture of design excellence across the enforcement portfolio.

Lead through collaboration and influence

  • Partner with cross-functional teams (product, engineering, operations, policy) to ensure design is deeply integrated into product strategy, planning, and delivery — not an afterthought.

  • Communicate design decisions, trade-offs, and recommendations clearly to stakeholders at all levels, ensuring alignment between user needs, operational constraints, and regulatory objectives.

  • Influence without authority by building trust, demonstrating value, and articulating how design contributes to measurable outcomes - not just better-looking interfaces.

  • Mentor junior designers and share knowledge across the organization, strengthening design capability and fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement.

Contribute to GovTech's design community

  • Drive efficiency and innovation by piloting new tools, methods, and AI-assisted workflows in your work, demonstrating how design can operate faster and smarter without sacrificing quality.

  • Actively participate in design community initiatives - sharing learnings, contributing to design standards, and supporting efforts that benefit all GovTech designers.

  • Support hiring and team-building efforts where relevant, helping build a strong, diverse, inclusive design practice.

What success looks like

Enforcement systems feel coherent and connected across critical journeys from licensing to address management to enforcement operations with measurable improvements in usability and operational efficiency.

Cross-functional teams trust design to frame problems, guide decisions, and deliver solutions that meet both user needs and regulatory requirements.

Design work accelerates through effective use of modern tools and AI-assisted workflows, enabling faster iteration, higher output, and greater strategic focus.

Enforcement division stakeholders recognize design as a strategic capability that contributes to measurable outcomes not just a service function

Experience and domain understanding:

  • 10+ years of experience in UX/UI design, product design, service design, or related fields
  • Proven experience leading design across complex, multi-stakeholder products or services
  • Experience in regulated, compliance-driven, or high-stakes environments (government, healthcare, financial services, legal/regulatory systems) strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated experience working on at least 2–3 different products, showing breadth and adaptability

You'll thrive here if you

  • Enjoy tackling complexity and ambiguity - breaking down messy regulatory and operational problems into clear, actionable design solutions.
  • See design as a means to measurable impact - cost reduction, productivity improvement, better policy outcomes not just better experiences.
  • Embrace efficiency and innovation - actively seeking ways to work smarter through modern tools, AI assistance, and streamlined methods.
  • Influence through clarity and credibility - earning trust by demonstrating value, not asserting authority.
  • Care about public service - motivated by the opportunity to improve critical government systems that affect thousands of employers, workers, and officers.
  • Are pragmatic and adaptable - able to balance ideal design solutions with real-world constraints, timelines, and trade-offs.
  • Want to build something meaningful - contributing to the transformation of legacy enforcement systems into modern, user-centered services.

About MOT

The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

  • Civil Aviation and Air Transport
  • Maritime and Ports
  • Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region. The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). About All Ears
All Ears (AE) is MOE's data-collection platform, purpose-built around how MOE actually works. Since 2022 it has been adopted across 337 schools, where staff have created ~177,000 forms and logged over 11.5 million submissions. It does natively what commercial tools cannot without prohibitive per-seat costs: rostering, identity verification, response tracking, and deep integration with MOE's master data.

AE is now evolving from a forms tool into essential infrastructure, connecting information from the ground (students, parents, teachers) to decision-makers (school leaders, middle managers, HQ), with speed and minimal administrative effort. We win on merit: schools and HQ choose AE because it is genuinely better for their context, not because they are told to.

What you will be working on
As Senior Product Manager for All Ears, you will own the platform end-to-end and define its next chapter. All Ears has established itself across 337 schools and millions of submissions, adopted on merit rather than mandate, and its future direction remains deliberately open. You will be responsible for shaping it: identifying the highest-leverage opportunities, determining what the platform should become, and driving it there. The mandate is broad and ambiguously scoped by design, and you will pursue it at MOE's scale, where every decision compounds across millions of transactions and is felt directly in schools and classrooms.

Your responsibilities

  • Own All Ears’ vision and roadmap, taking full ownership of broad, ambiguously-scoped initiatives from discovery through delivery and operations.
  • Identify high-impact problems and prioritise with discipline, using data to validate or kill ideas before development — and learn from both wins and misses.
  • Be the expert on All Ears’ data: measure key metrics at least quarterly and use them to drive and defend product decisions.
  • Ground decisions in user research, customer feedback, and market and competitor review, and mitigate product risks across technical and market dimensions.
  • Foster a culture of speed, simplicity, and agility — weighing speed against long-term technical debt — and partner closely with engineers and designers to run disciplined, metric-driven delivery.
  • Serve as the key liaison between HQ/business leadership and the product team, coordinating cross-functional collaboration and building alignment across stakeholders.
  • Navigate disagreements constructively and challenge existing processes to drive improvement at the team and division level.
  • Mentor junior team members and share successes and failures openly, reinforcing a strong learning culture.

What we are looking for

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent product experience.
  • Proven track record in product management (typically 6+ years), with at least one complex product or platform delivered end-to-end.
  • Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to turn ideas into shipped reality.

Your work impacts how Singapore receives its weather information. The national weather service runs three product families: data ingestion, forecasting, and public dissemination. As extreme weather events become more frequent, the accuracy and speed of these products directly affect public safety and national resilience.

The Government Digital Products (GDP) Team aims to spearhead the digital transformation of government. Our team designs and develops software applications that help government agencies to better serve the needs of the people of Singapore.

At the Engagement and Case Management Programme (ECMP), our products are the primary touchpoints through which residents interact with the Singapore Government. We design and develop a suite of high-impact software applications including FileSG, Signify, PersonaliseSG, CrowdTask SG, and BookingSG.

The Challenge: Elevating FileSG

FileSG is a central, secure file management system designed to streamline the issuance and distribution of official documents to Singapore residents. Beyond simple file transfer, it serves as a citizen-centric platform that supports the secure delivery of verified files—such as certificates, licenses, letters, and notices—directly to users. Trusted by agencies to replace inefficient legacy channels like physical mail and unencrypted emails, FileSG offers end-to-end traceability, confidentiality, and ease of access. Our mission is to consolidate document distribution onto a single, secure-by-design platform, eliminating the need for individual agencies to develop fragmented solutions and delivering a seamless, digital-first experience at a national scale. Furthermore, the team is now focused on developing automation and self-help features, empowering agencies to self-service and enabling the platform to support large-scale adoption across the government.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you are a trusted technical pillar of a cross-functional agile team. You will own the design and delivery of high-impact, cross-component features that span multiple services, ensuring they are built for massive scale, modularity, and resilience.

You will work closely with your Product Managers, Designers, and Engineering peers to solve complex scheduling and scalability problems, ensuring our systems remain secure, performant, and IM8-compliant by default.

[What you will be working on]

Design & Architect High-Impact Platform Features

  • Own the end-to-end design and implementation of complex, high-impact features spanning multiple services and integrations.
  • Evaluate technical tradeoffs, author clear design documents, and advocate for solutions that balance product velocity with scalability and long-term maintainability.
  • Proactively identify systemic bottlenecks and technical debt, championing refactoring initiatives to keep the core codebase healthy and modular.

Champion Engineering Quality & DevOps Practices

  • Foster engineering excellence by reviewing code and technical designs, providing constructive feedback that elevates the team’s overall capabilities.
  • Uplift automated testing strategies (unit, integration, E2E, performance) and contribute to reusable test frameworks.
  • Drive continuous delivery using modern CI/CD pipelines, containerization, and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) to ensure fast, deterministic, and reliable deployments.
  • Explore and champion innovative ways to embed GenAI into the team’s daily workflow, such as automating documentation, speeding up code reviews, while rigorously verifying code correctness.

Lead Operational Ownership, Security, and Performance

  • Treat system uptime, data integrity, system security and low-latency performance as core design constraints for every feature you ship rather than operational afterthoughts.
  • Own the implementation of comprehensive monitoring, alerting, and observability dashboards so anomalies are caught before they hit the user.
  • Act as a technical anchor during production incidents—rapidly triaging, debugging, and guiding the team towards resolving complex, cross-component issues. Lead blameless postmortems to turn operational failures into concrete preventive engineering actions.

Collaborate & Mentor

  • Partner closely with Product Managers, Designers, and Tech Leads to shape technical roadmaps and discover elegant solutions to complex user problems.
  • Translate high-level product goals into actionable engineering plans, breaking down complex scopes into well-defined, prioritized tasks.
  • Actively coach and mentor mid-level and junior engineers, conducting technical reviews that help them grow their architectural judgment and domain knowledge

[What we are looking for]

Experience

  • 5+ years of experience engineering, scaling, and delivering production-grade web applications, with a heavy emphasis on robust backend systems.
  • Proven track record of operating as a senior contributor or technical anchor within an agile engineering team.
  • A solid track record of designing, architecting, and operating scalable distributed systems, ideally within multi-tenant SaaS platforms or enterprise-grade applications.

Technical Skills

  • Deep, production-tested expertise in Node.js and TypeScript.
  • Strong hands-on experience building web applications and robust APIs using React or Next.js.
  • Solid understanding of cloud platforms (AWS preferred), container technologies (Docker), and establishing or operating modern CI/CD pipelines.
  • Deep commitment to comprehensive automated testing practices (unit, integration, and end-to-end) and structured architectural reviews.
  • Exposure to or a strong interest in GenAI technologies and incorporating AI-powered capabilities into product features is highly advantageous.

Mindset & Leadership

  • You look beyond the Jira ticket. You care deeply about user workflows, system security, compliance, and how your code affects the citizen / agency experience.
  • Ability to navigate architectural trade-offs pragmatically under shifting constraints.
  • Able to explain complex technical designs clearly to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.

jobDescription:
GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round.

Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today!

Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg.

At National Environment Agency (NEA), we are always on the lookout for high performing individuals who share our aspiration of making Singapore one of the world’s best living environments.

The NEA is building AI products and shared platform capabilities that can improve how we run complex operational workflows.

We are hiring software engineers who can take ambiguous problems from brief to production. This is not a pure research role and not a demo-building role. The work is to build reliable, maintainable, policy-sensitive AI systems that can survive real users, real operational constraints, and public-sector trust requirements.

AI will support how we build. Engineers still own the design, judgement, quality, and consequences of what ships.

How we build
We prefer simple, durable engineering choices over novelty for its own sake. The stack may vary by product, but the principles do not: clear architecture, automated testing, CI/CD, observability, secure-by-design delivery, and systems that are easy to reason about after launch.

The team’s operating model is product-led and platform-amplified. Product squads prove value in real NEA’s workflows; shared platform capabilities make those products observable, testable, governable, and reusable across NEA. Engineers may work inside a product squad, on the shared AI platform, or in a forward-deployed model where they help a vertical team build AI capability before bringing reusable patterns back to the centre.

[What you will be working on]

  • Design, build, test, deploy, and operate AI-enabled products and platform components across NEA.

  • Work on areas such as LLM integration, agentic workflows, evaluation harnesses, observability, guardrails, model access, retrieval/memory patterns, and multimodal AI use cases.

  • Take ambiguous operations problems and turn them into maintainable software with clear success metrics.

  • Build production features for products such as automation, tools, assistants, and deterministic and agentic workflow.

  • Create engineering patterns that other product teams can reuse, including templates, playbooks, test harnesses, and reference implementations.

  • Work closely with product managers, designers, data scientists, governance colleagues, and business owners.

  • Use AI coding and development tools to accelerate delivery while retaining human accountability for design and quality.

  • Participate in design reviews, code reviews, incident response, and technical decision-making.

  • Push for root-cause fixes rather than surface-level patches.

[What we are looking for]

  • At least 3 years of relevant working experience in fields related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, or software engineering.

  • Completed at least one hands-on AI development and deployment end-to-end project.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: system design, testing, version control, CI/CD, observability, security, and maintainable code.

  • Good engineering judgement: you can explain trade-offs clearly and defend a technical position without becoming attached to it.

  • Comfort with ambiguity: you can move from unclear policy, education, or operational needs into a working product shape.

  • Appetite for AI-native engineering: LLM applications, evaluation, agentic workflows, RAG/memory, multimodal models, or AI-assisted development.

  • Pragmatic taste in technology: you choose boring, durable tools when they are right, and newer AI tooling only when it genuinely improves the system.

  • Ownership mindset: you do not stop at prototype handoff; you care about deployment, monitoring, user feedback, and maintainability.

  • Ability to work with non-technical stakeholders in public-sector domains.

  • Bias for measurable quality: you care about evals, regression checks, traceability, and evidence before scaling.

Nice to have

  • Experience building production LLM or AI-enabled applications.

  • Experience with evaluation frameworks, prompt/context engineering, model monitoring, Langfuse/OpenTelemetry-style tracing, or AI safety guardrails.

  • Experience with Python, TypeScript, Go, PostgreSQL, containerised deployment, cloud services, or government/cloud-restricted environments.

  • Experience building internal platforms, developer tooling, or reusable engineering kits.

  • Familiarity with Environment Domain, public-sector operations, procurement, or high-trust digital services.

What success looks like

In the first 6 months, you should have shipped meaningful production work in at least one product or platform area, improved the team’s engineering quality bar, and helped convert one-off AI delivery into reusable capability. The best engineers in this role will not just “build features”; they will help define how NEA builds, evaluates, governs, and scales AI products.

Why this role matters

NEA’s AI work is moving beyond experiments. The next challenge is to make AI useful, safe, measurable, and maintainable across NEA workflows. This role is for engineers who want to build public-good AI systems with national-scale relevance, while shaping the operating model for how product teams use AI responsibly.
